Trump May 27-28 statements: US naval blockade "remains in full force and effect until agreement is reached, certified, and signed" — conditional-signing trigger inside standing "don't rush" envelope; conditionality firms without crossing into date-specific ultimatum.

Ukrainian military intelligence (Budanov, via The War Zone tier-2) reports Russia transferring Shahed-136 / Garpiya drone production technology to North Korea with ~12,000 NK workers being deployed to the Alabuga Special Economic Zone in Tatarstan — CRINK operational coordination expansion signal pending Western wire corroboration.

Pentagon convenes round-4 Israel-Lebanon-US security talks May 29 on schedule despite IDF Beirut strike May 28; talks NOT cancelled — 45-day ceasefire-extension framework intact; political track June 2-3 State Department remains scheduled.

Brent Day 5 held well below $108 (May 28 close ~$96.57; May 29 trading range similar per Trading Economics) — completing the five-day watch window and confirming a durable negotiation-premium repricing.

IDF's 36th Division crossed the Litani and struck Beirut (targeting Imam Hossein missile chief Ali al-Husni); Hezbollah fired its first rocket salvo at northern Israel overnight May 29-30 — no injuries, one launcher destroyed — escalating beyond drones during the ceasefire window. Pentagon May 29 talks produced no public readout; the June 2-3 State Department political track stands.

CNN's May 28 tentative two-phase US-Iran framework is now corroborated across Bloomberg, Axios, PBS, RFE/RL and NPR — verification upgrades Reported to Confirmed. Phase 1 terms surface (Iran clears Hormuz mines within 30 days, US lifts the blockade gradually, oil-sanctions relief). Trump held a May 29 decision meeting but issued no public approval or rejection as of May 30.

Mali's Defense Minister Gen. Sadio Camara — architect of Bamako's security strategy and its principal Moscow/Africa-Corps channel — was killed in a suicide attack, amid a JNIM jihadist-separatist offensive convergence, a JNIM blockade of the Bamako-Sikasso road, and a nationwide "State of War" alert in neighboring Niger. Material for Russia's Sahel posture and regional stability.

Brent settled ~$92/bbl at the May 29 close (WTI ~$87), down roughly 17% on the month — the largest monthly drop since 2020 — as the corroborated ceasefire framework drains the war premium; gold ~$4,539, VIX ~15.7.; durable repricing confirmed.

Ukraine's Special Operations Forces struck Lukoil's Volgograd refinery (15M tons/yr; primary AVT units damaged, production halted) on May 28-29, with further overnight strikes on Russian oil infrastructure reported May 30 — the selective refinery campaign holds at its sixth week.

The US, UK and Australia announced an AUKUS seabed-cable defense pact May 31 — Five-Eyes-plus-AU coordination on undersea-cable protection, framed as a response to hostile-environment risks (the Alcatel Hormuz force majeure since March is the standing cycle reference).

OFAC General License W (the Qingdao Oil wind-down authorization) expired at 12:01 EDT May 31 — a narrow, scheduled Iran-related lapse rather than a new designation; GL 134C in-transit cover for Russia crude holds to June 17.

Day 13: Trump has still issued no public approval or rejection of the corroborated two-phase US-Iran framework as of May 31 — the May 29 decision meeting produced no ruling, and the naval blockade remains in force pending a signature.
The May-24 Oreshnik count tilts toward a two-launch read as ISW and OSINT analysis converge against The National's four-launch claim; the count stays Disputed pending tier-1-wire convergence.

The 14-day window for a second strike on Gulf-state territory (from the May 17 Barakah/Saudi incidents) closed May 31 with no second incident — the UAE/Saudi/Iraq tri-actor firebreak held the full window.

An IDF soldier was killed June 1 in a Hezbollah drone attack in south Lebanon — the first Israeli military fatality of this flare — and Netanyahu and Defense Minister Katz ordered an immediate renewal of strikes on Beirut's Dahiyeh. The May-30 Hezbollah barrage is confirmed at 15-25 projectiles (no injuries); the June 2-3 State Department political track remains scheduled.

Day 14: Trump has still issued no public approval or rejection of the Confirmed two-phase US-Iran framework as of June 1; Bloomberg reports the two sides are still trading draft revisions, and the naval blockade remains in force pending a signature.

Iran briefly halted communications with the United States June 1 over Israel's expanded Lebanon offensive — including the IDF fatality and renewed Beirut strikes — before talks resumed via the Pakistan channel within ~24 hours, a short procedural pause rather than a structural walkout.

Ukraine struck the Saratov (Rosneft) refinery overnight May 31 — the eleventh major Russian refinery hit since May 1 — alongside the Lazarevo oil-pumping station and damage in Rostov/Voronezh/Belgorod; the selective refinery campaign holds, and no second 500+ aggregate Russian strike has materialized (Day 8).

Zelenskyy's letter to Trump and Congress states that Russia launched two Oreshnik missiles in the May-24 strike — a Ukrainian-official count that, with OSINT analysis, now converges against The National's four-launch claim and NPR's three; the count firms toward two.

Brent held around $91 (May 31 close) and traded $91-94 on the June 1 reopen — sustaining the sub-$95 repricing — with gold ~$4,530, VIX ~15.3, and the S&P 500 near record highs; the modest oil tick is tied to the Lebanon escalation, not any unraveling of the Iran framework.

Ukraine struck the Ilsky oil refinery (Krasnodar region) overnight June 2 — the 12th major Russian refinery hit since May 1 — with the campaign pace now running at roughly double the 2024 baseline (32 strikes in the first five months of 2026 vs 34 in all of 2024); the selective tempo holds in parallel to Russia's mass-strike resumption.

Russia executed an overnight 729-aggregate strike (73 missiles + 656 drones, including 8 Zircon hypersonic missiles confirmed at zero intercepts (note: the aggregate figure and any "largest of the war" framing are not the all-war record — the July-2025 728/741-weapon night and a later ~948-drone night were larger)) on nine Ukrainian cities including Kyiv and Dnipro; a Podilskyi nine-story residential building collapsed; preliminary toll 13-22 killed and 100+ wounded; the second 500+ aggregate Russian strike of the May-24 window resolves the forecast YES at Day 9.

OFAC imposed sanctions on the IRGC-linked "Persian Gulf Strait Authority" — the entity attempting to monetize Strait of Hormuz extortion — as part of a broader Iran enforcement action that also accompanied a routine modernization removing 76 outdated designations; a discrete enforcement step against the toll-monetization architecture, not a formal Hormuz-toll-regime designation tranche.

OFAC designated Nobitex — Iran's largest crypto exchange — plus Wallex, Bitpin, and Ramzinex on June 2, the largest Treasury enforcement action yet against Iran's digital-asset economy and the first cycle event materially clearing the standing crypto/blockchain two-question test (alters speed and path of sanctioned-actor funding via payment-rail access).

Round-4 of US-mediated Israel-Lebanon political-track talks convened at the State Department June 2 — led on the US side by Deputy National Security Adviser Mike Needham — with both sides agreeing to direct future negotiations; the round survived the June-1 IDF fatality and renewed Beirut campaign but produced no formal deliverable by the June-3 close.

Trump told reporters June 1-2 the US-Iran agreement reopening the Strait of Hormuz is "largely negotiated" and will be "announced soon" but the June 1 White House Situation Room produced no public ruling — fifth consecutive day of convening-without-ruling on Day 15 of the postponement.

The forecast formal Iranian Hormuz toll order at the June-2 deadline closed NO — no published government order with named fee schedules emerged; an Iranian official's "$2 million per transit" remark was rebutted by Iran's embassy in India as "personal views," and Iran's foreign ministry maintained "navigational services" ambiguity while the IRGC permission-transit regime continues as informal substitute.

Taiwan's Ministry of National Defence reported 18 PLA aircraft sorties and 8 PLAN vessels around Taiwan on June 3, with 14 of the 18 sorties crossing the median line into northern and southwestern ADIZ — high-end of the established gray-zone pattern (averaging ~300 sorties/month), not novel escalation.

Day 16 of the postponement: Trump issued no public ruling June 3; the deal is reported at "finalization stage" with Trump's May-31 requested edits to draft text (nuclear-uranium clauses, Hormuz terms) sitting pending Iranian response in a ~3-day window around June 3-4 per Axios and CBS — sixth consecutive day of convening-without-ruling and the verbal-deal-imminence pattern continues without crossing the public-approval threshold.

Iran's negotiator warned Tehran will halt nuclear-framework talks and pursue "direct confrontation" if Israeli aggression on Lebanon continues — the first on-record cycle warning explicitly conditioning the framework on the Lebanon kinetic surface; Secretary Rubio's June-2 Senate Foreign Relations testimony framed Iran as wanting to "mix it all together," set a "no sanctions relief until significant nuclear concessions" baseline, and said Iran has mined "large segments" of Hormuz with a US clearance estimate of ~6 months.

Brent crude broke the durable sub-$95 zone at $98.52 spot on June 3 (+2.63% intraday, third day of gains; WTI $96.42 +2.84%) — the durable-de-escalation-premium hypothesis that held since May 29 meets its first hard counter-evidence at Day 5 as Trump's May-31 edit requests sit pending Iranian response and Iran's "direct confrontation" warning compounds; equity-vs-energy divergence narrows.

Netanyahu's special cabinet meeting on the war-damaged north was boycotted by most ministers — only the prime minister and four ministers attended — even as he announced 13 billion NIS ($4.5B) for the region; National Security Minister Ben-Gvir publicly demanded defying Trump on the Lebanon ceasefire, telling the prime minister: "time to tell President Trump 'no'" and "unleash our fighters" — coalition discipline now openly contested as next-election mandate sits no later than 2026-10-27.

The US House passed a War Powers Resolution 215-208 directing Trump to end hostilities with Iran — the first cycle congressional move on Iran, with four Republicans defecting; the measure is symbolic pending Senate passage and a likely Trump veto override.

Trump publicly confirmed a heated phone call with Netanyahu, telling reporters "Bibi, we got to stop this" on the Lebanon ceasefire — the first cycle move of US-Israel friction from private channels to public on-record pressure, against the backdrop of IDF chief Halevi's "no ceasefire for our forces" framing and IDF evacuation warnings for six south-Lebanon villages (An-Nabatiya, Haruf, Tibnin, Hadasa, Srifa, plus one other) overnight June 3.

Ukrainian drones struck the St. Petersburg oil terminal, the Kronstadt naval base, and the Tambov weapons plant overnight June 3 — a 1,000+ km standoff reach extension hours before Putin's Economic Forum keynote; Russia claimed 354 drones downed across the night, and the strikes mark the campaign's furthest single-night reach to date while remaining within selective-tempo discipline (not a Russian-side saturation step).

OFAC designated 12 individuals and entities tied to the IRGC oil-sales architecture on June 3 — including the Shahid Purja'fari Oil HQ and payment-coordinator Golden Globe — a Treasury follow-on to the June-2 Nobitex/Wallex/Bitpin/Ramzinex crypto-exchange tranche hitting crypto and traditional payment networks within 48 hours.

Day 17 of Trump's postponement: no public ruling June 3-4; the deal is reported at "finalization stage" with Trump's May-31 edits to draft text still sitting pending Iranian response, the seventh consecutive convening-without-ruling day, and the Pakistan-track framework-text update window closes tomorrow June 5 with no surfacing.

Trump's heated June 3 phone call with Netanyahu became explicitly public on June 4 as a "f-cking crazy" framing reported across NPR, CNN, and Times of Israel, with Trump announcing a fresh Lebanon truce and Netanyahu appearing to call off Beirut strikes per the US announcement.

Brent retraced -1.64% to $96.41 on June 4 (WTI $94.82 -1.58%), walking back roughly two-thirds of the June-3 $98.52 break and reading as a tactical fade rather than a structural new ceiling — the durable-sub-$95 hypothesis is in retracement, not yet decisively dead, with Day 2 of the 5-day ≥$100 window inside the new $95-100 band.

Trump publicly said he would be "OK with Iran suspending nuke enrichment for 20 years if there's a real guarantee" — the first specific numerical floor from the US side on Phase 2 enrichment-moratorium length.

The IAEA released its first verification report on Iran's nuclear program since the Feb 28 blackout — 97 days zero inspector access — finding "little change" despite the war; Director Grossi separately stated on June 5 that US-Iran framework talks appear "close to" producing an agreement.

Israel and Lebanon agreed to a US-brokered conditional ceasefire framework on June 4, contingent on phased IDF withdrawal south of the Litani and Lebanese army takeover; Hezbollah explicitly rejected the framework, demanding Israeli withdrawal as a precondition. The same window saw the first IDF military fatality of the Beirut campaign (Qantara anti-tank missile) and continued IDF strikes across south Lebanon.

Brent never touched $115 across the May-21 through June-4 window — the high was the $98.52 June-3 break — closing the ceiling-side of the durable-de-escalation-premium test clean even as the floor loosens.

Putin delivered the St. Petersburg International Economic Forum keynote on June 5, touting BRICS leadership and a multipolar world; he said there was no reason to meet Zelenskyy — the keynote landed two days after Ukrainian drones struck the host-city oil terminal, the Kronstadt naval base, and the Tambov weapons plant overnight June 3.

Brent crude collapsed to $93.09 on June 5 (-2.04% on the day after -3.36% June 4 to $97.95), walking back roughly two-thirds of the cycle's recovery; WTI $90.54 (-2.69%); VIX spiked 39.68% to 21.51; S&P 500 -2.64% to 7,383; gold $4,365 (-3.10%) — atypical risk-off paired with commodity weakness suggests demand destruction + de-escalation premium reasserting.

Hamas reiterated it will not surrender its arms and stated that only police will carry weapons when the Palestinian National Committee assumes control of Gaza — the disarmament-blocking-knot persists structurally inside the October-2025 framework.

An IDF strike killed a Lebanese army brigadier general, a captain, and a soldier in the Nabatieh district on June 6, with the IDF stating the targeted vehicle had been moving suspiciously toward Israeli forces and announcing the incident was under review — the first cycle direct IDF kinetic act on Lebanese state-army personnel inside the announcement window of the June-4 conditional ceasefire.

IDF strikes across south Lebanon June 5-6 killed at least 12 in Habboush, Zebdine, and Aaba and prompted forced-displacement orders for nine additional southern villages — Hezbollah retaliated with eight calibrated launches; the kinetic surface continues inside the announced June-4 framework.

Day 20 of Trump's postponement: no public ruling June 6-7, the tenth consecutive convening-without-ruling day, with Trump's May-31 edits to draft text effectively elapsed without a publicly reported tier-1 Iranian response and the Pakistan-track framework-text-update window closed at deadline June 5 without tier-1 surfacing.

The NK-Russia drone-tech production-leg corroboration window firms on a June-7 Kyiv Independent follow-on plus standing CSIS Beyond Parallel satellite analysis — reciprocal-capability-transfer pattern strengthens at the cycle's first material follow-on Western reporting since the original disclosure. Full Western tier-1 wire (Reuters, AP, FT, Bloomberg, WSJ) corroboration remains pending with 4 days to deadline.

Trump publicly said on June 7 that he "calls the shots" on the US-Iran framework and Netanyahu "won't have any choice" but to accept the deal — extending the June 4 "f-cking crazy" framing to a public decision-authority claim. The Trump-pressure-goes-public-on-Israeli-coalition framing firms to a third public observation in 96 hours without converting to a named operational US lever.

Cabinet reappointed Itamar Ben-Gvir as police minister June 7 despite the Attorney General's High Court action over the Haredi-front rioting and Ben-Gvir's defiance of Trump's Lebanon pressure — institutional defiance institutionalized via ministerial reappointment without a formal Otzma Yehudit / Religious Zionism no-confidence motion.

Hezbollah fired two rockets at northern Israel June 7; the IDF intercepted both and struck Hezbollah HQ targets in Dahiyeh (southern Beirut), killing 2 and wounding 11+ inside the announcement window of the June-4 conditional ceasefire. The Hezbollah salvo size sits well below the 30-rocket framework rejection threshold.

Day 21 of Trump's postponement closes the June-8 framework-decision deadline without a public ruling — the eleventh consecutive convening-without-ruling day. The Pakistan-track framework-text-update window already closed without a tier-1 surfacing at the June-5 deadline; the May-31 edit-request window has effectively elapsed without a publicly reported Iranian response.

Ukrainian drones struck the Grushevaya oil depot in Krasnodar Krai and the Krasny Yar pipeline dispatch station in Volgograd Oblast on June 8 — critical nodes in Russia's southern oil-export network. The campaign holds at roughly double the 2024 strike pace without a new clearly named distinct 13th refinery.

China's Xi Jinping made a state visit to North Korea June 8-9 — his first since 2019 and the seventh Xi-Kim meeting — pledging to 'strengthen strategic coordination'; the most consequential CRINK signal of the period. (Recorded June 20 after the dashboard had omitted it.)

The Pakistan-track text-update window already closed at June 5; the May-31 edit window has elapsed without a publicly reported tier-1 Iranian response.

The named two-to-three Phase-2 enrichment-moratorium clauses window closed at deadline today without a tier-1 wire surfacing of the specific clause text; the named-clauses forecast resolves NO. Trump's standing 20-year enrichment-suspension floor and Grossi's "close to" framing remain the diplomatic anchors; the formal Phase-2 text remains unpublished.

Ukraine's DTEK and Ukrenergo did not publish a quantified MW-loss assessment from the May-24 Kyiv strike by deadline today; the MW-loss-assessment forecast resolves NO. Only general-capacity figures remain available (the standing ~70% loss-from-war-start framing and the ~14 GW available-capacity figure from January 2026).

Ilsky (June 2) remains the 12th distinct refinery; Ukraine's June-8 strikes on the Grushevaya oil depot and the Krasny Yar pipeline node are oil-infrastructure but not a new distinct refinery target.

The NK-Russia drone-tech production-leg corroboration firms further on a Kyiv Post + Institute for the Study of War (ISW) June-7 pickup of the Budanov disclosure — reciprocal-capability-transfer pattern strengthens. Full Western tier-1 wire (Reuters / AP / FT / Bloomberg / WSJ) corroboration remains pending with three days to the corroboration deadline.

Gold steadies and VIX contracts off Friday's spike.

Brent closed June 10 at $92.08 per Yahoo Finance futures data — fourth consecutive sub-$95 session after $93.09 (June 5), $94.34 (June 8), $92.48 (June 9). VIX contracts to 20.60 (-7.29% session); S&P 500 7,267 (-1.62%); gold $4,112 (-0.53%); 10Y 4.54%. Durable-sub-$95 firms over the $95-100 band hypothesis pending tier-1 wire confirmation.

Ukraine struck the Kuibyshev oil refinery (Samara Oblast) overnight June 10 — both CDU-4 and CDU-5 processing units halted after fires; Reuters and Ukrinform reporting confirms the strike. Kuibyshev is the 13th distinct Russian refinery of the 2026 campaign (after Ilsky June 2 as 12th); the cycle's named-13th-refinery forecast resolves YES inside the 14-day window.

Israeli airstrikes hit Tyre, Tayr Debba, Deir Qanoun en-Nahr, and Deir ez-Zahrani in southern Lebanon on June 10, killing at least 16 — Tayr Debba (9 killed), Deir Qanoun en-Nahr (3), Tyre (≥1), Deir ez-Zahrani mosque + clinic (≥3) per Al Jazeera. UN announced an inquiry into civilian-area targeting; the kinetic surface continues inside the June-4 conditional-ceasefire announcement window.

Day 24 of Trump's postponement opens as the fourteenth consecutive convening-without-ruling day; no tier-1 Western wire surfacing of a public Trump approve or reject of the Pakistan-mediated framework in the June 10-11 window. The IAEA "little change" verification report, Trump's 20-year enrichment-suspension floor, and Grossi's "close to" framing remain the standing diplomatic anchors.

Brent closed June 11 at $90.38 per Yahoo Finance futures data — the fifth consecutive sub-$95 session after $93.09 (June 5), $94.34 (June 8), $92.48 (June 9), and $92.08 (June 10). VIX 19.44 (-3.69% session); S&P 500 7,266.99 (-0.02%); gold $4,114.00 (+0.05%); 10Y 4.542; WTI $87.71. The cycle's named 5-day sub-$95 hold resolves YES at deadline today.

Anti-immigrant riots hit Belfast and other Northern Ireland towns for a second night after a June 8 knife attack; police used water cannon, 16 were arrested and 12 officers injured, with unrest spreading to parts of Scotland and England.

Day 25 of Trump's postponement opens as the fifteenth consecutive convening-without-ruling day; no tier-1 Western wire has surfaced a public Trump approve or reject of the Pakistan-mediated framework in the June 11-12 window. The IAEA "little change" verification report, Trump's 20-year enrichment-suspension floor, and Grossi's "close to" framing remain the standing diplomatic anchors.

The NK-Russia drone-tech production-leg corroboration window closes at deadline today without a Reuters / AP / FT / Bloomberg / WSJ pickup of the Budanov disclosure; the cycle's named-corroboration forecast resolves NO. The Kyiv Independent + Institute for the Study of War June-7 pickup and the standing CSIS Beyond Parallel satellite + NK News recruitment documentation hold as the most institutional Western surfacing.

June-12 intraday shows the cycle's largest single-session de-escalation-premium reassertion — Brent $86.48 (-4.32%) and WTI $83.94 (-4.30%) on Yahoo Finance delayed-quote data, paired with gold $4,245.60 (+3.20%), VIX 18.87 (-2.94%), S&P 500 7,394.30 (+1.75%), and 10Y 4.463 (-1.74%). Markets pricing expected US-Iran movement; tier-1 Western wire surfacing of an actual Trump ruling not yet confirmed.

Pakistan's Prime Minister publicly stated June 12 that the "final, agreed-upon text" of the US-Iran two-phase framework has been reached, with CBS News, NBC News, and CNN carrying the claim. Treasury Sec. Bessent told reporters the deal "could come this weekend or Monday"; Trump referenced an upcoming signing-ceremony location "shortly." Iranian Supreme Leader sign-off reportedly still pending; no tier-1 wire surfacing of an actual Trump approval at filing.

Day 26 of Trump's framework postponement enters as the sixteenth consecutive convening-without-ruling day; no public Trump approve or reject in tier-1 wires across the June 12-13 window despite Pakistan's text-finalization announcement and Trump's own signing-ceremony references.

Brent crude settled near $87 at Friday June-12 close per CNBC and Yahoo Finance, consolidating the sub-$90 band amid continued de-escalation pricing on Pakistan's framework-text-finalization announcement; gold around $4,215; S&P 500 holding mid-7,400s.

Russia launched 118 long-range attack drones against Ukraine overnight June 13, killing at least 8 and injuring 62 with a local market hit in Dnipropetrovsk Oblast — Day 12 of the 14-day window since the June-2 729-aggregate strike registers without a second 500+ aggregate Russian strike.

Ukraine struck an oil preparation / pumping workshop near Kotovo in Volgograd Oblast overnight June 13, triggering a large-scale industrial fire per Kyiv Independent — oil-infrastructure pressure that does not qualify as a new distinct refinery target; Kuibyshev (June 10) stands as the 13th distinct.

IDF airstrikes killed at least 5 across southern Lebanon June 13 and the IDF issued forced displacement orders for 24 towns along the Zahrani River line — the largest single-day civil-displacement scale since the June-4 Israel-Lebanon conditional ceasefire announcement window.

A Lebanese Armed Forces soldier was severely wounded by IDF drone strikes on the Kfar Reman-Nabatieh road June 13; the first LAF-personnel-affecting event since the June 6 Nabatieh fatality (1 brigadier general + 1 captain + 1 soldier killed).

Thousands attended an anti-racism counter-rally at Belfast City Hall June 13 after five nights of anti-immigrant unrest that began June 8 with a stabbing attack by a Sudanese asylum-seeker — the counter-rally is the largest of its kind in Northern Ireland per Amnesty International UK, registering rapid societal pushback within a 5-day cycle.

Day 27 of Trump's framework postponement enters as the seventeenth consecutive convening-without-ruling day; no tier-1 Western wire has surfaced a public Trump approve or reject of the Pakistan-finalized US-Iran framework text across the June 13-14 window despite Bessent's named "weekend or Monday" framing and Trump's signing-ceremony reference "shortly."

Israel's Attorney General urged the High Court to force Prime Minister Netanyahu to fire National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir following the June 7 reappointment despite the AG's prior High Court action — coalition fumes; institutional-channel escalation continues without a formal Otzma Yehudit / Religious Zionism no-confidence motion.

Russia launched 98 long-range attack drones against Ukraine overnight June 14 per the Kyiv Independent and Institute for the Study of War, well below the 500-aggregate threshold; Day 13 of the 14-day window since the June-2 729-aggregate strike enters tomorrow without a second 500+ aggregate Russian strike materializing.

The United States and Iran signed the 14-point memorandum of understanding in person at the Palace of Versailles on June 17, following the G7 summit dinner hosted by France — Trump and President Pezeshkian, with Pakistan's prime minister co-signing as mediator. The interim framework took effect immediately, extending the ceasefire 60 days and committing to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and ease oil sanctions.

IDF struck Tyre, Bint Jbeil, Kfar Tebnit, and Nabatieh al-Fawqa June 17 per Al Jazeera; Hezbollah responded with at least ten rockets at northern Israel and a drone detonation wounded five Israeli soldiers — sub-threshold of the 30-rocket framework-rejection mark; UN reports projectile fire dropped from 705 to 174 weekly baseline.

Ukraine launched the largest drone attack on Moscow of the war — approximately 555 drones nationwide per Russian Defense Ministry — and struck the Moscow Refinery (Kapotnya) for a second time in 72 hours with multi-unit damage to the catalytic cracker, visbreaker and MTBE/oligomerate unit; Zelensky said "Moscow will burn" if Putin continues the war.

Iran's foreign ministry said there will be no formal signing ceremony in Switzerland on Friday June 19 because both presidents have already signed the memorandum electronically; delegations will instead meet at Burgenstock to begin implementation talks.

A 29-country bloc and the UN warned June 18 of imminent atrocities as Sudan's RSF massed for a ground assault on El Obeid (North Kordofan); more than ten days of drone strikes had killed dozens of civilians, with roughly 500,000 people at risk.

Four IDF soldiers including the 52nd "Breachers" Battalion commander were killed in a Hezbollah drone strike on a tank in southern Lebanon overnight; five more wounded in separate explosive-drone attacks — the first major test of the Islamabad MOU's all-fronts cessation 48 hours after signing.

Commercial transit through the Strait of Hormuz began gradually resuming under the interim MOU with tankers crossing in the days since signing; commercial traffic remains a small fraction of pre-February-2026 levels and the Pentagon estimates 40 days to six months for full mine clearance and confidence restoration.

A US- and Qatar-brokered renewed Israel-Hezbollah ceasefire took effect about 4 p.m. June 19 after the flare-up that killed four IDF soldiers; the truce is fragile, with Israel keeping its south-Lebanon buffer zone and strikes reported after it took effect.

US Vice President JD Vance publicly rebuked Israel while defending the US-Iran memorandum, saying 'you can't kill your way to security' and that he 'might not be attacking the only powerful ally that I have anywhere left in the entire world'; CNN framed the remarks as a sign the US could be breaking with Israel.

Brent crude settled near $79 a barrel on Friday with the week on track for a roughly ten percent decline as markets priced the US-Iran MOU; the VIX fell 11 percent to 16.40, the S&P 500 set a record near 7,500 and gold eased to about $4,210.

US Central Command said all naval-blockade enforcement has ceased and commercial transit through the Strait of Hormuz is resuming under the interim MOU; three Saudi supertankers crossed and more than 12 million barrels of oil passed overnight, though analysts say shippers remain cautious and the floodgates have not opened.

President Zelensky gave Belarus's Lukashenko one week to remove Russian military equipment from near Ukraine's border, warning Ukrainian forces would act otherwise; Lukashenko has ruled out entering the war directly, but Ukraine reports rising Russian reconnaissance-drone activity and military buildup on Belarusian territory. (Ukrainian reporting; pending tier-1 Western-wire confirmation.)

Iran's IRGC re-declared the Strait of Hormuz closed on June 20 in response to Israel's continued strikes on Lebanon, warning vessels away — but the United States (VP Vance and CENTCOM) disputed it, saying commercial transit continued; the closure is so far a declaration, not a verified physical interdiction.

The UN Security Council issued a formal statement June 20 demanding the RSF halt its assault on El Obeid in North Kordofan; member states cited substantial RSF buildup with Emirati-supplied vehicles, drone strikes on fuel depots and the 5th Infantry Division headquarters, and roughly 500,000 civilians at risk of mass atrocities.

Iran withheld its delegation and the first round of US-Iran implementation talks was called off over Israel's continued Lebanon campaign; Foreign Minister Araghchi warned that any further Israeli attack on or occupation of Lebanon would be a violation of the interim MOU, tying the deal's survival to an Israeli pullout.

US-Iran Phase-2 implementation talks resumed June 21 at the Burgenstock resort in Switzerland with Vice President Vance and Foreign Minister Araghchi present; Iran's delegation returned within 48 hours of Friday's procedural withhold over Israel's Lebanon campaign.

US Central Command publicly disputed Iran's June-20 Strait of Hormuz closure declaration, stating about 55 commercial vessels and 17 million barrels of oil transited Saturday with US forces continuing operations; the declaration remains rhetorical posture rather than verified physical interdiction.

Hezbollah fired roughly 50 projectiles at IDF positions overnight June 19-20 and the IDF retaliation across south Lebanon killed at least 27 according to Lebanese media; on June 21 Netanyahu and Defense Minister Katz ordered IDF forces to hold fire everywhere except Ali al-Taher Hill, operationalizing a defined Lebanon carve-out from the MOU framework.

The named Power-of-Siberia 2 pricing-and-financing publication window closed June 21 without a tier-1 surfacing — the China $120-130 versus Russia $265-285 per 1,000 cubic-meter gap remains load-bearing; the May-20 Putin-Xi route understanding stands but the price file is not closed.

A multi-source cluster surfaced again on alleged Houthi resumption — MARAD MSCI 2026-006 advisory (dated March 26, 2026), the June 8-9 strike on M/V Tavvishi in the Gulf of Aden, and Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree's 'complete ban on Israeli maritime navigation' declaration; per the new recurrence-escalation rule the gap is promoted to critical operator tier-1 verification rather than declined.

IDF troops are advancing on the northern side of Ali al-Taher Hill, a strategic feature overlooking Nabatiyeh, after Netanyahu and Defense Minister Katz on June 21 ordered hold-fire everywhere except that hill; IDF Chief Zamir called the truce "fragile" and explicitly invoked Ali Taher and Beaufort as defending-the-north objectives.

The first round of US-Iran Phase-2 implementation talks at the Burgenstock resort produced a public "60-day roadmap to a final deal" with VP Vance, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner on the US side and Iranian Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf and FM Araghchi for Iran; immediate technical talks ordered to commence.

Ukrainian air force strikes a Voronezh-region plant producing missile and air-defense electronics with high-precision air-launched cruise missiles. Governor Gusev reports five dead and dozens injured — the first ALCM-attributed deep strike of this cycle.

Russian drone strikes across Ukraine kill at least six civilians, including a 13-year-old boy and three members of one family. UN HRMMU reports 274 civilians killed and 1,763 injured in May — the highest monthly toll since April 2022.

OFAC issues General License X authorizing the production, delivery, and sale of Iranian oil, petrochemicals, and petroleum products for a 60-day window through 2026-08-21, explicitly permitting USD settlement — the first US Treasury authorization permitting Iran USD oil revenue in roughly two decades, landing as a Phase-1 implementation deliverable five days after the Islamabad MOU.
Israeli officials publicly described Israel as "not bound" by the US-Iran MOU on Lebanon.

Live cross-aggregator prints have Brent near $80.59 (+0.93%), WTI ~$77.54, S&P 500 7,500.58 from the prior close (+1.08%), VIX ~16.78 (+2.32%) and gold $4,172.90 (-1.72%) — the post-MOU sub-$80 band holds with mild Hormuz-declaration bid; per standing rule #2 these are live-fetched, not stored constants.

Pakistan-Qatar joint statement confirms US-Iran technical talks continuing all week at the Burgenstock resort. Standing scaffolding now includes a High-Level Committee, a direct US-Iran communications line, a Lebanon de-confliction cell, and a Hormuz safe-passage MOU clause.

IDF strikes hit Lebanese targets in the Nabatieh region and the Beqaa Valley after Hezbollah attacks, with at least 27 reported killed; the IDF publicly says it will demolish Hezbollah infrastructure inside the security zone and strike threats beyond it.

A Bloomberg article dated June 8 surfaces Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree's total-ban-on-Israeli-ships declaration at wire level, narrowing the standing operator-verification gap on the Houthi June-8/9 cluster. The reported strikes on the Tavvishi and Norderney remain only at the regional and specialist-press level.

The fifth round of US-mediated Israel-Lebanon political-track talks opened in Washington on June 23, with Israeli Ambassador Yechiel Leiter publicly characterizing the two countries as "heading toward a train wreck" — the cycle's first cabinet-adjacent Israeli on-record escalatory framing of the bilateral talks themselves.

US Central Command stood up a real-time monitoring mechanism for the Lebanon fighting on June 23 to give US policymakers direct visibility into IDF-Hezbollah engagements — a new US-side de-confliction infrastructure layer that sits alongside the Burgenstock-track Lebanon de-confliction cell.

Trump on Truth Social claimed Iran agreed to "the highest level of Nuclear inspections long into the future (Infinity!!!)" as part of the MOU framework; Iran's UN envoy Ali Bahreini publicly rejected the framing the same day, asserting Tehran's sovereign control over unfrozen-asset disposition.

Live cross-aggregator prints have Brent crude near $77.20 a barrel and WTI near $73.40 at the June-23 close, with the S&P 500 at 7,365.46 (-1.44%), VIX near 17 and gold near $4,076 — the post-MOU sub-$80 band tightens further on OFAC GL X.

Oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz have recovered to roughly 4.8 million barrels a day per Kpler — the highest since the February-28 strikes, with 109 vessels transiting Saturday to Monday and about 35 million barrels exited since the deal, though still far below the ~15 million bpd prewar baseline. The Joint Maritime Information Center cut the threat level to "moderate" and the IMO began evacuating more than 11,000 stranded seafarers.

The nuclear-inspections question split three ways: Trump said Iran "completely agreed" to inspections, IAEA chief Rafael Grossi said inspectors will visit Iranian sites with the timing "not essential" — "this is going to happen" — and Iran's deputy foreign minister said access will be resolved only within the framework of a final agreement.

Israel's defense minister said the IDF will remain in the southern-Lebanon security zone "indefinitely," ruling out the return of displaced residents while Hezbollah remains a threat and signaling a continued hold on land in Lebanon, Syria and Gaza, as a US-brokered Lebanon deconfliction cell of the United States, Iran and Lebanon — facilitated by Qatar and Pakistan — was stood up pointedly without Israel. Israel and Hezbollah traded "blatant" ceasefire-violation accusations, and Syria declined a US request to intervene.

A one-way attack drone — attributed by US officials to Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps — struck the upper deck of a Singapore-flagged cargo ship as it transited the Strait of Hormuz off Oman; the vessel took structural damage but no casualties and continued, and President Trump called it a 'foolish violation' of the ceasefire. Iran did not publicly claim the strike.

US Central Command announced a 'powerful response' to the Hormuz ship attack, with US aircraft striking Iranian missile and drone storage locations and coastal radar sites — the first US-Iran kinetic exchange since the June-17 memorandum.

Israel and Lebanon signed a US-brokered framework agreement after four days of Washington talks mediated by Secretary of State Rubio; Netanyahu announced a limited IDF withdrawal from two pilot areas around the Litani — the Lebanese army moving in with US personnel overseeing — while vowing Israeli forces stay in other positions until Hezbollah is fully disarmed.

Following the US strikes, Iran reportedly launched drones toward Bahrain — headquarters of the US Fifth Fleet — widening the exchange beyond the Strait and onto Gulf-state territory hosting American forces.

The dispute over inspecting Iran's nuclear sites hardened: IAEA chief Grossi said visits 'will happen' and a report framed the deal as granting access, but Iran's Foreign Ministry said it had 'no plans' to admit inspectors to sites damaged during the war, citing 'no established protocol' for such a situation.

The Gulf Cooperation Council foreign ministers said any agreement with Iran should limit its missile capability, and Secretary of State Rubio said Iran would not be allowed to charge tolls in the Strait of Hormuz under a final deal — new conditions narrowing the landing zone for a final agreement.

The UN Security Council formally demanded the Rapid Support Forces halt the assault on Sudan's El Obeid amid mass-atrocity warnings, but the 1591 Sanctions Committee did NOT add Mohamed Hamdan Al Zaabi or Global Security Services to the Darfur sanctions list as HRW had urged — P5 consensus on a UAE national designation did not materialize.

CENTCOM conducted a third wave of strikes on Iranian surveillance, communications, air-defense, drone-storage and minelayer capabilities June 27; on Truth Social, President Trump warned that "Iran will no longer exist" if Washington was forced to "complete the job."

Hezbollah Secretary-General Naim Qassem publicly rejected the June-26 US-brokered Israel-Lebanon framework as "null and void," calling it a "humiliation" and a "surrender of Lebanese sovereignty," and demanded unconditional total Israeli withdrawal; the Lebanese army has not yet deployed into the two pilot zones.

Iran's Revolutionary Guard fired ballistic missiles and drones overnight at the Ali Al Salem airbase in Kuwait and Port Salman in Bahrain (US Fifth Fleet HQ); a US official told CBS no munitions reached the targets and there were no US casualties, while Kuwait's army intercepted two ballistic missiles.

A US official told CBS News that "both sides will stand down after trading strikes" and that vessels would move freely in the Strait of Hormuz; later Sunday Iran skipped a scheduled Burgenstock technical-talks session while Foreign Minister Araghchi urged parties to "adhere to the MOU" and said the Strait "remains under the total oversight and management of Iran throughout the 30 coming days."

Zelensky's one-week ultimatum to Lukashenko to remove Russian drone-relay equipment expired without a Ukrainian strike and without independently verified Russian-equipment removal; Lukashenko publicly 'ruled out Belarus entering the war.'

Lebanon's two main Shia parties Hezbollah and Amal jointly rejected the US-brokered Israel-Lebanon framework as 'unbalanced and a threat to Lebanese sovereignty'; SG Naim Qassem called it a 'humiliating surrender.'

The IDF destroyed the Qasmiya Bridge — the main Litani river crossing — after warning, and Defense Minister Katz publicly declared intent to destroy all Litani crossings and demolish Lebanese border villages.

President Putin personally chaired a Kremlin fuel-supply task-force meeting with a complete diesel-export ban under explicit consideration; Rosneft (90L) and Lukoil (100L) per-transaction pump caps were confirmed, extending the rationing pattern beyond Tatneft.

Ukraine struck two Russian oil refineries on June 28-29 — Slavyansk-na-Kubani in Krasnodar Krai and Yaroslavl (700 km from the front line) — with one killed at Slavyansk and Yaroslavl operations suspended.

Ukrainian drones struck the Slavyansk-na-Kubani refinery in Krasnodar (killing one and wounding one in debris) and a Yaroslavl-region refinery overnight June 28; Russia's overnight retaliation totalled 142 drones and 8 missiles (well below the 500-weapon mass-strike threshold), and President Putin publicly acknowledged a "difficult period" with fuel shortages.

The IDF said it destroyed a roughly 200-metre Hezbollah tunnel in Majdal Zoun containing weapons and rocket-launcher shafts; a separate Israeli drone strike was reported June 27 at the Farah amusement-park intersection in Nabatieh al-Fawqa — both inside the Israel-claimed security zone after the June-26 framework signing.

Russian drone and missile strikes overnight killed at least eight people in Ukraine, with five killed and 28 wounded in Dnipro and three killed in Zaporizhzhia; the total weapon count remained well below the 500-aggregate threshold.

The US Navy's Joint Maritime Information Center widened the Strait of Hormuz transit route near Oman, allowing increased two-way naval traffic — a unilateral operational move directly contradicting Iran's foreign minister who said the Strait would remain under Iranian oversight for thirty more days.

Iran's Burgenstock no-show extended into Monday with no confirmed return; Secretary of State Rubio publicly said technical talks were expected to resume Monday or Tuesday, but no tier-1 wire confirmed an Iranian delegation present.

Seventy-five House Democrats sent Secretary of State Rubio a letter urging investigation of whether the systematic Israeli demolition of Lebanese civilian infrastructure in southern Lebanon triggers conditionality under US arms-export law.
An IDF reservist was severely wounded in an explosion in southern Lebanon on Monday and hospitalized; the IDF did not name the location or attribute the explosion to a party at filing.

Lukashenko publicly ruled out Belarus entering the war on the Russian side, formally closing the Zelensky one-week ultimatum window that lapsed without a Ukrainian strike or independently verified Russian-equipment removal from Belarus territory.

Defense Minister Israel Katz publicly warned that 'any rocket fire directed at an Israeli community will be answered with a devastating strike in the Dahieh' (Hezbollah stronghold in southern Beirut); Katz also reaffirmed the IDF would not retreat from southern Lebanon until Hezbollah disarms.

Russia's Energy Ministry publicly advised against a blanket diesel-export ban citing overstocking and compliance risks recalled from the abortive 2023 ban; the ministry's brake sits inside Putin's June 28 personally chaired fuel-supply task-force deliberation.

Iran's Burgenstock no-show extended into a third business day on Tuesday with no tier-1 wire confirmation of an Iranian delegation present; Secretary of State Rubio publicly said technical talks were expected to resume Monday or Tuesday, but as of Tuesday close no tier-1 wire confirmed attendance.

Sweden and Ukraine announced a defense agreement providing 16 Gripen E fighter jets to Ukraine — a long-range capability closure on the Ukrainian side and a Nordic contribution to NATO cohesion firming.

President Putin publicly acknowledged Russia's fuel-supply crisis in televised remarks, citing pressure from Ukrainian refinery strikes, with queues reported at Moscow gas stations and fuel rationing active across regions — the first cabinet-principal-level candid admission of macro-supply effects from the campaign.

President Trump announced via Truth Social that 'Iran has requested a meeting' to take place Tuesday in Doha, and US envoy Steve Witkoff was reported en route to Doha; Iran's Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf publicly defended continuing Burgenstock talks in a July 1 statement, framing negotiations as a 'method of struggle' — Iranian delegation attendance verification at tier-1 wire remains pending.

Ukrainian drones struck a bearing plant in Penza, Russia, in the early hours of July 1 — the second cycle Ukrainian strike on a Russian defense-industrial supply-chain target beyond the refinery envelope.

Taiwan's Ministry of National Defense reported 13 PLA aircraft sorties with 9 crossing the median line into the Taiwan ADIZ — a 6x surge over the two-sortie baseline of June 30 and the first material Taiwan-lens escalation of the cycle.
Ukraine destroyed twelve electricity substations in southern Crimea on July 1 as part of an ongoing campaign to degrade the peninsula's military utility.

Russia's government formalized a nationwide ban on gasoline exports by producers through the end of July on July 1, with kerosene also included and diesel-export restrictions still under consideration by the Kremlin.

Ukrainian forces struck Russia's Ufa oil refinery in Bashkortostan for the second time within one week on July 1, deepening the campaign into repeat-target strikes on major Volga-Urals-region refining capacity.

Ukrainian overnight strike hit Russia's Penza NIIFI aerospace facility on July 1 at a stand-off range of roughly 1,300 kilometers, targeting sensors used in cruise and ballistic missiles and satellite components.

Sweden and Ukraine finalized a $2.5 billion contract for sixteen Gripen E fighter jets on July 1 with initial deliveries scheduled for 2029-2030, alongside sixteen Gripen C/D units transferred as aid arriving early 2027.

Russia's 11-hour overnight strike on Kyiv July 1-2 launched 74 missiles and 496 drones for a 570-weapon aggregate — clearing the 500-threshold at tier-1 wire (Al Jazeera + CNBC + CBS News); Poland scrambled fighter jets and Finland restricted airspace precautionary during the strike window (Poland/Finland scramble reported by CNBC).

Ukrainian drones struck the Lukoil-owned Nizhegorodnefteorgsintez (NORSI) refinery in Kstovo, Nizhny Novgorod, overnight July 2 — a 17-Mt/yr facility supplying the Moscow region that has been hit multiple times in 2026; the AVT-6 primary distillation unit was struck with fire reported.

Taiwan's Ministry of National Defense recorded 22 PLA sorties on July 2 with 20 of 22 crossing the median line — conducting joint air-sea training and long-distance flights to the western Pacific with a J-16, H-6 bomber, and KJ-500 AEW&C aircraft mix, escalating sharply from July 1's 13/9 count.

Al Jazeera reported that the UN Human Rights Council flagged 500,000 civilians at risk in Sudan's El Obeid as RSF ground troop movements were described as 'substantial' ahead of a possible ground assault, with 60-km encirclement geometry and hallmarks-of-genocide framing compared to El Fasher.

Iran's joint military command publicly warned that tankers must follow Tehran-designated Hormuz routes or face 'immediate and forceful response' and that Tehran will later charge passage fees — the first cycle formal Iranian claim of fee-for-passage authority over Strait shipping.

Gold spot broke above $4,100/oz on July 2 following a weak June US jobs report — intraday prints between $4,111 and $4,130 (up ~2.3%) per Yahoo Finance and Fortune as investors repositioned around the Fed rate-path narrative.

Al Jazeera reported the Tuesday and Wednesday Doha indirect talks produced a US-Iran dispute-resolution channel and framed the $6B frozen-funds release as an in-kind goods purchase mechanism rather than a cash transfer or USD settlement — Iran said 'the required goods would be purchased and made available to Iran' per Deputy FM Gharibabadi.

A massive eleven-hour Russian overnight strike on Kyiv and multiple other regions using Kinzhal hypersonic missiles and drones killed at least thirteen and wounded more than eighty-five in Kyiv alone on July 2.

Brent crude fell below $71 on July 2 (~$70.57 intraday) — the lowest since late February — as Reuters cited rising Strait of Hormuz throughput and progress in indirect US-Iran talks; WTI printed $68.11-$68.43.

Iranian negotiators attended Wednesday's Doha indirect technical talks with Qatar and Pakistan mediating, with Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf publicly citing the recovery of forty-plus million barrels of oil exports since the blockade lift.

Taiwan's Ministry of National Defense recorded five PLA sorties on July 2 with only two crossing the median line into the air-defense identification zone, confirming that the July 1 six-times baseline surge did not persist.

Taiwan's Ministry of National Defense detected 30 PLA aircraft sorties and 7 PLAN vessels as of the 6 a.m. UTC+8 count on July 3, with 26 of 30 sorties crossing the median line into the northern, central, southwestern, and eastern ADIZ — a three-day sustained tempo shift after July 1 (13/9) and July 2 (22/20).

The UN Human Rights Office issued a formal 'red alert' over the humanitarian catastrophe in Sudan's El Obeid on July 3 — 15 drone strikes over three weeks in June killed at least 45 civilians as markets, schools, fuel and water infrastructure were hit; the RSF continues encirclement with Darfur and West Kordofan reinforcements mobilized, but no named ground offensive crossed city limits by 2026-07-05.

The IDF struck approximately ten Hezbollah sites in southern Lebanon on July 3 — including Bint Jbeil, Baraashit, Kounine, and Beit Yahoun — in tactical retaliation for a gunfire attack on Israeli troops within the June 26 ceasefire framework.

Human Rights Watch and the UN's IOM warned Sudan's El Obeid is approaching total siege — an RSF drone campaign killed approximately 50 civilians over the prior ten days without a ground-assault threshold trigger yet.

Gold spot closed near $4,181 on Friday July 3 (up ~1.25%) after a weak June US nonfarm-payrolls print of +57k versus a +110k consensus — traders pared September-rate-hike bets; Brent held ~$72, WTI $68.76, natural gas $3.24/MMBtu; US equity and Treasury markets closed for the Independence Day observance.

Taiwan's Ministry of National Defense recorded eight PLA sorties on July 4 with six crossing the median line into ADIZ — a sharp reversion from July 3's 30/26 count that breaks the three-day surge on Day 4.

Iran's ambassador to China said on July 4 that Tehran will 'definitely' charge Hormuz passage fees after the 60-day sanctions-relief window, with possible 'special treatment' for friendly nations — a hardening of the July 2 verbal warning by joint military command via a non-standard sub-cabinet channel; the fee framing has not yet been formalized as a published toll order.

Ukraine's SBU and Special Operations Forces struck three Baltic-region targets overnight July 4 — the Kronstadt Marine Plant (with footage showing a hit on the Baltic Fleet corvette Boykiy in dry dock), the St. Petersburg oil terminal (Governor Beglov confirmed the large-scale attack, no casualties), and the Vysotsk port that handles oil, LNG, grain and coal — at approximately 850-900 km reach; Zelensky framed the strikes as 'long-range sanctions' marking a pivot from the top-10-refinery campaign to Baltic Fleet and export-infrastructure targeting.
Qatar's Foreign Ministry framed an Iranian religious mourning window running July 4-9 as the reason the next US-Iran Doha round will be deferred to July 10 or later.
US markets closed July 4 for Independence Day — thin global tape into the weekend; Brent held sub-$71 and gold near $4,140 spot into the close.

Taiwan's Ministry of National Defense recorded eight PLA sorties on July 5 with six crossing the median line — a second consecutive day matching the July 4 count exactly and confirming the July 1-3 escalation (13/9, 22/20, 30/26) broke on Day 4 rather than being paused; the candidate pattern stays reset and the pre-scheduled tactical demonstration hypothesis strengthens.

The IDF said a strike killed a Hezbollah operative emerging from a tunnel at the Ali Taher ridge in southern Lebanon on July 5, following an Egoz Commando manhunt — a single-target tactical response within the June 26 ceasefire framework and consistent with the standing tactical-response tempo without escalation conversion.

Iran's ambassador to China said Tehran will "definitely" charge Hormuz passage fees after the 60-day sanctions-relief window with possible "special treatment" for friendly nations — the ambassador-channel BRICS-buyer-first pricing signal now cleared multi-source corroboration across Fortune (1-wire), Al Jazeera and Times of Israel (2-established), with Reuters/AP/AFP direct pickup pending.

CSIS published satellite-imagery analysis of vehicle activity and construction at the Pickaxe Mountain tunnel complex near Natanz with reinforced tunnel entrances, joining Times of Israel and Iran International on the alleged post-MOU physical-facility activity file — first cycle-level tier-1 institutional footing for the imagery.

The US-Iran stand-down held into an eighth day with no fifth US strike and no third Iranian retaliation as the Iranian religious-mourning window (July 4-9, Ashura-adjacent) opened; Qatar and Pakistan mediators framed the next Doha round as scheduled 'as soon as possible' after the window closes, and no fresh Trump extinction-rhetoric surfaced.

CNN, NPR, and Al Jazeera surfaced coordinated "Khamenei state funeral / mourning procession July 4-9" framing across Tehran, Qom, and Mashhad — 127 days after Ali Khamenei's Feb-28 death, which is not a standard Shia memorial interval; framing held for operator verification per standing rule #9.

Russia launched an aggregate strike of a claimed 625 long-range drones and missiles on Ukraine overnight July 5-6 killing at least 22 people in the Kyiv region — first aggregate above the 500-drone threshold since the June-2 saturation strike; Russia's MoD claim of 613 intercepts is unverified by Ukrainian Air Force at filing.

Ukrainian long-range drones struck the Gazprom Neft Omsk refinery — Russia's largest by capacity — overnight at approximately 2,500 km reach, hitting the ELOU-AVT-11 primary refining unit; Ukraine's General Staff separately characterized it as the 9th of Russia's top 11 refineries hit in the 2026 campaign (Ukrainian framing, pending independent inventory reconciliation).

Taiwan's Ministry of National Defense recorded 5 PLA sorties on the July 6 morning update with 3 crossing the median line — third consecutive sub-threshold day continuing the pattern-break from the July 3 peak, with the Bessent-He Lifeng trade lane still silent into a seventh day of the arc.

An Israeli drone strike on a vehicle in Nabatieh al-Fawqa in southern Lebanon killed four civilians on July 6 — the deadliest single incident since the June framework — as Hezbollah again held kinetic discipline with no retaliatory salvo and no Beirut target struck.

China conducted a submarine-launched ballistic-missile test over the Pacific on July 6, confirmed at institutional tier (CNN + CSIS analysis + Washington Post), coinciding with the opening of the annual China-Russia Joint Sea naval exercise. A dummy warhead reportedly landed in the South Pacific — a first-cycle Chinese strategic-force demonstration held for verification yesterday and now cleared.

Brent held at $72.07 with WTI below $69 as US markets reopened after the Independence Day observance; the S&P 500 climbed 0.7% to about 7,483, VIX eased 1.1% to 15.97, and OPEC+ approved a +188k-bpd August quota expansion — the sub-$80 Brent band-hold now runs three-plus consecutive sessions.
Taiwan's defense ministry recorded four PLA sorties with three median-line crossings on July 7, a fourth consecutive sub-threshold day that extends the reversion from the July 1-3 surge.

The UN Human Rights Council passed a motion condemning Rapid Support Forces violence at El Obeid and opened an urgent inquiry as 28 countries jointly warned of impending atrocities, while the RSF siege continued without a ground assault across the city perimeter.

The US Treasury's OFAC formally revoked Iran General License X and issued a narrow replacement, GL X1, authorizing only a wind-down of existing dealings through July 17 — reversing the 60-day USD-settlement authorization 15 days after issuing it, with no executed Iran-oil sale ever surfacing.

Iran's IRGC struck commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz on July 7, hitting a Qatari LNG carrier, and the US retaliated against a reported 80-plus Iranian targets while revoking OFAC General License X for Iran oil sales. Trump declared the June framework "over" and Iran threatened a "crushing response," breaking the ten-day US-Iran stand-down. Brent crude spiked about 5% to roughly $78.

Brent held near $72 for a third session and the S&P 500 sat around 7,483 as OPEC+ confirmed a 188,000-barrel-per-day August quota increase — no war premium despite the mid-week Ukraine-Russia strike exchange.

The United States carried out additional strikes on Iranian coastal and IRGC sites — reported to include Sirik, Qeshm and Bandar Abbas around the Strait of Hormuz — a day after its 80-plus-target retaliation, while President Trump declared the June framework "over" and "a waste of time," deepening the collapse of the ten-day stand-down.

A multi-day state funeral for Iran's Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei — killed in the February 28 opening strike — drew very large crowds across Tehran, Qom, Najaf and Karbala from July 3-9, a delayed ceremonial funeral rather than a new death; his successor Mojtaba Khamenei has led since March.

NATO's Ankara summit on July 7-8 committed EUR70 billion in military equipment, assistance and training for Ukraine across 2026-27, reaffirmed the Article 5 collective-defence pledge, and approved a EUR27 billion investment to modernise allied fuel storage and distribution.

Brent crude held near $77.7 a barrel (up about 5% on the week) and gold traded near $4,075 an ounce with the VIX up to about 17.7, as the returned Strait-of-Hormuz war premium kept the month-long sub-$80 oil band broken.

headline: An additional US strike round on Iran — roughly 90 targets — firmed at a fresh Al Jazeera dateline, and Trump called the June ceasefire "over" while signaling Washington is still willing to resume talks with Tehran. Iran's IRGC claim of an 85-target strike on the same Kuwait and Bahrain bases hit in late June stays unverified against a re-dating tell, and Brent eased to about $76 rather than spiking.

Brent crude held near $76 a barrel (WTI ~$71.4) with gold about $4,111 and the VIX easing to ~15.7 at the July-10 close — the market kept pricing a bounded US-Iran exchange, not a Strait-of-Hormuz supply shock, even as shipping through the strait slowed.

Qatari mediators met Iranian officials to de-escalate the Strait-of-Hormuz standoff as the US-Iran exchange held without a new escalation and Washington's talks-resume signal persisted; Brent stayed near $76 and the IRGC's 85-target Gulf-base claim remained unverified on the standing re-dating tell.

The US-Iran exchange re-intensified after a two-day lull: a new US strike wave on Iran and an Iranian counter-strike on US bases in Bahrain, Kuwait and Jordan were reported on independent Al Jazeera datelines, though every tier-1 Western wire attempt was blocked and the specific '140-site' scale Iran claimed could not be verified.

Russia and Ukraine traded sub-threshold overnight strikes — about 137 drones and missiles, nine killed — and Russia suspended shipping through the Kerch Strait after Ukrainian drone raids on its tankers; the diesel-export ban through July 31 still stands.

Brent crude climbed more than 4% to about $79 a barrel as Washington and Tehran clashed over the Strait of Hormuz — a real oil-supply-risk bid, but short of the $90-plus a full closure would bring, with the waterway staying open to traffic.
With GL X1 set to expire July 17 and no successor license announced, the renewed US-Iran strikes made a full snap-back into the pre-June Iran-sanctions regime the more likely near-term outcome.

Iran struck two UAE tankers near the Strait of Hormuz on July 12, killing an Indian crew member and drawing GCC condemnation — the first commercial-shipping fatality of the US-Iran exchange. Coverage described attacks on shipping and a "battle over control" of the waterway, not a formal closure order; Brent climbed to about $87 but stayed below the $90-plus a genuine closure would bring.

Brent crude climbed about 4.5% to roughly $87 a barrel and the VIX ticked up to about 17 as the US-Iran exchange widened to Gulf shipping — an oil-supply-risk bid rather than a systemic risk-off panic, with equities off only modestly and the Strait still transiting.

OFAC designated more than 50 entities in an Iranian oil-shipping network spanning the UAE, Singapore, Hong Kong and India on July 14, and an IRGC weapons-procurement ring July 15 — the first post-snap-back enforcement actions, documented via law-firm summaries while Treasury’s own pages remain unreachable.

The US struck dozens of Iranian targets in a fresh daytime strike wave dated July 14, a roughly 90-minute CENTCOM operation, as President Trump said strikes would continue "until I say so" and demanded renewed negotiations.

Iran's cruise-missile strike on two UAE tankers near the Strait of Hormuz is now confirmed by UAE and Gulf outlets — vessels Mombasa and Al Bahyah, one Indian crew member killed and eight injured — upgrading the earlier single-source report; the outlets date the attack July 14.

OFAC's GL X1 wind-down license for Iran oil dealings is set to expire July 17 with no successor announced, and legal analysts confirm the pre-June sanctions regime automatically snaps back on July 18.

A reported US reinstatement of a naval blockade of Iranian ports appears in wire coverage but in no White House or Treasury order, and Trump walked back a previously floated 20% Hormuz transit toll; oil eased to about $86, undercutting a supply-shock reading.

US strikes on Iran continued into a fifth straight day, with President Trump saying the attacks would intensify nightly and framing them as protecting shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. No pause and no scheduled negotiating round have been confirmed.

OFAC's GL X1 wind-down licence for Iranian oil and petrochemical dealings expires July 17 at 12:01am EDT with no successor authorisation announced, restoring the full pre-June-22 Iran sanctions regime on July 18.

A Russian overnight strike on Kyiv killed two people and injured six across the Darnytskyi and Sviatoshynskyi districts, part of a roughly 122-drone night that stayed well below Russia's mass-strike scale.
Ukraine struck six Russian tankers and two tugboats in the Black Sea and Sea of Azov overnight, extending a shipping campaign that has now pushed Russia to suspend traffic through the Don-Azov canal.

Brent crude eased to about $83.96 a barrel and the VIX slipped to 15.84 even as US strikes on Iran ran a fifth day — no supply shock is being priced, and both readings sit far from the levels an effective blockade or a closed Strait would produce.

The full pre-June US sanctions regime on Iran returned to force July 18 after the wind-down licence expired at 12:01am July 17 with no successor. The restoration required no signature, and the secondary-sanctions threat against Chinese banks and refiners is live again.

A joint FLA-JNIM ambush near Anefis, Mali reportedly killed more than 50 Malian soldiers in a convoy attack alongside Russian Africa Corps personnel — evidence of deepening Tuareg-separatist and al-Qaeda-affiliate tactical coordination.

US strikes on Iran ran through a ninth consecutive night by July 20, widening to power facilities and a desalination plant in Hormozgan province, with about 50 people reported killed in July. No pause and no scheduled negotiating round accompanied the escalation.

Iran responded to the strike campaign July 19 with missile and drone attacks on US bases in Gulf states, per Al Jazeera. Iranian state media named an ammunition depot and a Patriot radar site in Kuwait, but no US or Kuwaiti confirmation of specific targets has surfaced.

Iran's deputy foreign minister said Washington is violating the June accord's terms and Iran is "no longer implementing them" — suspension language that stops short of a formal withdrawal, which no primary source carries.

A Russian strike killed 10 people on a ship near Odesa while Ukraine sent more than 400 drones at Moscow region, wounding at least 10 — Ukraine's largest capital-region raid of the war and a step past its refinery-and-shipping campaign.

Andy Burnham became UK prime minister, replacing Keir Starmer, after Labour elected him party leader on July 16 — a change of government in a nuclear-armed NATO member and one of Ukraine’s larger military backers.

Secretary of State Rubio signaled openness to diplomacy with Tehran as the strike campaign entered a ninth night — the first senior US de-escalation signal since the floated Qatari-mediated round stalled.

Three US service members were killed July 18-20 — two at Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Jordan, one in a drone detonation in Iraq — with nearly 100 injured across two weeks of Iranian retaliation. PBS reports 17 US deaths since the war began in February, an aggregate figure not previously carried here.

US strikes on Iran ran a tenth consecutive night into July 21, hitting military command centers and maritime capabilities. Greek tankers were struck in the Strait of Hormuz and off Oman as Iran kept pressure on commercial shipping.

Lebanon’s army deployed into the southern pilot zones of Froun, Srifa and Zawtar al-Gharbiya for the first time, and Israeli forces withdrew from Zawtar al-Gharbiyeh as the June framework requires. Defense Minister Katz said remaining forces stay "indefinitely" — "even if there’s an American demand."

Oil tankers made U-turns in the southern Red Sea after Houthi blockade warnings, and Trump threatened airstrikes if the group blocks shipping — the first material Red Sea re-activation signal since the September 2025 pause.
Hamas elected Khalil al-Hayya — the architect of its ceasefire and hostage-talks track — as political chief, filling a leadership vacancy of roughly two years.

US strikes on Iran ran an eleventh consecutive night while Iranian retaliation widened: Jordan’s military said six Iranian missiles were fired at the kingdom, four intercepted, and Iranian attacks targeted bases in Bahrain. The Pentagon identified a fourth US service member killed, Sgt. Michael Swinton.

Brent crude jumped 3.6% past $94 — its first genuine war-premium spike of the re-escalation — after Secretary Rubio said Iran is "not serious" about peace talks. A reported July 21 settlement of $91.01 had already topped $90, ending the market’s two-week refusal to price the war.

The Greek tankers struck near Hormuz were identified as Dynacom’s Acheloos (Liberia flag) and Kavomaleas (Malta flag); the Kavomaleas caught fire and its crew was evacuated by Omani authorities, with the attacks reported to UKMTO.

Rubio met China's Wang Yi for 90 minutes in Manila — the first senior US-China meeting since Iran sanctions snapped back — discussing Xi's planned September US visit and a South China Sea coast-guard clash, while Beijing's official silence on the restored sanctions entered a seventh day.

CISA warned that Iranian-affiliated hackers are exploiting programmable logic controllers across US critical infrastructure, days after a joint US-allied advisory detailed a sustained Russian FSB campaign against infrastructure routers.

Houthi forces attacked Saudi-linked oil tankers in the southern Red Sea: UKMTO relayed a confirmed strike and fire aboard the Encelia about 70 nautical miles southwest of Al Shuqaiq, while a claimed second hit on the Layla remains unverified. It is the group's first confirmed attack on commercial shipping since the September 2025 pause, converting Monday's blockade warnings into action within 24 hours.

US strikes on Iran ran a twelfth consecutive night, with CENTCOM targeting maritime capabilities, drone storage and logistics infrastructure. Al Jazeera carried reports of new Iranian retaliatory fire toward Kuwait, Bahrain and Jordan, though it is unverified whether this is a second salvo distinct from the July 21-22 attack.

Iran fired a second, distinct salvo toward Jordan, Bahrain and Kuwait on July 23 — Sheikh Isa Air Base and Muwaffaq Salti were named targets — 48 hours after the first six-missile Jordan salvo. Claims the fire extended to Oman and Qatar rest on a single flawed-dateline source and are unverified.

The European Union adopted its 21st Russia sanctions package, adding fourteen Chinese and Hong Kong companies for supplying the war effort; by 31 July Beijing had barred fourteen European companies from receiving Chinese dual-use goods in retaliation. (Backfilled 8 September.)

Brent crude settled at $94.07 on July 22 — confirmed by two independent fetches — capping three sessions of war-premium pricing since Rubio’s "not serious" verdict. Thursday-morning intraday prints conflict sharply between data feeds (one near $98, the chart feed near $86), so the day’s direction is unresolved pending the July 23 settlement.

The Pentagon-identified US death toll in the Iran war stands at four — Sgt. Michael Swinton, killed in a controlled detonation at Erbil Air Base July 21, is the fourth — while a circulating claim of 14-17 confirmed deaths failed a primary-source check, the second fabricated casualty ledger in two days.

Russia's July-8 diesel-export ban covering all producers is now documented at the state wire TASS, with odd-even gasoline rationing reported across multiple Russian regions; overnight, Ukraine sent more than 200 drones at Russian regions per the Russian Defense Ministry, while Moscow's answer to the July-20 raid stayed unfired a third day.

US strikes on Iran completed a thirteenth consecutive night, hitting command centers, drone storage and coastal surveillance, as Trump threatened the "biggest strikes yet" and said he is weighing a massive attack. Iranian media reported blasts at Khorramabad, Jask, Ahvaz and Bandar Abbas.

Russia struck a Kyiv arms exhibition with a daytime ballistic missile, killing at least 10 and injuring over 100 — an unusual departure from its night-strike pattern. Overnight, Ukraine sent one of its largest drone barrages of the war (Russia claims 571 intercepted), setting fire to Wildberries e-commerce warehouses near St. Petersburg.

Brent crude crossed $100 a barrel intraday for the first time since May, after a July-23 settlement between $99.17 and $100.69 depending on source. The suspected $86 feed print was confirmed as a contract-rollover artifact; the war premium is holding across a third session.

Ukraine's July-6 strike on the Omsk refinery — 2,500 km from the border, the war's deepest — is confirmed as a new distinct major, completing the set of Russia's 11 largest gasoline producers per Ukraine's General Staff. Overnight, 223 drones hit a Ulyanovsk refinery and Voronezh logistics.

Local officials in Lebanon's pilot zones disputed the withdrawal framework's progress — the mayors of Froun and Srifa told Al Jazeera "nothing changed" and Israeli forces remain visible on Zawtar's outskirts, while Defense Minister Katz repeated that forces stay until Hezbollah disarms.

US strikes on Iran ran a fourteenth consecutive night, hitting IRGC Navy headquarters in Gilan province and communications infrastructure — a claimed pause failed verification. Trump simultaneously threatened the "biggest strikes yet" and said he "hasn't decided" on major new strikes, calling Tehran "getting serious."

Brent crude settled at $96.78 on Friday, retreating 3.9% from a $101.19 intraday high — the first $100+ touch since May did not convert to a $100 close. The war premium held above $95 for a second straight session as equities steadied and VIX rose to 18.58.

The Senate is eyeing a floor vote on the revised "Sanctioning Russia Act of 2026" — with secondary-tariff authority — the week of July 28, with Trump pushing to fold Iran measures into the package; House recess would delay final action.

The US military made no strike announcement for the first time in fourteen nights, and no new strikes on Iran were reported overnight. Whether the campaign has actually paused is unconfirmed — no official statement exists, and mediators are reported pressing truce proposals.
Russia extended its gasoline-export ban through the end of 2026 — five months past the July 31 decision gate — with Deputy PM Novak saying the diesel ban lifts only when the domestic market recovers.

Ukrainian drones struck Wildberries logistics facilities again — the fifth hit on the e-commerce giant in a week, spanning St. Petersburg, Tver and Crimea — while the Novospasskoye refinery in Ulyanovsk took its first-ever strike.
Senate Republicans signed off on adding Iran to the revised Russia sanctions bill, Majority Leader Thune said, with a floor vote on the secondary-tariff measure expected as early as this week.

Red Sea war-risk insurance climbed above 1% of hull value and insurers are reported refusing cover for Saudi-linked vessels, even as UKMTO reported no confirmed attacks on merchant shipping in the past 72 hours.
Netanyahu convened his security cabinet ahead of a Washington visit centered on Iran strategy, as an Israeli court separately rejected his bid to cancel wartime Likud primaries.

Houthi forces fired missiles and drones at Saudi Aramco facilities at Jizan and Yanbu on July 25-26 — the war's first attacks on Saudi territory — with a smoke column reported at Jizan and the Yanbu missiles intercepted by a Patriot battery. Saudi Arabia has not commented on the extent of any damage.

US strikes on Iran stopped after Trump ordered a hold when an Omani mediation delegation arrived in Tehran, ending fourteen consecutive announced strike nights. A second quiet night is reported with Iran also standing down, though no official pause statement exists from either side.

Brent crude fell about 7% Monday morning to near $89.78 as the US-Iran pause reports unwound the war premium. The disputed July-23 settlement also resolved at $100.69 — retroactively the first $100 close since May.
Senate leaders moved to add Iran to the revised Russia sanctions bill, with a procedural vote on the secondary-tariff measure expected as early as Tuesday.

Zelensky said Russia is preparing to receive 30,000 additional North Korean troops for the war, with preparations reported underway in the Voronezh region — which would roughly triple North Korea's prior deployment.

Russia sent 147 drones overnight, killing one civilian in Zaporizhzhia, while Ukrainian drones struck an export terminal in Rostov Oblast — the deep-strike campaign broadening from refineries to export logistics as Russia's answer window passed its eighth day without a mass strike.

Sudan's army secured the Khartoum-El Obeid highway after a multi-day offensive — the first major territorial shift in months, opening a supply corridor to the besieged city — while RSF answered with drone strikes on El Obeid.

Netanyahu and Trump met at the White House for the first time since the war began — roughly 80 minutes, no press conference. Netanyahu called it "one of the best we've ever had"; the White House said "productive"; no substance was disclosed.

The US strike hold on Iran reached a fourth consecutive quiet night, with Trump saying the US is "in talks" with Iran and hopes for "good things." No official pause has been declared by either capital; Netanyahu meets Trump in Washington today with Iran strategy at the top of the agenda.

A second major-outlet compilation corroborates a US death toll well above the four officially identified: Al Jazeera's casualty overview carries 17 deaths attributed to CENTCOM with 15 names, alongside Time's earlier 18-name list. The Pentagon has published no official aggregate, and the precise count remains disputed.

Brent extended its slide to roughly $85-86 at Monday's settle and traded near $84 on Tuesday, deepening the war-premium unwind — while Gulf war-risk insurance held at 7.5-10% of hull value, a widening gap between the oil tape and the shipping market.

UKMTO logged a tanker-reported explosion in the southern Red Sea with crew and vessel safe, as Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree claimed a missile attack on the Saudi oil tanker NCC Ghazal. No maritime authority has attributed the explosion, and Saudi Arabia's public silence on attacks against its interests now runs to ten days.

The US strike hold reached a fifth consecutive quiet night, with Trump describing "very friendly negotiations" with Iran and a "good chance of progress." Israeli ministers countered that Israel "won't be bound" by any Iran deal; no official pause statement exists from either capital.

Ukraine struck the Ryazan oil refinery (fire confirmed), a Wildberries logistics center in Ryazan, and Black Sea Fleet infrastructure, with a blackout reported in occupied Crimea. Russia's overnight answer was 131 drones that killed nine across Ukraine — its threatened mass strike still absent on day nine.

The five-night halt in US-Iran fire ended.
