Iran launched ballistic missiles at Jordan's Muwaffaq Salti Air Base, all of which were intercepted, and aircraft then struck logistics and weapons sites in eastern Iraq used by Iran-aligned armed groups. Saudi aircraft were reported to have taken part, though Riyadh's own statement claims only air defence.

Saudi Arabia's defence ministry broke ten days of public silence, saying its air defences intercepted drones that targeted petroleum facilities in the Eastern Province and Riyadh and were launched from Iraqi territory. The statement described the strikes as a response to those attacks but characterised the Saudi role as defensive.

Iraq's presidency denounced and categorically rejected the strikes on Iraqi territory, and the prime minister convened an emergency meeting of the Ministerial Council for National Security. No ambassador was summoned and no parliamentary motion was tabled.

US Central Command struck dozens of Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps targets inside Iran, hitting command centres, missile and drone facilities and coastal surveillance sites at Qeshm Island, Ahvaz, Abadan, Bushehr, Kazerun and Farashband. CENTCOM described the two-hour operation as a response to Iranian attacks on US forces.

A Russian strike on Radushne near Kryvyi Rih killed at least six members of one family, including three children. Zelensky said that as of now it was a North Korean ballistic missile, with examinations to follow — the first reported use of a North Korean missile since August 2025. (Backfilled 8 September.)

Russia launched a mass strike on Ukraine after nine days of far smaller packages, firing 284 drones and 74 missiles overnight. Ukraine's air force intercepted 320 of them — 265 drones and 55 missiles. At least eight people were killed, and Poland scrambled fighter jets as the strike ran along its border.

Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said Russia will lift its diesel export ban once the domestic fuel market recovers, while extending the gasoline export ban through the end of 2026 — signalling relief rather than the tightening expected before Friday's decision point.

US Treasury Secretary Bessent and Trade Representative Greer held an hour-long video call with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng covering rare earths, agricultural products and trade and investment boards, ahead of an expected Xi Jinping visit in September. Beijing raised concerns about US trade restrictions.
Israeli air strikes killed at least six Palestinians in the Gaza Strip overnight, including two children, with more than thirty wounded.

The US Treasury designated six entities and individuals for supporting the sanctioned Iranian airline Mahan Air, including a Shanghai-based travel company. The action targets logistics rather than the Chinese banks or independent refiners that the restored sanctions wall had threatened.

The June-26 framework's deadline for Israel to complete its two-pilot-area withdrawal from southern Lebanon arrived with only Zawtar al-Gharbiyeh vacated, and no extension or replacement timetable has been announced as of this update. Israel said days earlier that it would accept no additional withdrawals and would retain freedom of action. The next scheduled talks fall on August 4.

Iran's military said it struck the US-used Ahmad Al-Jaber Air Base in Kuwait with drones. A second account says the drones were shot down, and a third describes Kuwaiti power and water plants being hit. No Kuwaiti or American official is on the record in any of them.

A Gaza disarmament agreement was announced under which Hamas would hand weapons to a Palestinian committee over roughly two to three hundred days, conditional on phased Israeli withdrawal and overseen by an international verification commission. Israel has not publicly confirmed it accepts the terms.

A federal advisory records malicious cyber actors targeting internet-facing controllers at water and wastewater utilities and causing operational disruptions, and urges operators to take those controllers off the public internet. It names no actor and no country.

Kuwait's defence ministry said on 31 July that hostile targets were engaged and destroyed, causing material damage from falling shrapnel and no casualties. The statement names no base and does not acknowledge that anything was struck.

Trump has ordered strikes on Iranian energy infrastructure — oil refineries and power plants — to begin as soon as this weekend, according to unnamed US officials cited in multiple reports. Nothing has been struck yet, and no official has confirmed the order on the record.

Russia struck Kyiv overnight with ballistic missiles and drones, killing at least nine people and wounding more than thirty. It is the deadliest single attack on the capital in this phase of the campaign.

Iran’s Supreme National Security Council said it would tighten control over the Strait of Hormuz and stop issuing transit permits until American operations end, while Quds Force officers coordinated with Hezbollah, the Houthis and Iraqi groups on raising the war’s cost to the United States.

President Trump said on August 2 that he would "cancel the attack" on Iran, subject to rapidly reaching a deal, naming the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz among the terms. He said negotiations would begin Monday.

Russia and Ukraine traded strikes on August 2 that killed at least fourteen people between them. Ukraine hit the Saratov oil refinery, the Engels strategic airbase, a fuel depot in Kaluga and a warehouse in Samara.

No account of the July 30 US target list inside Iran places nuclear infrastructure in it. Two independent descriptions of the strikes name Revolutionary Guard command centres, missile and drone facilities and coastal defence sites across four provinces, including Bushehr, and neither mentions a nuclear facility.

Michigan water utilities have reported breaches alongside Minnesota's, widening a campaign the FBI has described across seven states. No treatment or supply function has been disrupted, and no federal agency has attributed the attacks to Iran.

Israeli and Lebanese delegations are confirmed for talks in Rome running August 4 to 6, the first scheduled session since the withdrawal deadline lapsed. Israel has said it is concerned the Lebanese army is not fulfilling its role in the south.

Iran’s foreign ministry spokesman said Iran would neither host a delegation nor be a guest of another country “during these days,” declining the round President Trump announced for Monday. Trump described the prospective talks as Iran’s “last chance.”

At least twenty-seven people were reported killed as Russia and Ukraine traded heavy attacks across August 2 and 3, with strikes in Zaporizhzhia, Kryvyi Rih, Krasnodar, Belgorod and Crimea. The count comes from a single report and may include the fourteen recorded here for August 2.

Iran has not confirmed any direct talks with the United States. Foreign Minister Araghchi said negotiations with Oman over the Strait of Hormuz are in their final stages — a mediated channel about shipping, not a US-Iran round.

As of this morning's cutoff, a third consecutive night had passed with no reported strikes on Iranian territory, and the reported order against Iranian refineries and power plants remained unexecuted.
Oil fell about five percent after the announcement, unwinding a large part of the war premium built through late July.

The negotiations Trump said would begin Monday had not convened by Monday evening. Iran’s foreign ministry said it would neither host a delegation nor travel “during these days,” Trump called the prospective talks Iran’s “last chance,” and the round was being reported for August 5.

Taiwan’s defence ministry recorded a single PLA aircraft entering the southwestern air defence identification zone on August 3, alongside seven navy vessels and three official ships, with no median-line crossings reported.

The United States has expended virtually all of its long-range precision missiles — ATACMS and the Precision Strike Missile — during the Iran war, according to sources cited by Reuters. Interceptor stocks are reported heavily drawn down. The White House disputes the characterisation, saying the country holds more munitions than anyone in the world.

American officials said an agreement on the Strait of Hormuz could come within days. Treasury Secretary Bessent named Wednesday, Secretary of State Rubio said progress had been made but there was still work to do, and President Trump said all-day talks had been held and warned Iran would be hit very hard if the Strait did not open soon.
A projectile sank an Indian-flagged vessel off the coast of Yemen. All fourteen crew were rescued. No party has claimed responsibility, and no maritime authority has attributed the attack.

Israeli and Lebanese delegations opened talks in Rome on August 4, the first scheduled session since the withdrawal deadline lapsed on July 31 with a single disputed village vacated and no replacement timetable.

A fourth consecutive night passed with no reported strikes inside Iran, and the order against Iranian refineries and power plants remained unexecuted. The negotiations Washington announced for Monday still had not convened, and Tehran has agreed to nothing.

House Oversight Democrats have asked the Pentagon for records behind changes to its Iran war casualty database, after four deaths were moved into a separate overseas-operations category. No official cumulative casualty total has been published.
Russia dropped more than 8,300 glide bombs on Ukraine during July, a record since the full-scale invasion began, according to the Ukrainian military.

Iran has not confirmed that any direct negotiation is taking place. Tehran's account remains an Oman-mediated conversation about shipping, and President Pezeshkian publicly denied reports that he had threatened to resign during the Hormuz discussions.

Ukraine struck the Syzran oil refinery and Wildberries logistics warehouses in the Moscow and Vladimir regions overnight into August 4, with a fire reported at the refinery. Angarsk remains the only major Russian refinery not yet hit.

A Russian ballistic-missile attack on Kyiv and the surrounding region killed at least seventeen people and injured forty-four. President Zelensky said interceptors could have saved lives, and Ukrainian accounts report that none of the incoming package was brought down.

Police found a drone carrying an explosive device beside a Ukrainian cargo aircraft at Leipzig/Halle airport in Germany, and a second flying object struck a cargo plane at the same airport. Germany's interior minister called it a new level of danger. No attribution has been made.

Taiwan launched its annual military exercises as Chinese pressure continued. The island's defence ministry publishes daily counts of Chinese air and naval activity, and no verified change in those levels has been established since August 3.
North Korea's Kim Yo Jong threatened additional military options after Japan test-fired a US-supplied Tomahawk cruise missile, accusing Washington of enabling a Japanese military build-up.

Yemen's Houthis said they struck two Saudi-linked oil tankers and threatened to widen their campaign in the Red Sea. No maritime authority, vessel operator or Saudi official has confirmed any damage, and the group made a similarly worded claim on July 22.
The United Nations warned that drone strikes in Sudan are worsening, attributing more than 80 percent of this year's civilian deaths there to aerial attacks.
Israeli and Lebanese delegations continued direct talks in Rome without announcing a withdrawal timetable. Hezbollah called the negotiations a humiliation, and the process was described as stalling.

Israel struck southern Lebanon after issuing its first evacuation warnings there in weeks, killing at least one person and wounding twelve in Tibnin. Two Israeli soldiers were killed and one critically wounded in an explosion at Majdal Selem. The Israeli military described the strikes as a response to a ceasefire violation by Hezbollah, while Israeli and Lebanese delegations were holding a second day of talks in Rome.

Iran's foreign ministry said it and Oman had agreed the geographical coordinates of a commercial shipping route through the Strait of Hormuz and were preparing a joint statement. Spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei said reopening the strait remains contingent on the United States lifting its naval blockade and halting attacks on Iranian infrastructure. Oman issued no public confirmation of the terms.
As of this morning's cutoff, no strikes inside Iran had been reported for a fifth consecutive night, and the order against Iranian refineries and power plants remained unexecuted.

Ukraine struck two Russian oil refineries overnight, at Yaroslavl and in Bashkortostan, in what President Zelensky described as a deep-strike drone attack. Ukrainian reporting describes the Yaroslavl plant as among Russia's largest and the seventh top-tier refinery hit this year.

An oil tanker reported two explosions while transiting the Strait of Hormuz on August 6, southeast of Kumzar. The crew was reported safe. No party has claimed the incident and no maritime authority has attributed it.

Reuters, citing Ukrainian military intelligence, reported that North Korea has deployed a ballistic-missile unit to Russia's Voronezh region — around 90 personnel attached to the 112th Missile Brigade, with up to 120 short-range ballistic missiles. Neither Moscow nor Pyongyang has confirmed it.

Taiwan's defence ministry recorded 21 Chinese military aircraft in the island's air defence identification zone on August 5, including 17 crossings of the Taiwan Strait median line, and 14 aircraft with 6 crossings on August 6; the August 4 report was not retrieved. The last figure this dashboard carried, for August 3, was a single aircraft and no crossings. The readings fall during Taiwan's annual Han Kuang exercises.

A sixth consecutive night passed with no reported strikes inside Iran, and the order against Iranian refineries and power plants remained unexecuted. President Trump publicly denied that the United States is running low on munitions, days after reporting that it had expended virtually all of its long-range precision missiles.

The United States removed the Iraqi carrier Fly Baghdad from its sanctions list, unblocking the airline and delisting two of its aircraft, though its owner remains designated. The airline had been sanctioned over alleged links to Iran's Revolutionary Guard.

Houthi forces killed Saudi-backed Yemeni government troops in the heaviest ground fighting since the 2022 truce, with one established outlet reporting 58 dead and the government confirming more than thirty. Reporting describes a risk that Yemen's civil war reignites.

Iran is seeking to bar United States and Israeli ships from the Strait of Hormuz and to charge all other vessels a transit toll, according to NPR. No Iranian order or fee schedule has been published, and attempts to reach Iran's foreign ministry and its parliament's news agency to check the proposal's status did not resolve.

Shipowners' associations warned that transit tolls in the Strait of Hormuz would raise costs worldwide, as Iran and Oman worked on a route agreement. Iran says any reopening still depends on the United States lifting its naval blockade.

Rights groups said an Israeli strike that killed a Lebanese journalist in April was an apparent war crime, reporting that a deconfliction notice had been sent about ninety minutes before the strike. Israel has not responded publicly to the finding.

Russian strikes killed at least six people in Ukraine's Kharkiv and Sumy regions, a day after a ballistic-missile attack killed seventeen in and around Kyiv — eight of them on a railway station platform. NATO said fighter-jet scrambles have risen 250% as Russian aircraft probe alliance borders.
Lithuania warned that Russia may stage a false-flag drone attack on Baltic critical infrastructure using recovered Ukrainian drones, in order to divide NATO members over support for Kyiv.

Israeli and Lebanese delegations ended three days of talks in Rome without announcing an Israeli withdrawal timetable, with the American mediator saying that moving too quickly risked jeopardising the process and further discussions deferred to a later date.

US-backed talks on a political transition in Venezuela opened in Caracas, with the government delegation led by Jorge Rodríguez and the opposition by Dinorah Figuera. Opposition figurehead María Corina Machado was not at the table.
President Trump imposed a 15% tariff on polysilicon, the base material for solar cells and semiconductor wafers, in a measure aimed at Chinese supply dominance and taking effect in December.

Ukraine struck a Wildberries logistics centre in Yekaterinburg, roughly 2,000 kilometres from the front line, with a large fire reported. It is the second strike on the Russian e-commerce group's warehouses in four days.

A seventh consecutive night passed with no reported strikes inside Iran, and the order against Iranian refineries and power plants remained unexecuted. President Trump said the war had "got to end pretty soon" and that Iran could not "go on much longer," while expressing optimism about a Strait of Hormuz agreement.

Taiwan's defence ministry reported 10 Chinese military aircraft and 6 median-line crossings for August 7, a third consecutive daily decline from the 21 aircraft recorded on August 5. The ministry's previously missing August 4 record was retrieved and shows 6 aircraft, placing the rise into the island's annual exercises as gradual rather than abrupt.

Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan are expected to sign a joint defence agreement in Jeddah covering exercises, technology transfer, defence industry and intelligence sharing. Nothing has been signed: the Turkish and Pakistani foreign ministries and NATO's newsroom all resolved and carry no statement on it.

Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan signed a joint defence agreement in Mecca, committing each state to treat an armed attack on any one of the three as an attack on all. Turkish officials described the pact as defensive, directed at no particular actor and open to other regional countries.

The US Treasury sanctioned a Dubai-based cryptocurrency exchange and an Iran-based tether operation over a reported four-billion-dollar sanctions-evasion pipeline serving the Revolutionary Guards, on the same day the State Department published two Iran financial-pressure releases.

Ukraine's defence ministry said it intercepted 29 of 195 Russian ballistic missiles in July as air-defence shortages deepened, an interception rate near 15%. Ukrainian reporting put the overnight package at six Iskander-M ballistic missiles and 151 drones, with none of the ballistic missiles intercepted. Ukraine separately struck Russian oil refineries in Samara Oblast and Krasnodar Krai.

Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan signed a joint defence agreement in Mecca containing a mutual-defence clause, under which an armed attack on any one of the three states is to be regarded as an attack on all. Turkey's foreign ministry and NATO's newsroom have said nothing about it.

An eighth consecutive night passed with no reported strikes inside Iran, and the order against Iranian refineries and power plants remained unexecuted. Iran said the Strait of Hormuz accord is awaiting approval from its top security council, while a US official said a deal was expected soon.

Taiwan's defence ministry recorded 14 Chinese military aircraft and 11 crossings of the Taiwan Strait median line for August 8, alongside 6 navy vessels and 8 official ships. The count rose from 10 the previous day, ending a three-day decline, with median-line crossings nearly doubling.

The US Senate passed a sweeping Russian energy sanctions bill in a final-passage vote of 86 to 11 on August 7, targeting buyers of Russian energy and named as Vote 224 in the Senate's own roll-call record. The measure still requires House passage and presidential signature.

Russian missile strikes near Kyiv killed at least three people including a child and injured seven, in a further overnight attack on the capital region. Wider reporting put the night's toll across Ukraine at twelve killed and 81 injured.

Houthi attacks killed at least ten more Yemeni government personnel as the group targeted the oil-rich Marib region, days after the heaviest ground fighting since the 2022 truce. The UN warned Yemen faces a return to full-scale civil war.

Lebanon and Israel agreed on a shortlist of countries that could verify Hezbollah's disarmament, according to an official, days after the Rome talks ended without a withdrawal timetable. France was reported to have been excluded at Israeli and American insistence.

Six unidentified drones were sighted over the Mechernich military base in North Rhine-Westphalia, a Bundeswehr logistics site, days after an explosive device was found beside a Ukrainian cargo aircraft at Leipzig-Halle airport. German authorities have named no actor for either incident.

Iran issued a list of demands for reopening the Strait of Hormuz: an end to strikes in Iran, Lebanon, Yemen, Iraq and the Palestinian territories, the withdrawal of US naval and air forces, war reparations, the release of frozen assets and the lifting of sanctions. Tehran also said any agreement would not by itself reopen the waterway.

Saudi Arabia's energy ministry said a fire at the Aramco facility in Jizan had been extinguished and did not say what caused it. The Houthis separately claimed they had struck the refinery with a drone. Neither the EIA nor the IEA records any Saudi refining outage.

The United Arab Emirates says an Iranian missile struck a vessel affiliated with its state oil company ADNOC as it transited the Strait of Hormuz, with no injuries reported. The UAE foreign ministry condemned what it called a hostile Iranian attack. It is the first kinetic incident between Iran and the UAE in this war.

Ukraine's General Staff confirmed strikes on two Russian oil refineries — Ilsky in Krasnodar Krai and Syzran in Samara Oblast — and on a Black Sea drilling rig. Kyiv separately said it had struck twelve Russian shadow-fleet vessels in the Black Sea and Sea of Azov over the past week.

Taiwan's defence ministry recorded four Chinese military aircraft and two median-line crossings for 9 August, down from fourteen and eleven the day before, with six navy vessels and nine official ships. Typhoon Dolphin closed ports across the region the same day and the Han Kuang exercises run to 14 August.

President Zelensky said Russia could receive up to fifty thousand North Korean troops, well above prior estimates. No Western wire has independently confirmed the figure, which remains a Ukrainian presidential claim.

A Russian morning strike on a Kharkiv high-rise killed two men and wounded twenty-one, and a missile attack damaged residential buildings in Odesa, injuring at least eight. The child killed in Kyiv Oblast the previous night has been identified as a three-year-old boy who died alongside his grandparents.

Israel rejected the American 15-point plan for Gaza. Netanyahu told a cabinet meeting that no withdrawal would be carried out until Hamas is genuinely disarmed, and said Israel was still talking to the Americans. The White House did not immediately respond.
Oman said the Strait of Hormuz talks it mediates are progressing positively, its first public comment on the arrangement after weeks in which Iran described it repeatedly and Muscat said nothing.

A drone exploded near a gas pipeline on the Bulgarian-Romanian border. Bulgaria's defence ministry said it was most likely a decoy type widely used by Ukraine's armed forces, and Kyiv said it would open an inquiry.

Turkey's foreign minister said the Mecca defence pact identifies no common threat in writing and named Iran specifically as not its target — the first time a signatory minister has spoken on the record. Neither Ankara nor NATO has addressed how the mutual-defence clause sits alongside Article 5.
A World Health Organization warehouse holding front-line medical supplies in Dnipro was struck twice within 24 hours, destroying about $500,000 of stock. The organisation reported no casualties.

Syria's foreign ministry announced an agreement with Russia to convert the Tartous naval facility and the Hmeimim air base into joint training centres. Moscow has not publicly confirmed it, and the sourcing does not support reports that Russia is ending military use of the sites.

President Trump said the United States is “low-keying it” with Iran and only “semi-negotiating,” describing a shift from military strikes to economic pressure as Iran's economy deteriorates. He did not say strikes had been paused, and the White House public record carries no statement on it.

The reported death toll from the Ukrainian drone strike on the Taneco complex at Nizhnekamsk in Tatarstan rose to at least thirteen. Seven of the dead were Uzbek nationals working at the site, according to Uzbekistan's consulate, and a child was also among them.

UN peacekeepers in Lebanon counted 455 Israeli projectiles and 97 airspace violations over a single weekend, with 229 on Saturday alone — the highest one-day figure since 21 June — and reported two Israeli tanks firing near a UN position.

Iran appointed Mohsen Rezaei, who commanded the Revolutionary Guards from 1981 to 1997, as secretary of its Supreme National Security Council — the body Tehran says must approve any Strait of Hormuz arrangement, seven days before the memorandum's deadline.

Houthi missile and drone attacks on the government-held Yemeni port of al-Makha killed ten people, seven of them military, a day after strikes on the same port killed eleven. The Houthi military spokesman claimed both.

Ukrainian drones struck the Taneco refinery and petrochemical complex at Nizhnekamsk in Tatarstan, more than 1,200 kilometres from the border. Russian regional authorities said twelve people were killed, a figure no independent source has yet confirmed. Moscow said it intercepted 456 drones overnight.

Taiwan's defence ministry recorded one Chinese military aircraft, one median-line crossing, nine navy vessels and eleven official ships for 10 August, a second consecutive single-digit day. The Han Kuang exercises run to 14 August and Typhoon Dolphin was still closing regional ports.

No American strike inside Iran has been reported for a tenth consecutive night, as of this dashboard's 05:30 cutoff. The reported order against Iranian refineries and power plants remains unexecuted since 31 July, and the President has described the pause as a shift to economic pressure.
President Trump was moved off Air Force One and onto a smaller military aircraft while leaving Turkey after what the Washington Post described as a credible Iranian threat.
Protests over electricity shortages in the Iraqi city of Kut turned violent in temperatures near 44C, with more than fifty police reported injured and more than thirty people detained.

Germany warned that it faces “daily hybrid warfare” after an explosive-laden drone was found at Leipzig-Halle airport and further drones were sighted over a Bundeswehr base. Berlin has still named no actor for either incident.

Three days after Pakistan published the text of the Mecca mutual-defence pact, neither Turkey's foreign ministry nor NATO has said anything about it on its own website, and no statement linking the agreement to NATO's Article 5 can be found at the Turkish state news agency it was attributed to.

A drone strike set fire to a storage tank at Libya's Zawiya refinery, the country's largest operating refinery at about 120,000 barrels a day, and the National Oil Corporation warned it could declare force majeure if attacks continue. Nobody claimed the strike. A car bomb separately killed eastern Libya's military intelligence chief.

President Trump said the United States would require compensation from Iran covering roughly fifty years of damages, including the deaths of US service members, and said the Strait of Hormuz is open with the US Navy in control. Iran's Supreme National Security Council said the same day that the Strait stays closed until Washington corrects its behaviour.

A Russian ballistic-missile strike on the Zaporizhstal steel plant killed at least six workers on their way to a shelter — seven by later counts — and wounded dozens, shutting the plant; at least twelve people died across Ukraine overnight. Zelensky said the city was struck with North Korean ballistic missiles, Zircons and guided aerial bombs. (Backfilled 8 September.)

No American strike inside Iran has been reported for an eleventh consecutive night, as of this dashboard's 05:30 cutoff, and the reported order against Iranian refineries remains unexecuted since 31 July. Reporting describes the administration pivoting back to sanctions as its principal instrument.

Taiwan's defence ministry recorded two Chinese military aircraft, seven navy vessels and six official ships in the twenty-four hours to 06:00 on 11 August — a third consecutive single-digit aircraft day, during Typhoon Dolphin and with the Han Kuang exercises still running to 14 August.

Houthi forces struck the Yemeni government-held port of al-Makha a second time, killing seven — four of them military — and wounding about thirty, launched ballistic missiles at Marib, and killed two government soldiers in a drone strike in Shabwa.

Russian attacks across Ukraine killed at least four people and injured about fifty over the past day, Ukrainian officials said, after an overnight package of roughly 126 drones and a missile of which Ukraine reported 92 intercepted.

Ukraine damaged four Russian warships in a single night at Novorossiysk, the Black Sea Fleet port Russia had moved its ships to for safety — two Kalibr-carrying frigates, a small missile ship and a patrol vessel.

President Trump said the United States will “keep” the Strait of Hormuz, hardening a position that four days earlier described the waterway as merely open and under US Navy control. Iran's stance that the Strait stays closed until Washington changes its behaviour is unchanged, and the memorandum's sixty days run out the following weekend.

Israel's defence minister Israel Katz said the army is “here to stay” in security zones in Lebanon, Syria and Gaza and had been instructed to prepare for a long-term presence. The United States publicly responded that a permanent presence in south Lebanon is not consistent with the commitments made in the framework.

Oil from a grounded tanker reached Oman's mainland beaches, spreading through an Arabian Sea marine protected area that supports rare seabird and turtle habitat. Reporting describes the vessel as part of the sanctioned shadow fleet.

Members of the President's cabinet remained aboard a decoy aircraft after he left Turkey on a smaller plane, and reporting says the CIA held low confidence in the Israeli intelligence about an Iranian threat that prompted the switch.

Russian strikes hit major grain export terminals at Ukraine's Black Sea ports, and reporting describes a blockade of the ports that threatens global grain supplies. Ukraine has cut its export forecast for the coming season.

President Putin visited the Kuril Islands, seized from Japan at the end of the Second World War, in the first such visit by a Russian president. Japan summoned Russia's ambassador, and its prime minister called the visit unacceptable.

The US ambassador to Israel, Mike Huckabee, called an Israeli settler siege of an American Palestinian family's home in the West Bank village of Qusra a horrific act of terror. Israel sent additional troops to the village while the settlers remained.

The UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission recorded at least 437 civilians killed and 2,610 injured in Ukraine in July — the highest monthly death toll since May 2022, and a sharp rise over both the previous month and the same month last year.

The United Nations envoy told the Security Council that Yemen faces a more serious risk of returning to large-scale conflict than at any point since the 2022 truce, after Houthi ground offensives at Marib, al-Makha and Taiz.
The White House said more than forty countries — among them Japan, South Korea, Canada and Mexico — have helped China evade US tariffs by routing goods through third countries.
Poland detained a Russian man over an alleged Kremlin plot to assassinate a US-Ukrainian dual national in Warsaw. Prime Minister Donald Tusk called it the first attempt of its kind on NATO territory.
Iraq's government said the 30 September deadline for ending the US-led coalition's military presence is final, and officials said American forces are on track to complete the pullout by that date.

Taiwan's defence ministry recorded 18 Chinese military aircraft, 15 median-line crossings, 11 navy vessels and 3 official ships for 13 August — breaking a three-day single-digit run and posting the month's highest crossing count, still inside the Han Kuang exercise window.

No American strike inside Iran has been reported for a thirteenth consecutive night, as of this dashboard's cutoff, and the reported order against Iranian refineries remains unexecuted since 31 July. Talks are described as deadlocked with the memorandum expiring on Monday.
Paramilitary Rapid Support Forces drones attacked Sudan's capital for a second consecutive day, as the United Nations reported further attacks and displacement in Blue Nile and North Kordofan.

Germany moved to expand the powers of its intelligence services, citing constant cyberattacks from abroad, days after warning it faces daily hybrid warfare following the discovery of an explosive drone at Leipzig-Halle airport.

Ukraine's General Staff confirmed a strike on a Gazprom refinery 1,300 kilometres from the border — the Salavat complex in Bashkortostan, hit for the second time in a month — and Ukrainian drones blacked out occupied Sevastopol.
The United Kingdom defended its seizure of a shadow-fleet tanker after President Putin threatened to seize British vessels in response, framing European sanctions enforcement at sea as piracy.

Japan is weighing tighter sanctions on Russia after President Putin's visit to the Kuril Islands. Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi called the visit absolutely unacceptable and offensive to the Japanese people.

Iran demanded compensation for an oil spill that reached Qeshm Island, which reporting attributes to its own 3 August attack on the bulk carrier Minoan Pioneer. Tehran says preliminary evidence points to a different foreign vessel.
An explosion tore through an ammunition plant at Colleferro, south of Rome, that produces 155mm artillery shells for Ukraine. No casualties were reported and no cause has been established.

A replacement aircraft carrier is heading toward the Middle East after reports of deteriorating conditions aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln, deployed more than 250 days. A senator has pressed the Navy for answers on the deployment's length.
NATO fighters shot down a drone over Latvia's north-eastern Balvi region, the second such incident in two months. Latvia's defence ministry did not identify the drone by type.

The Treasury secretary said the United States will roll out an unprecedented plan for Iran's economic isolation next week, describing economic pressure and a naval blockade as a deliberate pair. It is the first time Washington has attached a timetable to what replaces the strikes that stopped a fortnight ago.
Israel's prime minister called the United Kingdom "the Islamic Republic of Britain" and joked it would be the first such state with nuclear weapons. London called the remarks completely unacceptable.

President Trump said he will declare the Strait of Hormuz "a territory of the United States," speaking at a police academy event in New York; one report noted it was unclear whether he was serious. No United States government channel carries the claim.

Russia shut the Sheskharis oil export terminal at Novorossiysk after a Ukrainian drone attack, citing threat warnings and storage capacity. It is the first reported export stoppage from the campaign against the port.

An analysis of North Korean KN-23 missiles fired at Ukraine found their miss distance fell from 500 to 1,500 metres in 2024 to 50 to 100 metres from February 2025, citing Ukraine's intelligence chief that Russian missile experts made technical modifications; the analysis attributes the gain to restored satellite navigation and disputes that Russia analysed combat telemetry. (Backfilled 8 September.)
Ukrainian drones struck the Ust-Luga oil port on the Baltic, the sixth attack on the facility this year, and a regional governor said port infrastructure in Leningrad Oblast was damaged.

North Korea's foreign ministry denounced the Ulchi Freedom Shield exercises the United States and South Korea will hold from 17 to 27 August, promising a response at a new level of deterrent. Pyongyang launched a ballistic missile on 12 August.

Taiwan's defence ministry recorded 9 Chinese military aircraft, 6 median-line crossings, 12 navy vessels and 2 official ships for 14 August — down from 18 aircraft a day earlier, on the day the Han Kuang exercise closed.

The memorandum on the Strait of Hormuz entered its final weekend with no published text, fee schedule, venue or negotiating round either government confirms attending, and a fourteenth night passed with nothing reported struck inside Iran.

The Houthis said they attacked Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery, their second such claim in a week. Saudi Arabia acknowledged a fire there on 9 August without naming a cause, and no energy institution has recorded damage or an outage.
US Central Command announced its first multinational attack drone task force in the Middle East, drawing unmanned systems from American and regional partner forces.
Five drones targeted Erbil at dawn and coalition air defences intercepted three; one fell near a hotel in the city centre and the airport closed temporarily.

Romania's defence minister said more than 100 drones were detected near Romanian territory over four days and NATO jets scrambled seven times, but did not say how many entered Romanian airspace or attribute them to Russia.
Iran's foreign minister said no decision has been taken on returning to talks with the United States, and that messages passed through Qatar and Pakistan do not amount to negotiations.

Israeli strikes killed eleven in southern Lebanon — seven at Ansar and four at Deir al-Zahrani, among them three children and two women, with 19 wounded. The Israeli military said it hit Hezbollah sites after an attack on its troops.
Ukraine reportedly struck the Savasleyka military airbase in Nizhny Novgorod Oblast, which hosts aircraft used to launch ballistic missiles, as rockets also targeted Samara.

Israel said a Hezbollah drone attack at the Ali Taher Ridge seriously wounded three of its soldiers — an officer and two soldiers of the Yahalom engineering unit — and that its strikes in southern Lebanon later that day were the response.
Taiwan's legislature passed its defence budget after a record delay of more than eight months, keeping drone-industry funding intact after an earlier proposal to cut it sharply.

Taiwan's defence ministry recorded 4 Chinese military aircraft, 3 median-line crossings, 8 navy vessels and 1 official ship for 15 August — the first reading taken after the Han Kuang exercise closed.
No American strike inside Iran has been reported for a fifteenth consecutive night, as of this dashboard's cutoff, and the reported order against Iranian refineries remains unexecuted since 31 July.
South Korea's president proposed talks with North Korea to formally end the Korean War, two days before the Ulchi Freedom Shield exercises that Pyongyang has denounced.
Russia threatened serious damage to its relations with the United States and Turkey over a weapons shipment to Ukraine — a warning aimed at a NATO member over arms transfers.

Iran said Qatar has held three of its pilots since their aircraft came down in March, in a letter to the Red Cross. Qatar's foreign ministry categorically denied detaining them, saying it recovered one pilot's remains and that Iran has not answered an April invitation to review the search.

Yemen's government said Houthi missiles and drones hit residential areas of Marib and that its forces had launched a counteroffensive, days after strikes at the port of Mokha suspended its operations.

Ukraine launched roughly 600 drones at the Moscow region overnight, damaging a Wildberries warehouse, while Russian strikes across Ukraine killed seven and injured 51, including at a steel plant at Kryvyi Rih.

Romania's defence ministry said an aerial target entered national airspace at 04:44 from the direction of Moldova, about 24 kilometres north of Galati. Its statement does not attribute the target to any state, identify it by type, or say what became of it.
Taiwan's defence ministry recorded 11 Chinese military aircraft, 7 median-line crossings, 8 navy vessels and 2 official ships for 16 August, up from four aircraft the day before.

Israel struck southern Lebanon for a second consecutive day and families were reported fleeing north, with Defence Minister Israel Katz vowing to settle scores. No toll has been reported for the second day.
Ukrainian strikes killed at least six people in Russia's Belgorod region, according to Russian regional authorities, on the same day Russian strikes across Ukraine killed seven and injured 51.

Iran's army commander-in-chief, Major General Amir Hatami, announced a reward of five billion tomans — about $30,000 — for killing or capturing an American soldier, according to Iranian state media. The announcement was framed as part of a military reorganisation ordered by the Supreme Leader.

Jared Kushner met Hamas's political leader Khalil al-Hayya in Cairo, alongside Egyptian and Qatari officials, to press Hamas disarmament and an end to its role governing Gaza. Kushner flew to Israel the following day to meet Prime Minister Netanyahu.

An Israeli tank in Gaza was hit by an explosive device, which the military called a grave breach of the truce; no soldiers were hurt. A Hamas leader travelled to Cairo for talks ahead of a visit by the American envoy.
Vladimir Putin said Russia and North Korea would continue cooperation in all sectors, in messages exchanged with Kim Jong Un marking Korean Liberation Day.

An explosion near the Zawiya power station blacked out western Libya including Tripoli, and the state electricity company said a substation had been attacked — widening a campaign that until now had struck only the refinery.

Houthi missile and drone strikes hit the Red Sea port of al-Makha and residential areas of Marib, killing four and wounding four, as Yemeni government forces and Houthis renewed fighting at Marib and Taiz.

Turkey's president called for the Strait of Hormuz to be reopened, saying continued closure serves no one's interest — a NATO member's head of state taking a public position on the waterway Washington says it already controls.

A NATO spokesperson was reported as saying the aerial target that entered Romanian airspace appears to be Russian, and Romania's defence minister as congratulating the pilots involved. Neither NATO's newsroom nor Romania's ministry was reachable to confirm either statement.

No American strike inside Iran has been reported for a sixteenth consecutive night, as of this dashboard's cutoff, as the memorandum's sixty days run out with no published text, fee schedule, venue or confirmed negotiating round.

The US-Iran memorandum's sixty days lapsed with no published text, no fee schedule, no venue and no negotiating round either government confirms attending. Neither government marked the expiry, and a federal document search returns no result mentioning the Strait of Hormuz since 1 August.

President Trump ordered the Pentagon to substantially reduce joint military exercises with South Korea, saying they are costly and send the wrong signal to North Korea. Neither the Pentagon nor South Korea's defence ministry has published confirmation that any exercise changed.
President Trump publicly welcomed the Saudi-Turkey-Pakistan defence pact signed on 7 August, calling it an important first step, while Turkey's president said Egypt could join it.

Taiwan's defence ministry recorded 1 Chinese military aircraft, 9 navy vessels and 7 official ships for 17 August, down from eleven aircraft the day before. The ministry's median-line crossing figure for the day was not retrievable. A fresh three-day run of readings below ten begins today.

No American strike inside Iran has been reported for a seventeenth consecutive night, as of this dashboard's cutoff, and the reported order against Iranian refineries remains unexecuted since 31 July.

President Trump said that if Oman gets in the way of Washington's dealings with Iran the United States would, in his words, bomb it, speaking in a Fox News interview recorded on 16 August. Oman hosts American forces and has mediated between Washington and Tehran. Iran's foreign ministry spokesman said an understanding had been reached with Muscat on the map of a transit route through the Strait of Hormuz; neither Oman nor the United States confirmed it.

A commercial vessel was struck by what a maritime authority called an unknown projectile in the Strait of Hormuz early on 18 August, about 23 nautical miles north-east of Al Khasab. The engine room was damaged and one crew casualty was reported, and the Omani coastguard assisted. No party has claimed responsibility.

Russian strikes killed at least ten people in Kharkiv overnight, and President Zelensky said Ukraine would respond. Ukraine sent hundreds of drones at the Moscow region in the same window, and Russian air defences were reported to have shot down more than 180 of them.

The IAEA's director general said several tons of natural uranium metal were found at an undisclosed Syrian site and will be placed under international safeguards. Natural uranium is unenriched, and placing it under safeguards moves the material into inspection rather than out of it.

The United States designated the International Criminal Court's president, Tomoko Akane, and senior trial lawyer Abdoulaye Seye over the court's investigations of Israeli officials. The court said the measures undermine the rule of law.

Israel struck the Abu al-Duhur airbase in Syria's Idlib province, saying it acted to prevent a Turkish deployment there. Turkey's foreign ministry published a statement on the attack and called the Israeli account a frivolous allegation. A named American envoy called the strike an unnecessary escalation, and no operational American step accompanied the words.

Russia warned the United Kingdom that it will pay and faces consequences over reports that Ukraine is using British-made drones in strikes on Russian territory. No British government source has confirmed that British drones have been used.

Iraq is investigating a drone strike on the office of the Kurdistan regional prime minister, while Iran publicly warned against what it called false-flag ploys. No party has claimed the attack and no government has attributed it.

Britain publicly answered Russia's warning that it would pay over British-made drones, with the prime minister and a minister saying the country would not be bullied and would keep supporting Kyiv. Neither statement said British-made drones have been used in strikes inside Russia.
The International Atomic Energy Agency said a drone explosion at a bus stop used by workers of the Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant killed one person and injured fifteen.
France expelled two Iranian diplomats, its foreign minister citing the detention of French nationals in Tehran.

A maritime-intelligence publisher's weekly briefs record 78 Strait of Hormuz transits for 3-9 August and 84 for the week before, counting cargo vessels over 10,000 tonnes. The publisher says its own figures undercount because of extensive dark sailing.

No American strike inside Iran has been reported for an eighteenth consecutive night, as of this dashboard's cutoff, and the reported order against Iranian refineries remains unexecuted since 31 July.

The United Arab Emirates halted all trade, commercial exchange and financial transactions with Iran, announced by the foreign ministry's director of strategic communications on the ministry's own channel. It is the first economic measure a Gulf partner has taken against Tehran independently of any American framework.

The UAE says Iran fired two missiles at it, both of which fell in the sea. Iran's foreign ministry spokesman called the allegation a false-flag operation, and no independent source has corroborated that any launch took place.

South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff announced that the Ulchi Freedom Shield exercise has been shortened by six days at Washington's request, and Defence Minister Ahn acknowledged the change to reporters. It is the first command-level confirmation after two days in which US Forces Korea, the Pentagon, Indo-Pacific Command and Seoul's own ministry published nothing at all.

Taiwan's defence ministry recorded twenty Chinese military aircraft, fifteen of them crossing the median line, plus seven navy vessels and six official ships, in ministry record 87490. The previous day's record 87447 showed five aircraft and three crossings.

Ukrainian authorities put the toll from Russian attacks at seventeen killed and fifty-three injured across the country over the past day, including a drone strike on a minibus in Kherson. Russian regional officials reported nine killed and twenty-three injured in Belgorod and one killed in Astrakhan from Ukrainian drone attacks.

A US defence official said the department had substantially reduced the Ulchi Freedom Shield exercise on the direction of the President and the Secretary of War, with some live-training events cancelled or converted to simulations. It is the first American confirmation of the change, two days after South Korea announced it; the official was not named and no US command issued a statement.

No American strike inside Iran was reported overnight, and the order against Iranian refineries remains unexecuted since 31 July. By this dashboard's running count it is the nineteenth consecutive such night, and the pause has now outlasted the agreement it accompanied by two days.

Australia summoned Israel's ambassador hours after Israel declined a criminal investigation into the killing of Australian aid worker Zomi Frankcom. It is the first formal diplomatic instrument a US ally has used against another US partner in this war.

Israel's military opened a criminal investigation into the killing of Hind Rajab and the paramedics sent to reach her, and confirmed its soldiers fired at the vehicle, reversing a standing denial. The incident dates to an earlier phase of the war; the investigation is the new development.

Russian missiles and drones struck Kyiv shortly after midnight on 20 August, killing at least fifteen people and injuring about forty, according to the mayor and the president. A children's hospital was damaged, and a later strike the same day cut hot water in two districts.
More than two hundred thousand people were newly displaced in Sudan's Kordofan region as fighting between the army and the Rapid Support Forces intensified, with thousands reaching El Obeid.

North Korea launched about ten short-range ballistic missiles from its capital region at around 5pm local time on 20 August, South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff said, each flying roughly 300 kilometres toward North Korea's eastern waters. Japan's Ministry of Defense said it had detected what may be a ballistic missile at about the same time and that the missiles appeared to fall outside Japan's exclusive economic zone. The launches came a day after the Pentagon confirmed the Ulchi Freedom Shield exercise with South Korea had been substantially reduced on the President's direction, and a day before that exercise was due to conclude. South Korea's military described it as North Korea's twelfth launch episode this year.

The United States sanctioned ten people over an alleged cash-smuggling network said to serve Iran's Quds Force and Hezbollah, announced through the State Department spokesperson's office on 20 August. Separately the same day, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told CNBC that "it is going to work in Iran, and we are going to collapse this regime," describing the campaign as the greatest coordinated economic isolation in history and warning that any party transferring money, buying oil or carrying it by sea would face enforcement. He declined to say whether China would be penalised. No country-level Iran sanctions package has been published, six days past the window the dashboard has been tracking. The state.gov release page returned an error to a direct fetch, so the designation is carried here from the department's own release feed plus two Western outlets.
Israel re-established a West Bank settlement closed more than twenty years ago, and advanced tenders for the E1 project, in the face of mounting international objection.

Taiwan's defence ministry recorded zero Chinese military aircraft around the island in the twenty-four hours to 21 August, against twenty two days earlier. Seven Chinese navy vessels were still present, the same number as before, so the air activity stopped and the naval activity did not.
President Zelensky confirmed a Ukrainian drone strike on the Lukoil refinery at Perm, roughly 1,500 kilometres from Ukraine and among the deepest targets of the campaign.

China's foreign ministry said it rejects sanctions and pressure tactics and will not change its policy toward Iran, answering the American campaign that names consequences for countries trading with Tehran. It is the first on-record refusal by a named target of that campaign.

Fuel rationing spread to Moscow and St Petersburg as Russian refiners capped purchases per customer, and Russia began importing petrol. Reporting ties the shortages directly to the Ukrainian strike campaign on refineries.

Eleven governments — Britain, France, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, Canada, Norway, Australia, New Zealand, Sweden and Belgium — signed a joint statement condemning Israel's E1 settlement project in the occupied West Bank. The statement was published on the British and French governments' own sites.
Russian strikes across Ukraine killed at least six people and injured seventy-seven, with a residential building in Sumy hit in what Ukrainian officials called deliberate targeting.

A Russian drone strike on a crowded shopping centre in Kryvyi Rih killed at least sixteen people and injured about 130. A second strike roughly thirty minutes later hit the rescue workers who had arrived for the first. The European Union's foreign policy chief called the attack terror by design.

Turkey moved to seek an Interpol red notice for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu over a Gaza flotilla case. Turkey's own foreign ministry site carries no statement about it, and there is no indication Interpol has accepted the request.

President Trump said he views the Strait of Hormuz as American territory. Direct checks of the White House actions page and the Federal Register on 22 August, both of which answered normally and one of which returned 308 unrelated documents as a control, found no United States government page carrying any such claim.

Iran called the American economic campaign economic terrorism, and a senior official said Washington's turn to it showed the military effort had failed. Tehran said it would plan to operate through the measures rather than negotiate under them.

American equity markets fell after the economic campaign against Iran was announced, with the Dow down about 1.3 per cent and the S&P 500 about 0.9 per cent. Reporting attributed the move to the announcement rather than to any battlefield event.

Eight days after it was promised, the American economic-isolation package for Iran is still not a published document. The Federal Register's interface and the White House actions page both answered normally on 21 August and carry nothing matching, and a control query returned ten unrelated orders from the same day.

Britain, Canada and Australia condemned Israel for declining a criminal investigation into the killing of World Central Kitchen aid workers in Gaza. It is the second allied instrument aimed at Israel in two days and, like the first, carries no measure with material cost.

Germany said it had identified a plot behind a weapons cache found hidden in woodland near Berlin, and named no culprit. Reporting links the cache to Russia; no German authority has made that attribution.

A maritime publisher recorded seventy-three transits of the Strait of Hormuz for the week of 10 to 16 August, down from seventy-eight the week before. The count includes all cargo vessels over ten thousand tonnes, a wider measure than this board's tanker-only chart.

The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo passed two thousand five hundred deaths, becoming the deadliest in the country's history, with the United Nations describing it as growing faster and wider.

Iran's new national security chief said neighbouring states that join the American economic campaign will be treated as enemies. It is the first time Tehran has aimed the threat at the Gulf rather than at Washington, four days after the United Arab Emirates halted trade with Iran.
Iran's president said it was time to end the war with the United States from a position of strength, a day after Tehran called the American sanctions a declaration of war on all nations.
Ukraine struck an Ozon logistics hub in Russia's Samara region, the first reported attack on that company and the second named Russian e-commerce operator hit after Wildberries.
A South Korean container ship began a trial of the Arctic route, with the operator citing Middle East conflict disruption to the Suez corridor as the reason.
Russian attacks killed at least six people and injured twenty-six across Ukraine, including a strike on the border crossing with Moldova, and ballistic missiles struck Kyiv overnight.

American tariffs of fifty percent on close to twenty billion dollars of Canadian goods took effect at midnight Eastern time after trade talks collapsed. Prime Minister Carney said Canada will impose matching tariffs from 8 September on steel, dairy, appliances, agricultural equipment, paper and electronics, and that Canada walked away because the United States asked too much and offered too little.

President Putin said Ukraine had opened a Pandora's box by striking Russian economic targets, and threatened to strike back at Ukraine's own economy. He rejected the peace proposals passed to Moscow as unacceptable, saying Russia would talk only on the basis of the realities on the ground. Neither report of the interview carries any comment from him on the Kryvyi Rih shopping-centre strike.

Iran granted permission for a number of Iraqi oil tankers to pass through the Strait of Hormuz after repeated requests from Baghdad, Iran's state news agency said. Iraq's president told a policy conference in Baghdad that Iran had facilitated the passage of some ships carrying Iraqi oil in recent days. No number of vessels and no Iranian body issuing the permission was named.

The vessel struck in the Strait of Hormuz on 18 August is still unnamed at four days. The report of the incident names no ship and states one casualty without saying whether the crew member was killed or injured, UKMTO refused access again, and no maritime trade publication carries the incident at all.

A direct check of the Federal Register found three Canada tariff proclamations dated 23 July and one Canada document published this month — a temporary suspension of those same duties. The fifty-percent rate and the twenty-billion-dollar figure reported this week appear on no page that could be opened.

Ten days after Washington declared an economic campaign to isolate Iran, a search of the federal record returned two Iran documents, neither of them the campaign, against a control query returning twenty-nine. The authority behind the ten designations announced on 20 August is still unread; Treasury and its sanctions office did not answer on four attempts.

An Iran-linked cyberattack took a small British power generator offline for four days, according to reporting first carried by the Telegraph. No United Kingdom government page confirms it, no Iranian group has been named for this operation, and the plant has not been identified.

Ukrainian drones struck a second Ozon logistics site, this one in Russia's Orenburg region, a day after hitting the company's Samara hub. Reporting of a strike on a major Russian refinery in the same overnight package does not name the refinery at any source in this board's directory.

Israeli strikes were reported overnight in southern Lebanon, near the Ali al-Taher ridge and Kfar Rouman. No casualty figure has been given. It is the first strike there reported after 16 August, the date the board's record of the previous round closes on.

This board published that Taiwan's daily air-activity figures could not be retrieved on 20, 21 and 22 August and made it a critical intelligence gap. A direct fetch today returned the records immediately, at the address the board had already recorded.

Qatar's and Jordan's state news agencies are publishing normally and carry no statement from either government on the American economic campaign against Iran. Kuwait's and Bahrain's own agencies would not open at all, so their silence cannot be read either way.

Russian attacks killed five people and injured forty-four across Ukraine over the past day. A jet-powered drone hit a passenger train in Odesa Oblast, the delivery method Ukraine has said it cannot yet reliably intercept.

Two days after a Russian drone killed at least sixteen people at a Kryvyi Rih shopping centre, no Russian authority has said anything about it. President Putin gave a long interview in between, threatening Ukraine's economy at length and never mentioning the strike.
A Russian strike damaged an American-owned food plant in Sumy Oblast, injuring workers. The outlet reporting it says this is the third attack on the same site this year.

Syrian and Israeli delegations met in Jordan under American mediation to discuss de-escalation and a revived security agreement. Syria said the talks also covered staying out of the tensions between Israel and Turkey.

Britain's prime minister arrived in Kyiv for Ukraine's Independence Day, saying he would share long-range missile component designs for assembly in Ukraine. No British government publication carries the offer yet. Six Nordic and Baltic leaders were there with him, and the European Union approved new defence loans the same day.

Taiwan's defence ministry has now recorded four consecutive daily windows with almost no Chinese military aircraft around the island — none, three, none and two, against twenty on 19 August. Chinese navy ships stayed at seven to eight throughout. The air activity stopped and the naval presence did not change.

Eleven days after Washington declared a campaign to isolate Iran economically, and a day after the Treasury secretary called it an economic D-Day, the federal record holds no sanctions office document published since 18 August — against a control query returning 469 documents. The White House actions page carries ten items and none concern Iran.

A proclamation published today suspends the additional duties on Canadian alcoholic beverages, dairy and motor vehicles — effective 12:01 a.m. eastern on 22 August, the same moment they were due to begin. The imposing proclamations authorised duties of up to fifty percent under section 338. Both the rate and the suspension are in the federal record.

South Korea disclosed that the United States has cancelled the Ssangyong amphibious exercise. The Marine Corps notified Seoul in June that force availability would be constrained by the Iran war, so the decision predates its disclosure. It follows Ulchi Freedom Shield being shortened by six days on 19 August.

The Secretary of State authorised the formal rescission of Syria's designation as a state sponsor of terrorism, at the end of a mandatory forty-five-day congressional notification period. Syria's president welcomed it publicly the same day. It lands alongside Syrian and Israeli delegations meeting in Jordan under American mediation.

The President sent a civil nuclear cooperation agreement with Saudi Arabia to Congress, starting a ninety-day review after which it takes effect unless Congress objects. The thirty-year accord would let American firms export reactor technology, and Trump has said approval is subject to Riyadh joining the Abraham Accords. Saudi Arabia says it will not normalise with Israel without a path to a Palestinian state.

Britain approved the release of classified Storm Shadow and SCALP missile technology to Ukraine, authorising the manufacturer MBDA to share component data so a production line can be established in Ukraine with French cooperation by the end of the year. The announcement came during the prime minister's first visit to Kyiv.

The Treasury secretary said Washington would mount what he called an economic D-Day against Iran, and the President said any country trading with Iran would be sanctioned. Iran's foreign minister called the threat desperate and Tehran said it would halt oil exports through the Strait if the pressure continued.

Seventy-two hours after the strike on the shopping centre in Kryvyi Rih that killed at least sixteen people, no named Russian authority has said anything about it — including the President, who used a long interview in between to threaten Ukraine's economy.

Yesterday this board published that the tariff rate on Canadian goods appeared on no page it could open. The rate is stated in the suspension proclamation the board had already found and named. This is the second day running that a claim of unfindability has failed at the source.

The declared campaign became an instrument. The State Department published two releases on 24 August implementing what it names Operation Economic Outcast, sanctioning entities, individuals and vessels tied to Iran's military activities and procurement, cyber operations and petroleum trade. Separately, a Treasury sanctions notice entered the federal record on 25 August — for designations the notice says were issued on 20 August, not for the 24 August action.

Trade talks with Canada collapsed and the President said tariffs on Canadian cars, trucks, auto parts and steel will rise to fifty percent on 1 January 2027. It is an announcement rather than a published instrument, and it comes three days after the 22 August duties were suspended at the same moment they took effect.

The Iran sanctions package names around sixty entities, individuals and vessels — including some in the United Arab Emirates, Hong Kong, China, Singapore and Switzerland — and five sectoral determinations under Executive Order 13902 covering digital assets, technology, gold, aviation and shipping. No Chinese bank has been identified among them, and the individual names have not been retrieved.

The European Commission approved about €6.1bn in defence loans to Ukraine for air defence, missiles, ammunition and radars, drawn from a wider €90bn support package. It settles the figure this board declined to publish yesterday when two research returns disputed whether the number was seven billion dollars or ninety billion euros.

A ballistic missile struck the Saudi national carrier's tanker Amzan about 63 nautical miles west of Yanbu, starting a fire aboard and sending nearby ships out of the area. Bahri confirmed the incident and said all crew were safe; the British maritime authority recorded a tanker struck by an unknown projectile. A Houthi military spokesman claimed the strike; no Saudi authority has commented.

Taiwan's defence ministry logged a fifth consecutive daily record at or near zero Chinese military aircraft around the island — record 87551 shows none, against twenty on 19 August. Naval vessels held at seven across the entire run. One instrument of pressure has been withdrawn and the other left exactly in place.

Ukraine struck the Afipsky refinery in Russia's Krasnodar Krai, forcing the plant to shut down. A Russian drone hit a residential building in central Chernihiv, injuring at least twenty people including three children, and Ukrainian drones destroyed a second MiG-29 in two days at the Millerovo airbase.

Turkey's Interpol request concerns the May 2026 Global Sumud Flotilla, was filed by its Justice Ministry, and names thirty-seven Israeli officials on charges of genocide, crimes against humanity and torture. On 21 August this board declined a claim of that shape and identified the matter as a 2010 flotilla case. The refusal was right about the evidence then available and the counter-identification was wrong.

Canada announced retaliatory tariffs on about 27.6 billion dollars of American goods, effective 8 September, and raised its duties on American steel and aluminium from twenty-five to fifty percent. It follows the collapse of trade talks and the President's plan to tax Canadian cars, trucks, parts and steel at fifty percent from January 2027.

An oil tanker was struck by a projectile in the Strait of Hormuz off Oman early on Tuesday, damaging its engine room and disabling the vessel, with the crew reported safe. The British maritime authority that reported it named no attacker. It is a different location from the 18 August vessel, north-east of Al Khasab.

A research return supplied a name, an owner nationality and a specific crew fatality for the vessel struck in the Strait of Hormuz on 18 August, sourced only to an encyclopedia entry. A direct fetch of the article the board has read since the 18th shows it says "one casualty" and names no vessel, flag or owner. It is the second fabricated identity offered for this same ship in four days.

A United Kingdom government page carries the summons of Israel's chargé d'affaires in the past tense, dated 19 August. This board published on 21 August that two UK government pages carried the statement and not the summons. The sanctions half of that report remains unsupported — the page pledges measures "in the coming weeks" and none has been imposed.

The director of the CIA made an unannounced visit to Moscow on Tuesday, the first by an American intelligence chief since 2021, tracked by public flight data from Joint Base Andrews. The United States asked Ukraine to hold off striking Moscow and northern Russian cities from Monday to Wednesday. The Kremlin denied any planned talks with American envoys.

Archbishop Paul Gallagher, the Holy See's Secretary for Relations with States, met Russian foreign minister Sergei Lavrov in Moscow on 25 August — the first in-person talks between Vatican and Russian officials in five years. Gallagher said the war must end and cannot be resolved by military means; Lavrov called the talks productive and thanked the Vatican for its balanced position while repeating Kremlin arguments about the war's root causes. The two agreed to cooperate on humanitarian questions including children affected by the war. The visit runs 24 to 28 August; Gallagher is due to meet Putin's foreign policy adviser Yuri Ushakov on 26 August and did not meet Putin.

The International Maritime Organization recorded twenty deaths across sixty-eight incidents near the Strait of Hormuz in six months of war — roughly one incident every two and a half days. It is the first institutional casualty and incident count this board has for the waterway.
Israeli forces raided an UNRWA training centre at Qalandiya in occupied East Jerusalem, injuring five Palestinians by gunfire and forcing agency staff out of the building.
Dozens of people were killed in attacks on North and South Kordofan in Sudan, according to a medical group, in assaults attributed to the Rapid Support Forces and the SPLM-North.

The Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces announced their dissolution and integration into Syria's national military, their commander Mazloum Abdi speaking from the presidential palace in Damascus. Turkey said the step would help Syrian unity.

The Treasury's sanctions office has indefinitely suspended five general licences under the Iranian sanctions regulations, effective 24 August, saying the step aligns the rules with a change in American foreign policy toward Iran. It is the first piece of the economic campaign to appear in the federal record, eleven days after it was announced. It names no company, bank or vessel.

Iran's deputy foreign minister said Tehran and Muscat have agreed a temporary shipping route through the Strait of Hormuz, about seven miles wide, whose entry and part of whose exit run through Iranian territorial waters. He added that Iran does not regard the Strait as open. In June, Oman and the International Maritime Organization announced an American-backed corridor along the Omani coast instead.

Taiwan's defence ministry logged a seventh consecutive day at or near zero Chinese military aircraft — records 87552 and 87556 both show none. The naval count, unmoved at seven throughout the run, fell to six.

Russian attacks killed at least four people and injured ninety-five across Ukraine, and a first-person-view drone struck rescue workers responding to an earlier strike in Kramatorsk — a second attack timed to hit the people sent to help.

The sixty entities designated in the 24 August Iran package became readable: about twenty Hong Kong and mainland-Chinese logistics, technology and shipping companies, Iranian ministries including intelligence and defence, and firms across Singapore, Malaysia, France, the UK, Greece and the Marshall Islands. No Chinese bank is on the list.

OFAC's sectoral determination and two new general licences were retrieved in full a day before their Federal Register publication. The determination formally extends sanctions to Iran's aviation, digital-asset, gold, shipping and technology sectors, effective 24 August. The licences reveal that the five suspended authorisations were all people-to-people channels — including personal remittances to and from Iran — now in wind-down until 8 September.

Russia's defence minister proposed a five-year military cooperation plan with North Korea running from 2027 to 2031. The first road bridge across the Tumen River between the two countries is nearly finished, with an opening targeted for early September.

Hungary designated Russia a threat to Hungary, Europe and the global order in an official gazette instruction, and stated it condemns Russian aggression and supports Ukraine's sovereignty. Peter Magyar's government, which replaced Viktor Orban after the 12 April election, had earlier lifted a two-year veto on the European Peace Facility, releasing 6.6 billion euros in Ukraine reimbursements.

Trump cited South Korea's refusal to join the American campaign against Iran, alongside cost and his relationship with Kim Jong Un, as reasons for ordering the Ulchi Freedom Shield exercise cut from eleven days to five. This board has carried the exercise reductions as a force-availability constraint; that reading is incomplete.

Four Democratic members of Congress called the Saudi civil nuclear agreement 'the starting gun for a Middle East nuclear arms race' on the day of its submission, demanding a mandatory bar on weapons-grade enrichment and the IAEA's most stringent inspection standards.

Iran and Oman issued a joint foreign-ministry statement on a temporary Strait of Hormuz corridor and said they would clear mines from the waterway. Navigation rights, jurisdiction and costs are still being negotiated. Oil fell for a third session on the day of the announcement.

The suspension of American duties on Canadian drinks, dairy and vehicles lasted three days and lapsed on 25 August with no extension published, so duties of up to fifty percent are again in force. Canada's own retaliatory tariffs on about 27.6 billion dollars of American goods take effect on 8 September.

The Treasury's sanctions office published two more Iran general licences. One winds down the operations of a named French refining company through 23 October; the other requires every remaining humanitarian, educational and personal-remittance activity to be concluded by 8 September, with any payment to a blocked person routed into a blocked account.

Taiwan's defence ministry logged an eighth consecutive day with no Chinese military aircraft detected around the island, record 87573 stating that none was found. The naval count rose to nine warships, the highest of the run.
Kyiv recorded 13 air-raid alerts in a single day on 27 August, the most since the full-scale invasion began, as a Russian drone and missile attack ran into the evening.

A research return reported that Taiwan had recorded twenty-three Chinese military aircraft, which would have reversed this board's reading of Chinese air activity around the island. The ministry record it cited says no aircraft were detected; the figure came from aggregators outside this board's source list and was not published.

Qatar's prime minister travelled to Tehran to try to restart talks between Washington and Iran, the first Gulf principal to move since Iran warned that neighbours joining the American economic campaign would be treated as enemies.

Russian drones and missiles struck Kyiv in an hours-long overnight barrage that injured at least seven, and Ukrainian strikes forced a second shutdown at Russia's second-largest gasoline producer. Ukraine had not struck Moscow or St Petersburg in the day since an American-requested pause expired.

The world's largest container shipping line suspended bookings through the Russian port of Novorossiysk after a drone attack, while continuing to serve St Petersburg. No vessel has been named, and the underlying report could not be opened directly.

Israeli forces struck across southern Lebanon and raided sites in Syria despite an American diplomatic push, hitting al-Mansouri, Sarbine, Beit Lif, Yater, Wadi Zibqin and Hula. No casualty figure was published for the strikes.

This board's Iran and Lebanon casualty figures were wrong in opposite directions. Iran's health ministry counted 3,468 dead to 10 June against the 8,200 carried here; Lebanon's counted 3,526 to 5 June against 1,650 carried here. Both ledgers have been replaced with the ministries' own totals.

An Israeli strike in southern Lebanon killed one person and wounded six, including a child and a woman. The United Nations warned the same day that risks to civilians in Lebanon are growing as military activity continues.

Russian glide bombs destroyed all generating equipment at the Kherson thermal power plant ahead of the heating season. No employees were reported hurt; residents were urged to leave as power and heating supplies came under threat.

Iran's Supreme National Security Council secretary, Mohsen Rezaei, set out five conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz: an end to the regional war, a corridor arrangement routing vessels through a middle channel, an end to the American blockade of Iranian ports, compensation for war damage, and sanctions relief. He said the United States must act first.
