Chad accused Sudan of carrying out an air strike near their shared border that killed 12 people at a fuel market. Sudan has not responded. It is the first allegation in this record of direct state-on-state military action between the two, in a war the board has carried as internal.

The United States, South Korea and Japan will hold the Freedom Edge trilateral exercise from 7 to 11 September, in waters off Jeju. The announcement cites North Korean pressure on Washington as the reason, without specifying what that pressure consists of. It is the first trilateral exercise announced since the Ulchi Freedom Shield drill was cut from eleven days to five.

Taiwan's defence ministry recorded no Chinese military aircraft around the island for a ninth consecutive day, in record 87621 covering 27 to 28 August. The naval count fell back to seven warships from nine the day before.

Traffic through the Strait of Hormuz averaged about five vessels a day between 15 July and 23 August, against roughly 100 a day before the war — a fall of about 95 percent, with crude shipments at 2.2 million barrels a day. The figure comes from the tracking firm Kpler and is a floor: the same report says remaining vessels sail under naval escort or with their transponders switched off.

Ukrainian drones targeted Moscow and struck the Slavneft-YANOS refinery at Yaroslavl overnight, setting at least two fires on the plant. Moscow's mayor said air defences destroyed two drones heading for the capital. Casualty reports for the Yaroslavl region conflict: one outlet reports one killed and 27 injured, while the regional governor reported none.

The State Department published a sanctions action naming a Bank Melli manager in Dubai and a Hong Kong trading company, together with a proposed rule to cut the Egyptian bank Banque Misr off from correspondent banking in the United Arab Emirates.
Israeli aircraft killed three Palestinians in Jenin, the first Israeli air strike in the occupied West Bank since February 2025. The military named one of the dead as a Hamas commander in the city.

Trump announced what he called the biggest oil deal in world history, saying the United States would take control of 65 billion barrels of Venezuelan reserves at no cost to taxpayers, under an agreement with interim president Delcy Rodríguez. No instrument has reached the federal record: a Federal Register query for Venezuela covering 27 to 29 August returned nothing, and the White House's own news index carried no item on it.

The International Maritime Organization said at least 70 attacks on international shipping near the Strait of Hormuz have been verified and 19 seafarers killed, and that up to 400 ships carrying about 6,000 seafarers have been unable to depart safely since the war began. It is the first institutional count of the trapped shipping population.
The Board of Peace's high representative, Nikolay Mladenov, warned that the Gaza ceasefire risks collapse unless both sides follow the roadmap, and said Gaza could be gone for good.

Trump said "there is no problem" when asked about the threat of a Russian attack on NATO, days after the CIA director's unannounced Moscow visit. No readout of the Moscow meeting has been published by either government.
Israel is weighing expelling British officials from the American-led Gaza civil-military coordination centre amid a row over settlements. Britain said its removal would undermine the peace effort.

The Treasury published a further sanctions notice, Federal Register document 2026-17613, dated 28 August and recording an action taken on 24 August. It states no expiry, making it the fifth Iran-related instrument in five days.

A research pass reported that no strike on Moscow was confirmed, after its own fetch returned an unrelated 6 August article. A direct fetch of the outlet's index found the story and a second carrier, with Moscow's mayor on the record. The finding was reversed before publication.
Russia has destroyed about 90 percent of Ukraine's modern commercial storage capacity, according to Ukrainian reporting, reshaping how retail goods move through the country.

Trump signed an order renaming Lake Ontario "Lake America" as the trade dispute with Canada escalated; Canada's prime minister pushed back. A Federal Register query covering 26 to 28 August returned two presidential documents and no such order, so it has not yet reached the official record.
Sudan's foreign ministry rejected Chad's accusation that it carried out a cross-border air strike, saying its armed forces were surprised to be held responsible without an independent investigation.

The IMO Council reaffirmed that the right of transit passage through straits used for international navigation must not be impeded or suspended. The statement makes no mention of the temporary corridor Iran says it agreed with Oman, and does not endorse any route.

The United States Justice Department narrowed its account of a Chinese state-linked hacking campaign, saying agencies including the Senate, the Federal Reserve and NASA were targeted rather than all compromised, and that the NASA intrusion did not succeed.
A fourth vessel has been hijacked off Somalia since April, with ransom demands reported up to 10 million dollars, in a resurgence attributed to naval resources drawn away by the war with Iran.

Zelensky said Ukraine had been briefed by the United States on the Moscow meetings, the first account of a channel neither government had described. “Today we received information from the American side about the meetings in Moscow that took place these past days,” he said.

The Russian strike outside Kyiv killed 38 people and injured 20, with four missing. The site was a Ukrainian military ammunition depot at Myla, hit at about 20:10 on 28 August, and it was the secondary detonations that destroyed the surrounding houses. Some 381 people, including 59 children, were evacuated.

The Israeli military said a strike on the Shuhada al-Aqsa hospital compound at Deir al-Balah killed a Hamas commander. The hospital reported three injured near a maternity warehouse; another outlet reported three killed. The claim that a commander was the target is not independently corroborated.

The Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant had been entirely without off-site power for over a week as of 29 August, running on emergency diesel generators with about ten days of fuel. It is the twenty-seventh such blackout since 2022. The IAEA was negotiating a local ceasefire to allow line repairs. The status since has not been established here.

Gunfire and explosions were reported at Niamey's airport, a military base and near the presidential palace, and Niger's national television signal was cut. Niger's military government described it as an attempted mutiny by its own soldiers and said its forces had regained control of the sites.

Ukrainian drones struck an Ozon logistics warehouse in Rostov-on-Don and other sites across Rostov Oblast, with falling debris reported to have damaged two apartment buildings in the Proletarsky district.

Taiwan's defence ministry recorded no Chinese military aircraft around the island for a tenth consecutive day, in record 87624 covering 28 to 29 August. It logged seven navy vessels and six other Chinese government vessels.

headline: Ukraine said it shot down more than 200 drones overnight as air-raid alerts across the country stretched into a third consecutive morning.

Two proposed findings failed when the sources they named were fetched. A claim that the United Arab Emirates had published its Iran trade halt on its foreign ministry's media hub, with a date and a named official, did not survive: the ministry's own index resolved and carried no such item. A headline figure of at least 27 dead outside Kyiv was declined after the outlet carrying it returned an access error twice.

Netanyahu condemned "criminal acts of violence" after settlers again raided the West Bank villages of Qusra and Jalud, seizing a home with a Palestinian family inside. Settlers also attacked an NBC News team and a Palestinian woman. No arrests were reported.

Ukrainian forces struck the Kirishi refinery in Leningrad Oblast and an airbase at Yeysk overnight, according to Ukrainian reporting. Kirishi is the fourth named Russian refinery hit in six days, after Afipsky, NORSI and Slavneft-YANOS.

Taiwan's defence ministry recorded three Chinese military aircraft around the island in record 87626, covering 29 to 30 August, ending ten consecutive days at zero. All three crossed the median line. The ministry counted eight navy vessels and five other Chinese government vessels.

Ukraine's president said the first strike at Myla hit a military ammunition depot and that regulations bar storing ammunition near homes, promising "appropriate conclusions". The prime minister called making the same mistake in the fifth year of the invasion "criminal negligence". No inquiry has been announced.
Turkish and Somali forces freed a cargo vessel hijacked by pirates off Somalia. It follows a fourth hijacking since April in a resurgence attributed to naval attention held in the Gulf.

A Federal Register query found no Venezuela document for 28 to 30 August, on a search whose control returned results, and no new Iran or Russia sanctions instrument for 29 to 30 August. The five-instruments-in-five-days run has stopped and the announced oil arrangement is still unfiled.

The International Maritime Organization, recorded on this dashboard as unreachable for four consecutive days, answered a direct fetch on the first attempt. Its figures replace a lower-confidence incident count carried here since 26 August. Oman's foreign ministry refused connection; its news agency resolved and carried nothing on the Strait.

This dashboard reported that Niger's government called the Niamey attackers terrorists, citing an article that describes an attempted mutiny by the army's own soldiers and never uses the word. The cited page was already on the record. The characterisation has been corrected.

United States Central Command says its forces bombed two Iranian Revolutionary Guard rocket launchers on Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz. It is the first reported American strike on Iranian territory in about a month, ending the pause this dashboard has been counting since late July.

Iran said it had attacked American bases in Jordan and military targets at the al-Minhad airbase in the United Arab Emirates in reply to the Larak Island strike. The Emirati defence ministry rejected the claim that al-Minhad was targeted, and no Jordanian government page could be reached to confirm or deny the Jordanian half.

The United States Treasury says the Egyptian state bank Banque Misr's Emirati branches processed about 1.8 billion dollars for 103 companies it links to Iran between January 2024 and June 2026, and that its financial-crimes bureau has proposed a rule cutting those branches off from American correspondent banking. The Emirati central bank has ordered an examination of the branches.

Russia says its Africa Corps helped Niger's government put down the mutiny at Niamey, after the junta asked for assistance. Moscow's ambassador made the statement; it is the first time in this war's record that a Russian paramilitary force has been described as operationally decisive inside a Sahel state.

A Ukrainian strike on Belgorod killed two people, including a sixteen-year-old, and injured sixteen, damaging an Ozon warehouse and a thermal power plant, Russian regional authorities said. It is the second Ozon site struck in three days and the same operator, not a third.

A supertanker was reported afire in the southern Strait after striking mines. No page retrieved for this dashboard names the vessel, its flag or its crew, the maritime authority for the waterway refused connection twice, and the shipping agency's own media centre carries nothing after 28 August. The report is recorded here as unestablished, not as a tanker.

A Federal Register query returned no Iran document published between 29 and 31 August, on a search whose control returned seven. The run of five sanctions instruments in five days has now been stopped for three days.

The International Maritime Organization's 28 August figures were verified at its own page: 70 attacks on shipping verified, 19 seafarers killed, and up to 400 ships unable to depart. The 400 counts vessels stuck inside the Gulf since the war began on 28 February, not ships avoiding the route worldwide.

Kyiv was under attack for a fifth consecutive day, with about 800 jet-powered drones launched over four days and close to 2,000 across the week. Russian attacks killed eight people and injured 41 in the previous day.

The United Nations recorded settlers cutting power and water to three Palestinian families at Qusra in the occupied West Bank and Israeli forces cordoning off the town of Taybeh. No arrests have been reported over the weekend raids Netanyahu condemned.

Libya's rival authorities agreed a two-year roadmap to elections at United Nations-led talks, covering the electoral commission and the legal framework. The National Oil Corporation has still declared no force majeure.

A Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit was reported to be opening with Russia's and China's leaders and Iran's president attending. The organisation's own site announced no such summit when it was checked yesterday, and no page could be retrieved today to settle it.

A Russian missile and drone attack on Kyiv struck a railway depot and killed at least twelve people, including six railway workers, on the sixth consecutive night of the barrage. It is the deadliest night of the current campaign against the capital.

Ukrainian drones damaged Russia's Ust-Luga port on the Baltic, the regional governor said. It extends the deep-strike campaign from refineries to a major export terminal on Russia's northwestern seaboard.

The Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit convened at Bishkek with Russia's and China's presidents and Iran's president attending. India's prime minister publicly urged Vladimir Putin to move from an endless war to an end to the war, and Iran's president offered talks with Washington.

Europe protested the United States decision to seat Russia's finance minister at the Group of Twenty finance meeting in North Carolina, his first in-person attendance since 2022. Germany's vice-chancellor confronted him at the table and called his presence irritating.

Eight people were arrested over assaults on Palestinians and mosque arsons in the West Bank, days after Israel's prime minister condemned the settler raids at Qusra and Jalud. It is the first reported enforcement action following that condemnation.
United States Army Secretary Dan Driscoll resigned after eighteen months, amid reported friction with the Defense Secretary over Army transformation and readiness.

Iran's claim that it struck American bases in Jordan was recorded here as uncorroborated because Jordan's news agency carried nothing about it. That was wrong: Jordan's military had said it intercepted eight missiles breaching the Kingdom's airspace. Corrected 2 September.

Every American military page checked for the Larak Island strike returned an access error for a second consecutive day, across eight Central Command, Defense Department, Navy and Army addresses. No United States command has published an account of the strike.

Thirteen of fourteen institutional and news endpoints that failed on the busiest day of the week failed again today, on a quieter one. The pattern is a standing closure rather than one that tightens when the news is large.

German authorities identified two suspects in the Leipzig airport drone attack — a Russian-born holder of a Latvian passport as coordinator, and a Belarusian with a Russian passport whose DNA was on the drone and explosives container — both of whom have left Germany. Berlin is also tightening entry rules for Russian nationals and seeking EU sanctions on hybrid-attack actors. Putin called the measures a grave mistake.

The United States struck Iranian air-defence installations, radar sites, anti-ship cruise-missile launchers and Jiroft airport in Kerman province around the Strait of Hormuz. Iranian officials reported civilian deaths including at a wedding in Hormozgan; carriers give differing tolls and no American command has published an account.

Jordan's armed forces said thirteen ballistic missiles entered the Kingdom's airspace, that ten were intercepted and three fell in remote areas, after Iran's Revolutionary Guard said it struck American bases there. Kuwait and Bahrain separately reported Iranian drone attacks with no injuries or damage.

Two supertankers were struck by projectiles minutes apart near Khasab inside the Strait of Hormuz: the Sidr, run by Saudi Arabia's Bahri, and the Senegal Prosperity, operated by South Korea's Sinokor. No casualties were reported and no party has claimed the attacks.

Germany formally blamed Russia for the explosive drone found at Leipzig airport in August, saying it had proof the operators worked for Russian state entities, and closed a Russian consulate and a cultural centre. NATO's Secretary-General said the evidence was clear; the EU called it state-sponsored terrorism.

Putin publicly pledged support to Iran at the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit, where leaders signed the Bishkek Declaration and the organisation issued a statement condemning military strikes on Iran and unilateral coercive measures.

A Russian overnight attack killed at least sixteen people and injured fifty-four across Ukraine, with Kyiv and Odesa worst hit, on the seventh consecutive night. Putin separately ordered preparations for massive strikes on Ukraine's energy system and dismissed mobilisation reports.

The American channel with Russia was named: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent met Finance Minister Anton Siluanov at the Group of Twenty meeting in Asheville on 31 August to discuss a twenty-eight-point peace plan. A Ukrainian official said Kyiv knew nothing of the meeting; the White House briefings page opened and carries no readout.

No negotiated limit has bound American or Russian strategic nuclear forces since 5 February 2026, when New START expired with no successor. Inspections, data declarations and telemetry exchange all lapsed with it. Russia offered to keep observing the old ceilings for a year; the United States did not respond. It is the first such gap since 1972.

A United States Central Command spokesman, Tim Hawkins, said the American military never targets civilians and that reports of the wedding deaths at Kuhestak in Hormozgan originated from Iranian state media. It is the first on-the-record American comment on the resumed strikes recorded here; no command has published an account of the strikes themselves. Iran's foreign ministry spokesman called them a catalogue of atrocities, and the Iranian Red Crescent wrote to the International Criminal Court's prosecutor. The Hormozgan governor's office named four dead, including a four-year-old boy, and more than sixty injured; the Red Crescent gave a higher toll.

Saudi Arabia's foreign ministry said Iran attacked the Bahri supertanker Sidr as it transited the Strait of Hormuz on 1 September, and that two Filipino crew members were killed. Iran's Revolutionary Guard says the tankers struck mines. Kuwait and Qatar condemned the attack. It is the first named attribution and the first reported deaths from the two tanker strikes.

Ukraine's commander-in-chief, Mykhailo Drapatyi, issued leadership guidelines pledging accountability and pushing authority down to combat-tested sergeants. This dashboard had no record that Drapatyi has held the post since 21 July 2026, replacing Oleksandr Syrskyi. The appointment decree itself has not yet been read at a primary.

Kpler recorded five, 11 and six vessels crossing the Strait of Hormuz on 31 August, 1 and 2 September, a 10-day average of 13 a day, and Lloyd's List Intelligence about 12 transits a day from 26 August to 1 September, against about 100 a day before the war.

Correction. This dashboard reported that Iran's claim of striking bases in Jordan was uncorroborated because Jordan's news agency carried nothing about it. Jordan's military had in fact said it intercepted eight missiles that breached the Kingdom's airspace at dawn on 31 August.

Zelensky warned airlines and foreign governments that Russian airspace is effectively closing as Ukrainian drone operations extend deeper into Russia. Putin called the warning an act of state terrorism.

The White House published terms of the Venezuela oil arrangement on its own site: a thirty-five percent American equity stake, twenty percent of output at production cost and first refusal on the rest, across seventeen fields. No signed instrument, executive order or licence number has been published.

The International Atomic Energy Agency said findings at the Deir Az Zor site struck by Israel in 2007 are consistent with a nuclear reactor, citing cooling infrastructure and seventy-three tonnes of natural uranium metal at an undeclared location.

Twelve Israeli prison guards were charged over the beating death of a Palestinian detainee at Ketziot prison in 2023. No charges have yet been filed against the eight arrested last week over West Bank assaults and mosque arsons.

A global government bond sell-off deepened, which reporting attributes to the renewed American strikes on Iran and the inflation risk of higher energy prices. Ryanair warned European air fares would rise next year if oil stays high.

Xi Jinping arrived in Cairo for a state visit, his first to Egypt in a decade, with defence ties and technology cooperation on the agenda. Reporting places it against an American sanctions threat over Egyptian links to Iran.

Iranian hackers targeted American water systems, telecommunications and energy infrastructure in recent weeks, four people with access to government and industry threat information said; the attempts have so far been unsuccessful, and an Iranian group warned that unexpected and critical events would soon target American infrastructure.

Iran struck Kuwait for the second time in three days and warned Washington that all-out war could return. Kuwait's army said it intercepted an incoming missile and drone attack. No casualties or damage have been reported.

The Financial Times reported that Russian specialists are helping Iran develop supersonic cruise missiles, working on the propulsion system. It is the most direct account yet of Russian material support to the state the United States is bombing.

Taiwan's defence ministry record reopened after four days unread, showing no Chinese military aircraft around the island on 3 September and one the day before. Naval presence held at five vessels with three Chinese government ships alongside.

headline: Russia said it would close Goethe-Institut cultural centres, answering Germany's closure of the Russian House in Berlin and the Russian consulate in Bonn over the Leipzig airport drone.

The Treasury's press-release index published a readout of the Treasury secretary's 30 August meeting with the Bank of Japan governor, and carries none for his 31 August meeting with Russia's finance minister. The index is current and carries that kind of item for that official.

Poland's prime minister said a fire at a drone-components plant was deliberate sabotage after a masked figure was recorded entering the site. Prosecutors opened a terrorism investigation. No state has been named.
Ukraine's military intelligence confirmed the strike on the Novatek fuel plant and port complex at Ust-Luga on the Baltic, saying a large fire destroyed key equipment.

A Russian air force general was shot by a gunman on a motorcycle near Saratov. His condition has not been established, no Ukrainian body has claimed the attack, and Ukrainian sources say he ordered a strike on a Kyiv children's hospital.

Two Palestinian teenagers were killed at a West Bank village. Accounts differ on whether settlers or Israeli soldiers fired the fatal shots, and the outlets carrying the story give different names for the dead.

A far-right Israeli minister presented a plan for the removal of the Palestinian population from Gaza, framed as voluntary emigration. It is a ministerial proposal, not government policy, and no cabinet decision has been reported.

The Iranian Red Crescent said on its own site that it had written to the International Criminal Court's prosecutor over the American strike on a wedding at Kohestak in Hormozgan province, and that it was collecting evidence.

A United Nations country page carried the first institutional casualty figure this dashboard has obtained for Iran: a UNICEF statement of 31 July reporting 386 children killed and 2,117 injured over five months. It counts children only and does not replace the wider total on the ledger.

Correction. Niger's government named the men behind the 29 August gunfire in Niamey as a military faction and called them mutineers. This dashboard recorded them as terrorists for five days; the article it cited never used the word.
Norway seized the Russian vessel Professor Molchanov at Barentsburg on Svalbard to enforce a Hague tribunal award to Ukraine's Naftogaz, on a district court decision of 31 August.
Estonia's defence minister resigned over a failed seventy-million-euro contract for artillery shells intended for Ukraine that were never delivered.

Every American military index checked returned an access error for a third consecutive day: three Central Command routes, two Defense Department routes, the Air Force, the Navy and the State Department. No account of any strike since 30 August has been readable.

The US vice president said the military is investigating whether an American strike hit a wedding in Iran, and that he is extremely sceptical of Iran's account; the military said it never targets civilians and did not confirm carrying out the strike. He gave no timeline for the war's end, tying it to Iran halting attacks on shipping.

Israel released a Lebanese civilian detainee and said four more would follow, the first such release since the June ceasefire. Israeli forces separately said they had cleared and would demolish a Hezbollah tunnel complex on the Ali Taher ridge.

Reporting on the Russian energy sanctions bill diverged: a major wire said it had stalled in the House over tariff concerns with no vote scheduled, while a Ukrainian official was quoted saying the House might fast-track it. The Senate passed it on 7 August.
Houthi forces killed thirteen Yemeni government troops in clashes along the western coast, on the axis toward the Bab el-Mandeb strait. No Saudi or Emirati ground role was reported.

Taiwan's defence ministry recorded no Chinese military aircraft around the island for a further day, with five navy vessels and five other Chinese government vessels — two more government vessels than the day before.

South Korea was reported to be preparing a naval logistics ship, maritime patrol aircraft and about 150 personnel for the Strait of Hormuz under American pressure. Seoul's presidential office said the reports differed from the facts and that nothing had been decided, adding only that it was discussing ways to help restore free navigation.

Houthi forces opened their first major ground offensive in four years on Yemen's west coast, pushing toward the port of Mokha and the heights above the Bab el-Mandeb strait and firing more than twenty-five ballistic missiles at the port. A news-agency tally put the dead at 129 across the opening days: sixty-six government troops, sixty-two Houthi fighters and one civilian.

The United States sanctioned the Turkish bank Golden Global, which the State Department called a financial lifeline moving Iranian oil revenue. The bank threatened legal action. It is the first time in this war that Washington has aimed a designation at a bank in a NATO member state.

The Treasury was reported to have issued general licences allowing BP, Shell, Chevron, Eni and Repsol to operate in Venezuela. It is the first sanctions relief this dashboard's reverse query has surfaced; the same query found nothing lifted for Russia or Iran.

Argentina's president said he would sanction oil companies drilling in Falklands waters, extending penalties to their suppliers, shareholders and directors, and repeated Argentina's claim to the islands.
Four more people were arrested over settler violence in the West Bank, including a serving Israeli army conscript. No charges have been filed against any of the eight arrested last week.
Germany set 18 September as the date for closing Russia's consulate in Bonn, following its attribution of the Leipzig airport drone to Russian state entities.
Israel handed five Lebanese civilians back to Lebanon through the Red Cross, completing the release this dashboard had reported as one detainee with four more promised.

Israel said it was cementing its foothold in southern Lebanon after seizing a ridge, with the defence minister on record. It is a claim of ground control rather than a raid, and it stands beside the June truce that both sides still describe as in force.

Trump called the war on Iran small potatoes. The Guardian reported him giving the American death toll as eighteen service members so far, the highest figure a sitting president has offered for this war, and no official cumulative total has been published against it.

Correction: the Iranian Red Crescent's own page places the wedding struck on 1 September at Sirik, not Kuhestak as this dashboard published, and names one six-year-old victim. It carries no death toll, so neither the figure of four nor the figure of five with 68 injured has an institution behind it.
The United States announced a new round of sanctions on Cuba, targeting what the State Department called the country's elites, financial channels and resource-exploitation apparatus.

China's president continued a state visit to Egypt, his first in a decade, with reporting describing an American and Chinese contest over supplying data-centre chips for Egypt's artificial-intelligence programme.
Israel's next scheduled Knesset election is 27 October 2026. This dashboard's political calendar had carried no entry for Israel at all, and now does.

American military pages could not be read for a fourth day, and no command has published an account of any strike on Iran since 30 August. The Treasury's own index is current and still carries no readout of its secretary's meeting with Russia's finance minister.

A Russian drone struck the central building of Ukraine's Security Service on Volodymyrska Street in Kyiv, across from St Sophia Cathedral. Zelensky said the drone was aimed directly at the office of the service's head and instructed him to prepare a response; Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha called it a major escalation coming during a renewed push for peace. France 24 reported five wounded in the strike; Al Jazeera reported at least twelve injured in the Friday attack on the headquarters. No Russian comment was reported.

Israeli strikes hit five places in southern and eastern Lebanon on the evening of 4 September, in the Tyre, Nabatieh and Bekaa areas, including a house at Rmadiyeh more than ten kilometres from the border. Lebanon's health ministry counted three killed and twenty-three wounded, among them two children, three women and six rescue workers. The truce with Hezbollah remains formally in force; Israel's defence minister said the army had taken the Ali al-Taher ridge and would prevent Hezbollah re-establishing itself there.

More than 120 people were killed in fighting on Yemen's west coast in the days to 4 September, by a news agency tally reported as 129: sixty-six government troops, at least sixty-two Houthi fighters and one civilian. The fighting is around the government-held port of Mokha and near Taiz, with Houthi forces reported to be seeking the hills overlooking the Bab el-Mandeb strait. It is described as their largest ground offensive in four years, after the 2022 truce collapsed in July 2026. The tolls come from an anonymous Yemeni military official, Houthi sources and medical sources.

Ukraine ordered a three-day halt to fighting as American envoys prepared to visit Moscow and Kyiv, and Kyiv's air-raid alert sounded as the pause began. Russia rejected the ceasefire and kept striking: seven people were killed and fifty-one wounded across Ukraine over the past day.

Hezbollah flew a drone at Israeli troops in southern Lebanon and the Israeli military, which said it shot the drone down without casualties, called the launch a violation of the June truce. It is the first Hezbollah fire against Israeli forces since that truce was struck. Israeli strikes on five locations killed three people and wounded twenty-three, among them two children and six rescue workers.

Global food prices reached their highest level since 2022, with the United Nations citing attacks in the Black Sea among the drivers. It is the clearest reading yet of this war reaching households outside the theaters through the price of grain rather than the price of oil.

Explosions were reported near Kharg Island, Iran's main crude export terminal, and Iranian outlets said a tanker had been hit by missiles off the island. Later the same day Central Command named the vessel: this was the strike on the tanker Downy, and this record and the Central Command record are the same incident.
At least five people were killed in an attack by a rebel group in Sudan's South Kordofan, keeping active the front that sits closest to the grain corridor this dashboard tracks.

The sanctions reverse query — this dashboard's check for measures being lifted rather than imposed — ran against live addresses for a second day. The Treasury's sanctions and press pages both opened and carried no relief for Russia, Iran or Venezuela, making this a verified negative rather than an unanswered one. The same pages carried amended Venezuela oil licences dated 2 September.

United States Central Command said it struck three Iranian crude oil tankers after the Revolutionary Guard fired ballistic missiles at two American warships. Central Command named the vessels — the M/T Downy off Kharg Island, the M/T Stark 1 near Jask and the M/T Kylo in the Gulf of Oman — and described them as part of a shadow network funding the Guard. It said an aircraft carrier and a guided-missile destroyer evaded the missiles and that no American personnel were harmed. Iranian accounts said four missiles hit a tanker about six miles from Kharg Island, the crew evacuating with no casualties reported. This answers the morning's held Kharg Island claim: an American command has now published on the record.

Russia and Ukraine each announced a pause in strikes on the other's capital around the visit of American envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner to Moscow, who met Vladimir Putin for more than three hours. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Putin had ordered a three-day halt to strikes on Kyiv beginning at midnight; President Zelensky said Ukraine would refrain from aerial strikes on Moscow through the end of 7 September, saying Ukraine was ready to observe a halt on the cities involved in the negotiating process. The two announcements were made separately rather than as a joint agreement, and Zelensky said Russian attacks across Ukraine, Kyiv among them, continued overnight regardless.

Germans voted in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt, where the far-right AfD is projected to win the most seats and could form the first far-right state government in Germany since the war. It is a state election, not a federal one, and no result had been published when this was written.

Yemen's internationally recognised government flew fifteen air strikes of its own against Houthi positions in Taiz and Hodeidah rather than relying on Saudi-led coalition air power, and its forces claimed a district on the road toward Mokha. Saudi Arabia has said nothing at all about the offensive.

Israeli strikes killed four people and wounded twenty in southern Lebanon after Hezbollah launched two drones at Israeli troops, the second attributed Hezbollah launch in two days. Lebanon's health ministry gave the toll; the Israeli military said both drones were shot down without casualties on its side.

American envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner travelled to Kyiv after more than three hours with Putin in Moscow, their first visit to Ukraine in this process. The White House said the Moscow talks covered next steps for ending the war; neither side published a document, a proposal or a date.

The United Nations humanitarian office said 1,800 families were displaced from Taiz in two days as the Houthi offensive on Yemen's west coast continued. It is the first civilian-displacement figure published for this offensive, against a fighter toll now above three hundred.

Russia's foreign minister said German accusations over the Leipzig airport drone amount to the start of a real war with Germany. Berlin attributed the drone to Russian state entities on 1 September and is closing Russia's Bonn consulate on 18 September.

Iran's parliament speaker said the period of proportionate responses is over and warned that any further American attack would meet a faster, heavier and more painful reply. It is a stated abandonment of the tit-for-tat framing both sides have used since the exchange began.

Lebanon's health ministry published a cumulative count: 4,358 killed and 12,359 wounded since 2 March, and 8,920 killed since October 2023. The figure this dashboard refused on 7 September, carried only by Chinese state media, was twelve deaths from the ministry's own.

The Revolutionary Guard claimed a second wave of attacks on three American-affiliated vessels and three oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, calling it an answer to an American naval blockade. The claim appears in one liveblog only; no Western wire, no maritime authority and no American command carries it, and it is published here unverified.

Israel's prime minister called Qatar a hostile state and spoke publicly about having bombed it. Qatar hosts the largest American air base in the region and has been mediating between Washington and Tehran alongside Oman and Pakistan.

Ukrainian drones were reported to have struck the Ryazan oil refinery and cities across Russia. One directory outlet carries it, no Russian regional authority or refinery operator has acknowledged damage, and this dashboard records it as a single-source report.

Russian attacks killed eight people and injured sixty-nine across Ukraine over the past day, inside the window both capitals had declared a pause on striking each other's capital cities. The pause was two unilateral announcements rather than an agreement, and neither government published it at an official address.

More than three hundred fighters have been killed in four days of fighting on Yemen's west coast since the Houthi offensive opened, along with some civilians, by a news agency count drawing on military officials from both the recognised government and the Houthi side. The fighting is on the port of Mokha and the Hays front, less than thirty kilometres from the Red Sea coast, and west of Taiz.

The far-right AfD took about 44 percent of the vote in Saxony-Anhalt on early results, more than doubling its last result, with the Christian Democrats on roughly 18 percent. It finished just short of half the seats in the state parliament, so no far-right state government is settled; its co-leader named the small pro-Russian BSW as a partner she would find interesting, and every other party still refuses to govern with the AfD.

The United States energy secretary said there may not be a nuclear agreement with Iran. It is the most explicit public doubt a cabinet-level American official has expressed about the nuclear track since the war began.

Russia struck the Orlivka border crossing between Ukraine and Romania for the second time in a week. The strike landed on the Ukrainian side, and no munition is reported to have reached Romanian territory.

The Kyiv leg of the American envoys' shuttle ended without a document, a proposal or a date. Zelensky said he hopes to reach agreements with Washington and is counting on European support if the war continues in winter, adding that this is how it appears at the moment. Witkoff called the discussion meaningful and substantive; a Ukrainian official called the American proposals more effective than earlier attempts.

Israel's prime minister ordered the removal of unauthorised West Bank settler outposts, reported as a response to American pressure over settler violence. It is the first concrete Israeli action in this sequence attributable to that pressure; no charges have been filed against those arrested over the earlier assaults.

What this dashboard refused to publish today: a twenty-aircraft Chinese surge around Taiwan, carried by one outlet outside this board's directory a day after the ministry's own record showed none; and an American move to refer Iran to the Security Council, whose supporting detail was dated to 2025. The Treasury's sanctions pages opened again and carried no relief for Russia, Iran or Venezuela.

Ukraine's nuclear operator said the occupied Zaporizhzhia plant has run on emergency diesel generators as everyday power since losing its last off-site line on 20 August, and was down to two generators by 5 September, cycling its cooling pumps to save fuel; the nuclear agency's chief has warned of a total blackout within days.

NATO jets were scrambled three times over the Baltic in a week, Lithuania's defence ministry said: for Russian Il-20 reconnaissance aircraft flying toward Kaliningrad without transponders on 31 August and 5 September, and for an unidentified object that entered Estonian airspace from Russia on 1 September.
Israel's prime minister said the end is near for Iran's regime and that Israel is determined to see it fall — the most explicit statement of regime change as an Israeli objective on this record.

Iran said it will declare a prohibited zone in waters outside the Strait of Hormuz within days, with vessels entering it to face penalties. The announcement came from Mohsen Rezaei rather than a naval commander, and no coordinates, entry points or start date were published.

The far-right AfD took about 43.8 percent in Saxony-Anhalt against roughly 18 percent for the Christian Democrats, short of a majority. The Christian Democrats, Social Democrats, Greens and Left all refuse to govern with it; the BSW, on about 5.3 percent, has not ruled it out. Poland's foreign minister called the result very worrying and France called it a serious moment.
Russia and North Korea opened the first road bridge across their shared border, adding a road link to the single rail crossing that has carried their wartime trade.

Taiwan's defence ministry recorded 21 Chinese military aircraft and 13 median-line crossings in the twenty-four hours to 6 September, alongside ten navy vessels and five other government ships. The count fell back to two aircraft the next day while navy vessels rose to thirteen. This dashboard had refused the same surge a day earlier because it reached it through an outlet outside its source directory.

Israeli strikes killed eleven people in southern Lebanon overnight, including two infants, at Kfar Reman and Deir Zahrani. The Israeli army had ordered the area evacuated before the strikes. It is a separate incident from the four killed on 6 September at Arab Salim, and roughly triples the toll.

The Treasury's sanctions page carries a Russia-related designation removal dated 3 September. It is the first positive result this dashboard's reverse query — the standing check for sanctions being lifted rather than imposed — has returned since the check was added.

Qatar is building a legal case for compensation from Iran over missile and drone attacks since 28 February, including strikes on Ras Laffan and Mesaieed, citing an estimated $26bn in infrastructure damage and up to $20bn a year in lost gas revenue, and invoking Security Council Resolution 2817. No forum or amount has been filed.

Ukraine's intelligence chief said units of Russia's 101st Missile Brigade, equipped with the nuclear-capable Oreshnik, are deployed in Belarus — which Zelensky said in February had drawn Belarus into the war — and that Minsk is allowing radio repeaters that help adjust Russian Shahed strikes on Ukraine. Kyiv assesses the direct threat from Belarus as low and sees no sign Minsk is preparing to enter the war.

Shipping documents traced 46 tonnes of a carbon-fibre precursor from China's Jilin Chemical Fiber Group to Alabuga-Volokno, a Rosatom subsidiary that builds attack drones — enough for about 1,300 drones by one expert estimate. The documents, gathered by a Kyiv research centre, were judged legitimate by a US congressional committee; China's embassy called it an attempt to smear and scapegoat China.

North Korean state media announced a destroyer, the Kang Kon, which it described as part of the country's nuclear response system. The capability description is Pyongyang's own and is not independently verified; an earlier launch of the vessel ended with it capsizing.

Ukraine's prosecutor general resigned over a corruption case centred on a call-centre protection scheme, a day after saying he would not go unless the president asked him to. His deputy has been detained.

Lebanon's health ministry raised the toll from Monday's Israeli strikes in the south to thirteen. Eleven were killed in one building at Kfar Rumman, among them two children and four women; a second strike on the same town killed an eighteen-year-old civil defence rescuer; one more was killed at Rihan and nine were wounded at Nabatieh, and the strike at Deir Zahrani that Israel warned of first is reported without casualties. This is the same incident as the count of eleven published earlier in the day, not a separate one.

The Lebanon casualty figure failed a sixth refresh and is now 94 days old. Lebanon's health ministry blocked both its English and — tried for the first time — its Arabic route; the UN humanitarian office also blocked; the national news agency and UNIFIL returned pages carrying no cumulative count. A higher figure circulating through Chinese state media was refused.

What this dashboard refused to publish today: the Revolutionary Guard's claim of attacks on six vessels in the Strait, carried nowhere but one liveblog after maritime and American military pages blocked for a sixth day; a Hormuz traffic figure derived from ship transponders during a period of switched-off transponders, a fourteenth day without a usable transit number; and a claim that Washington and Caracas jointly published oil-deal terms, which the Treasury and Federal Register pages actually read do not carry.

Iran described the prohibited zone's scope for the first time — from the Gulf of Oman and the Arabian Sea, through the Strait, into Gulf waters to the north — and said maps were due to be signed within days. No coordinates, entry points or start date have been published anywhere.

The United States is removing its Patriot and counter-rocket air defences from Iraq's Kurdistan Region by the end of September, and Iran-aligned Iraqi factions said they do not treat the government's 30 September weapons deadline as binding.

Oman's navy evacuated sixteen of the twenty-five crew from the Saudi tanker Sidr, which Saudi Arabia's foreign ministry said Iran struck in the Strait of Hormuz on 1 September, killing two Filipino sailors, Oman's Maritime Security Centre said.

The nuclear agency said the Assad-era Syrian reactor was configured to produce weapons-usable fissile material had it been completed, and that undeclared natural uranium was found at the site, now placed under safeguards.
Libya's government said it had dismantled the cell behind drone attacks on the country's energy sites and arrested five people, without naming them or identifying any state backing.

Iran's security chief touted an improved solid-fuel ballistic missile, the Qassem Basir, with a stated range of at least 1,200 km and a half-ton warhead, and said Tehran will act against any threat before it is carried out — a stated doctrine of preemption, delivered on state television.

Houthi forces said a Saudi air strike on the central prison at al-Hazm in al-Jawf killed seven people, including a child, and wounded seven. Saudi Arabia has not commented, no independent body has confirmed it, and the only footage is the Houthis' own — a day before Houthi missiles hit Saudi energy sites.

Israel's public broadcaster reported a 'grey line' plan for a security zone three to four kilometres inside Lebanon, with positions along it and freedom to strike, in place of the handover of villages the June framework required. It is not finalised and no political leader has approved it.

The European Commission pledged 200 million euros to Greenland over two years and proposed doubling direct aid for 2028-34, its president saying in Nuuk that Greenland's future is for Greenlanders and Denmark to decide and no one else, with Trump not having ruled out using force to take the territory.

Iraqis queued for fuel as the Hormuz disruption delayed tanker arrivals, the oil minister said: daily consumption is 33 million litres against 38 million in demand, and August exports through the Strait fell to 2.2 million barrels a day from 3.4 million before the war.

Russia resumed strikes on Kyiv after the three-day pause on capitals, killing two people and injuring sixteen. Ukraine counted 32 cruise missiles, 166 drones and at least twelve ballistic missiles across the night.

The nuclear agency told its board that inspectors have been unable to carry out on-site verification in Iran, and that more than a year has passed since it lost continuity of knowledge over uranium enriched to 60 percent. France, Germany, the United Kingdom and the United States are drafting a resolution referring the file to the Security Council — the first such referral in two decades.

Canada's counter-tariffs on about $20bn of United States goods took effect at one minute past midnight, covering more than seven hundred products at rates from 15 to 50 percent. Trump threatened to block Bombardier aircraft sales in the United States.

Houthi ballistic missiles and drones struck energy-sector facilities in four southern Saudi provinces — Abha, Khamis Mushait, Jizan and Najran — wounding 73 civilians and forcing a temporary halt to some operations, Saudi officials said. The Houthi military spokesman called it a large-scale, long-range operation.
Britain said it would ban trade with Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank, drawing public criticism from the United States ambassador, from Israel and from some British MPs.

A Russian drone crossed Moldovan and Romanian airspace and crashed inside Moldova, and NATO jets were scrambled. A separate Russian drone strike killed two people at a crossing on the Ukraine-Moldova border. Moldova's president said Russia's front line is moving west.

Twelve countries joined Britain's settlement-trade measures — Canada, Denmark, Finland, France, Iceland, Ireland, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Spain and Sweden among those named — after Israel published tenders for about 1,200 homes in the E1 area.

Trump spoke with Putin by telephone after his envoys' visits to Moscow and Kyiv, the Kremlin said: Putin set out his vision of a peace process and assured Trump that Russia has no aggressive plans toward Europe, and Trump said ending the war would open the door to restoring relations. No breakthrough; Washington is pushing for trilateral talks and Zelensky hopes to meet Trump around 20 September.

Hungary expelled ten staff of Russia's diplomatic mission for activities its foreign minister called unacceptable under the Vienna Convention, two weeks after Budapest designated Russia a threat to Europe. Russia's foreign ministry promised a harsh and painful response.

Britain imposed an import ban on settlement goods, sanctions on those expanding settlements and a refusal of arms-export licences supporting the occupation, its foreign secretary saying settler terrorism is rampant; twelve countries including France and Canada joined. Israel ordered Britain's Jerusalem consulate closed, expelled British representatives from the Gaza support centre and the Ramallah training team, and barred twelve British nationals.
Yemen's internationally recognised government launched a counteroffensive against Houthi forces and said a decision had been taken to retake Sanaa, as fighting continued on the west coast.

Iran doubled the price of petrol above a subsidised 110 litres a month, to 100,000 rials a litre, the second rise since December, and its parliament speaker urged citizens to cut consumption, citing sanctions and the American siege of Iranian ports.

Britain's air-traffic service blamed two days of flight disruption on a technical issue in its flight-processing system. Its published statement does not mention a cyber cause either way, and no British body has ruled one out on the record.

The Treasury published wind-down general licences alongside its new Iran aviation designations, and separate licences naming oil and gas operations in Venezuela. Relief and restriction are being issued in the same week, on the same pages.
Six settlers were indicted on terror charges over an arson attack on a West Bank mosque with people inside, and police arrested eight more over assaults and arsons in the South Hebron Hills.
Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin sent messages to Kim Jong Un pledging stronger ties on North Korea's founding anniversary, days after Moscow and Pyongyang opened their first road bridge.

Taiwan's defence ministry recorded eight Chinese military aircraft and eight navy vessels around the island in the day to 8 September, with four other government vessels. The aircraft count has run 21, then two, then eight across three days.
Brent rose about 2.3 percent toward $99 a barrel, its highest since 23 July, with an intraday high of $99.46 — it did not reach $100. Gold fell slightly and American equities were mixed.

What this dashboard refused to publish today: Saudi Aramco as operator of the struck facilities and a 400,000-barrel-a-day capacity figure, because the article it fetched named neither; a Strait of Hormuz transit count derived from ship transponders; and a defence-minister quotation dated tomorrow. A vessel name and death toll it also refused this morning were already on this board from 2 September — see the correction.

Correction: this dashboard said this morning that no authority had named the Saudi vessel Oman's navy assisted. The ship is the Sidr, named on this board on 2 September by Saudi Arabia's foreign ministry; Oman's Maritime Security Centre said it evacuated sixteen of the twenty-five crew after two Filipino sailors were killed. The refusal was wrong and the research return was right — the third such case in three days.

The Revolutionary Guard said it captured an advanced American unmanned submarine at the entrance to the Strait of Hormuz at dawn in what it called a complex intelligence and operational action. No American command has responded, and nothing beyond the Guard's statement supports the claim.

Qatar said it is working with partners in the region and around the world, including China, to resume talks between the United States and Iran — the same day it was reported to be building a compensation case against Iran.

The European Commission will approve on 11 September a 28.3 billion euro tranche of defence loans for Ukraine, with a 3.2 billion euro disbursement and a derogation from the 65 percent European-content rule so Kyiv can buy Patriot interceptors; Ukraine has received only 8.4 billion of the 90 billion euro loan so far because of documentation delays. Zelensky separately said Germany is ready to provide Patriot missiles.
Israel's navy chief warned Turkey and Houthi forces against threatening Israel's freedom of action at sea — naming a NATO member alongside an Iran-aligned militia in one warning.
The United States sanctioned 36 targets supporting Iran's aviation sector, including 27 Iranian airlines and third-country firms, an action carried on the Treasury's own sanctions page.

US Central Command struck five Iranian oil tankers and said it rendered them inoperable — M/T Kaviz, M/T Charminar, M/T Horizon 1 and M/T Riesco in the Gulf of Oman and M/T Derya near Kharg Island. CENTCOM said the Revolutionary Guard had tried twice over two days to hit a US warship with ballistic missiles and that the vessel evaded the attempts; American forces directed the tanker crews to abandon ship before striking. No American personnel were reported harmed. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Iran continues to try to hit US naval ships and that every time it does so it will lose tankers. The CENTCOM release itself could not be read directly — centcom.mil returned HTTP 403.

The Revolutionary Guard fired ballistic missiles at the Al Azraq base in Jordan in retaliation for the US strikes on Iranian tankers, and claimed hangars used by US fighter jets were destroyed. Jordan's armed forces said their air defences engaged twenty missiles and intercepted eighteen, with two falling in unpopulated areas and no casualties.

The Revolutionary Guard warned the crews of oil tankers in Kuwaiti and Bahraini ports to abandon their vessels immediately because they would be targeted — extending its threats from the Strait to the ports of two Gulf states that are not parties to the war.

The Pentagon said the unmanned undersea vehicle Iran says it captured had malfunctioned more than a day earlier and was an older model carrying no sensitive data. A US Navy captain called it defective; the vehicle is an Anduril Dive-LD.

Ukrainian drones struck the naval base and an oil-shipping terminal at Novorossiysk, Ukraine's General Staff said, with the president citing hits on cruise-missile carriers. The local authority said only that debris had fallen.

Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, Qatar and Egypt condemned Iran's ballistic-missile attack on Jordan. It is the first time in this war that the Gulf mediators have criticised Tehran by name over a strike on a partner state's territory.
Russian strikes killed at least twelve people and injured seventy-two across Ukraine, including six railway workers, as attacks on Kyiv continued for a second night after the pause on capitals ended.
Israel ordered Britain to close its East Jerusalem consulate within thirty days and gave British staff at the American-led Gaza coordination mission seven days to leave.
The United States will ban imports of most Canadian alcohol, some dairy goods and motorcycles from 29 September, a day after Canada's counter-tariffs on about $20bn of American goods took effect.

Brent crude closed at $101.21 a barrel on 9 September after the United States destroyed five Iranian tankers and Iran struck a base in Jordan, having traded as high as $101.71. This dashboard earlier reported no close above $100 from a mid-session reading.

Saudi Arabia was reported striking back in Yemen a day after Houthi missiles hit its southern energy sites. The corroborating detail available describes Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces at Marib and on the west coast, not confirmed Saudi air strikes. No named operation was announced.

The nuclear agency told its board that North Korea has built a new uranium enrichment facility at Yongbyon, with capacity described as about 28 centrifuge cascades, and said it violates Security Council resolutions. Construction began in 2024 and the exterior was complete by mid-2025.

The nuclear agency's board voted to refer Iran to the United Nations Security Council for breaching its non-proliferation obligations — twenty-three in favour, Russia, China and Niger against, eight abstentions. Britain, France, Germany and the United States submitted the resolution. It is the first such referral in twenty years, and Russia and China can veto any sanctions that follow.

The Revolutionary Guard claimed strikes on two US vessels, eight oil tankers and ten other ships in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf of Oman, and said its prohibited zone now covers parts of the Gulf of Oman and the Arabian Sea. It named no vessel and gave no coordinates; UKMTO said several vessels in the Gulf of Oman and the Gulf were subject to disabling fire, without saying who fired.

Pakistan's defence minister said aggression against one member of the Mecca defence pact is aggression against all three, and that an attack spilling into Saudi Arabia would make it operational. A regional diplomat said Pakistan urged Iran to rein in the Houthis; Pakistan describes the pact as defensive and limited to protecting Saudi territory.

Trump said the Iran war would not end until after the November midterm elections and, at his party's convention, warned Iran "not to get cute" over activity at the Pickaxe Mountain site, saying the United States would hit it very hard.

Ukrainian drones struck a gas facility in Russia's Yamalo-Nenets region, more than 3,000 km from the border, Ukraine's General Staff said — the deepest strike of the war. Fires were separately reported in Dagestan after a drone attack on a Caspian port.

The decree appointing Ukraine's commander-in-chief was located: Presidential Decree No. 630 of 21 July 2026, which put Mykhailo Drapatyi in place of Oleksandr Syrskyi. This board carried no record of the change for forty-nine days.

Gulf war-risk insurance is running at $10m to $14m per very large crude carrier voyage through the Strait of Hormuz, or 2.5 to 5 percent of hull value, against 0.15 to 0.25 percent before the war — a roughly tenfold rise.

What this dashboard refused to publish today: a death toll of 168 at an Iranian school, because the figure is attributed to Iranian state media and the strike happened on 28 February, not this week; an American federal advisory on attacks against water-utility controllers, because every agency page returned an access error; and a claim that Britain's air-traffic service ruled out a cyberattack, because its own statement does not mention one.
Iranian state media reported strikes on Sirik, Minab and Qeshm Island in Hormozgan province. No attacker was named and no American command has commented.

Houthi spokesmen said Saudi aircraft carried out 54 air strikes across Yemen in twelve hours and about 40 more the next day. Saudi Arabia has not commented, and no independent source has established whether Saudi or Yemeni government aircraft flew them.
The United States and Poland signed a $4 billion foreign military financing loan guarantee, bringing American support to Poland to nearly $20 billion, the State Department said.

Norway's prime minister said a drone nearly hit Volodymyr Zelensky's plane as it took off from Moldova on the way to the Norwegian king's funeral. A Ukrainian presidential source called the account exaggerated.
Netanyahu visited Israeli troops on Mount Hermon inside occupied Syrian territory, and Syria's government called the visit a blatant violation of its sovereignty.

Taiwan's defence ministry recorded eighteen Chinese military aircraft in the day to 10 September, thirteen of them crossing the median line, with eight navy vessels and one other government ship. The daily aircraft count has run 21, 2, 8, 6 and now 18.

headline: The Houthis seized the Red Sea port city of Mokha, near the Bab el-Mandeb strait, after days of fighting with Saudi-backed government forces. Yemeni government military sources confirmed the loss to Reuters, government forces and their allies relocated south to Dhubab, and presidential council head Rashad al-Alimi said developments around the port are not a purely Yemeni affair. The UN Security Council met in emergency session the same day.

A US official told Reuters that Iran's missile attack this week on Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Jordan damaged American military aircraft: one A-10 attack jet was left with a missing wing, and about eight F-15s were lightly damaged and returned to service. US forces fired roughly thirty Patriot interceptors. The official was not named.

Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman twice asked Trump by phone for US strikes on the Houthis, and Trump declined, Axios reported, citing US officials who said Washington would keep its focus on Iran and the Strait of Hormuz. Reuters said it could not verify the report.
China and Iran have used a barter arrangement to trade around US sanctions, according to a Reuters investigation citing Iranian officials, carried by The New Arab.
Russian drone and missile strikes killed at least seven people across Ukraine overnight, hitting warehouses and ports, and a drone strike on a Kyiv gas station injured four.

What this dashboard refused to publish on the morning of 10 September: a Houthi capture of Mokha, carried by one research return and no page that would open — the capture was established later that day and is published; oil-supply-loss and corridor-coordinate figures relayed only by outlets outside this board's directory; a 2025 exercise article offered as current; and an aggregator's Iranian death-toll range of 3,549 to 11,338.

UN envoy Hans Grundberg told an emergency Security Council meeting that Yemen's war has entered a new and more dangerous phase, and said more than 11,400 households had been displaced since 3 September. Yemen's government representative gave a figure of 6,145 families.
Algeria cut diplomatic ties with the United Arab Emirates and said it would close its airspace to Emirati aircraft from 12 September.
Israel's military said it destroyed a Hezbollah tunnel complex beneath the Ali al-Taher ridge in south Lebanon; the demolition registered as a magnitude-4.1 tremor.
A Russian strike on a shopping centre in Pavlohrad killed five people and injured at least 67, Ukraine's interior minister said.

Reuters reported on 10 September that Britain, Norway and the United States tracked and disrupted a Russian deep-sea exercise near Svalbard earlier this year that simulated disabling undersea cables; Norway's defence minister confirmed the joint operation.
Zelensky said Canada agreed more than $1 billion in defence assistance, including for air defence, during his visit to Canada.

The State Department announced new sanctions on networks it says support Iran's proxies in the Middle East. The release itself could not be opened, so the names and number designated are not yet established.

Houthi forces seized Perim island, also called Mayyun, in the Bab el-Mandeb strait on 11 September, a day after taking the port city of Mokha, and two Yemeni government sources told Reuters they had also reached the town of Dhubab. A local Yemeni official said government forces had withdrawn from the island before the Houthis arrived.

Vladimir Putin arrived in New Delhi for a two-day BRICS summit hosted by India, expected to be dominated by the wars in Ukraine and the Middle East. Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian is attending, and China's Xi Jinping is expected.

Saudi Arabia shut its East-West oil pipeline as a precaution after its foreign ministry said drones launched from Iraqi territory hit it in the Riyadh and Medina areas, causing injuries and damage. Riyadh said it would hold off on retaliating to give Baghdad an opportunity to act; Iraq's prime minister dismissed a military commander and ordered an investigation, and two Iraqi sources told Reuters the Shalamcheh border crossing with Iran was closed.

Houthi forces took the Hanish islands on 10 September alongside Mokha, then Perim island and Dhubab on 11 September. A Yemeni government military official told AFP they now hold Yemen's entire Red Sea coast, and government sources told Reuters the group has near control of the Bab el-Mandeb.
Gulf foreign ministers plan to meet Iran's foreign minister in Salalah, Oman, on Monday, the Financial Times reported.

UKMTO said it had received a report that projectiles hit two vessels off Oman, and Iran's Revolutionary Guard claimed action against a US Saildrone-type unmanned vessel in the Strait of Hormuz; reports differ on whether it says the craft was struck or captured. No vessel was named and no US command has commented.
Russian strikes hit two petrol stations in Kyiv during the morning rush hour on 11 September, killing two people and injuring at least four.
Ukrainian drones reportedly struck the Saratov oil refinery and an Ozon warehouse in Russia's Saratov region, where fires were reported. Neither government had confirmed damage.

What this dashboard refused to publish today: a Brent price for 10 September from a price site outside its directory; a Lebanon death toll lower than the health ministry's own; a report of a Russian fuel-shortage admission dated June, offered as new; and an aggregator's Iranian death-toll range, again. A report that Saudi crude output fell to its lowest since 1990 is held until the article can be read.

Iran's Foreign Ministry said Iran will meet Gulf states in Oman on Monday to discuss the Strait of Hormuz, describing the aim as to 'promote better understanding among the countries of the region'. Spokesman Esmail Baghaei said Iran remains committed to ensuring the security of navigation in the strait. No Omani or Gulf government confirmation was cited.

The Houthis' military spokesman, Yahya Saree, said maritime navigation remains safe for all shipping except Saudi vessels, which fall under a previously announced ban, and vowed "blockade for blockade and escalation for escalation".

Yemen's internationally recognised government launched air strikes on Houthi forces on the west coast, including on the road between Taiz and Mokha; Al Jazeera attributed the strikes to government aircraft.
The International Organization for Migration said at least 46,000 people have been displaced by fighting in south-west Yemen since early September, and that the number is rising by the hour.

Anthropic said Russian and Iranian state-linked actors used its Claude AI model between December 2025 and August 2026, including a Russian campaign against Ukrainian officials' WhatsApp accounts and government ministries. Military Times reported the company as saying Iranian actors compiled targeting material on US Navy positions, which it blocked. No government has commented.
A US official told Military Times that all American Saildrone vessels are accounted for and fully operational, rejecting Iranian claims to have captured one.
The United Arab Emirates is revising a planned artificial-intelligence data-centre campus into a more dispersed network after Iranian attacks, Reuters reported.

A passenger train derailed at Cléon in Normandy on 11 September, injuring 44 people; a police source told AFP investigators suspect sabotage after a rail fragment was found on the track. No suspect has been named.

The UN Security Council unanimously extended the partial arms embargo on Sudan's Darfur region by one month, as Russia said it would block any broadening toward the nationwide ban the United States has proposed.

Taiwan's defence ministry recorded eleven Chinese military aircraft in the day to 11 September and seven in the day to 12 September, five of them crossing the median line, with navy vessels falling from eight to six and two other government ships each day.
