headline: US officials believe Iran obtained satellite imagery from Chinese sources for its July attack on Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Jordan, where American service members were killed, the Wall Street Journal reported. Chinese officials denied the involvement of Chinese firms when US officials raised it, the report said.

Xi Jinping arrived in New Delhi as the two-day BRICS leaders' summit opened, joining Vladimir Putin and Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian; Brazil's Lula sent his foreign minister, and no declaration had been adopted.
North Korea fired several short-range ballistic missiles off its east coast, South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff said.
Russian strikes hit two cargo vessels overnight in the Black Sea port of Chornomorsk, and Russia's defence ministry said it struck steel plants in Zaporizhzhia, Dnipro and Kryvyi Rih.
A Russian strike hit a multi-storey apartment building in Odesa, injuring at least 12 people.
Fires were reported at manufacturing sites in Tolyatti and Taganrog in Russia after Ukrainian drone strikes.
The next round of Israel-Lebanon talks has been delayed from next week until October, a US official told the Times of Israel.

What this dashboard refused to publish today: a claim that Brent jumped about 8 percent in a day to $104.61 (the board's own price feed has that level, reached in daily steps of under 2 percent); a claim that Iran's September attack on Jordan killed three US troops, which attached July's deaths to this week's strike; a Hormuz figure of six tankers a day from transponder tracking; and August reports on British missile technology offered as new government confirmation.

BRICS leaders at the New Delhi summit, including Xi Jinping, Vladimir Putin and Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian, unanimously adopted a declaration urging restraint and expressing "serious concern over deliberate attacks on civilian infrastructure and peaceful nuclear facilities under full safeguards of the IAEA". The text, published by India's prime minister's office, names no state in the conflict, unlike last year's statement condemning the strikes on Iran.

Bahrain's Foreign Ministry said it will not attend the meeting Iran proposed with Gulf states in Oman on Monday on the Strait of Hormuz, or any collective meeting that includes Iran, until the two countries restore diplomatic relations. It said the strait must stay open without discrimination, fees or permits. Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman called the meeting a sign of good intentions.

Saudi civil defence said a Houthi projectile hit al-Tuwal in the Jazan region on Saturday, wounding two people and damaging a mosque, several buildings and vehicles. The Houthis said their attack targeted a Saudi military base in Sharurah, in Najran province; the two accounts name different locations.

A Russian drone struck the locomotive of a Kyiv-Warsaw passenger train about 2 km from the Polish border, shortly after a train carrying Boris Johnson, David Petraeus and Carl Bildt passed through. No one was hurt, and Poland issued air-raid alerts for border counties; nothing was reported entering Polish territory.

Trump said Zelensky "has to stop knocking out diesel fuel in Russia", blaming Ukraine's strikes for a global diesel shortage; hours earlier Ukraine's military said it had hit the TANECO refinery in Russia's Tatarstan republic.

Oman postponed the meeting of Gulf states and Iran on the Strait of Hormuz planned for Salalah on 14 September, giving no new date. Iran's foreign ministry spokesman said Saudi Arabia asked for the delay, citing events in Yemen; Oman said the aim was conditions for constructive dialogue.

US officials held direct talks with Houthi representatives at the US embassy in Muscat over the weekend of 12-13 September, with Omani help, Reuters reported citing three sources. The Houthis said they had no intention of attacking US vessels and remained committed to their 2025 ceasefire with Washington.

More than 450 Russian drones and missiles struck across Ukraine overnight, killing at least six people and injuring more than 40, with western regions hit hardest; Ukraine's air force said it intercepted 405 drones.

Trump said the United States would ultimately leave Iran "unless we decide to stay and keep the oil like Venezuela", and said he expects the war to end this year, possibly after November's midterm elections.

The EU extended by a week, to midnight on 22 September, its deadline to renew sanctions on about 2,600 Russian individuals and entities, as France and Slovakia push to delist oligarch Alisher Usmanov; Zelensky said it is "definitely not the time to shield Russian oligarchs from sanctions".

Trump posted that "Ukraine has agreed not to hit Russian Energy Targets. Russia has agreed to do, likewise!"; Zelensky said Ukraine is ready to halt its strikes only if partners ensure Russia stops hitting Ukraine's electricity, and neither Kyiv nor Moscow confirmed a deal.

The United States sanctioned VTB Bank, one of Russia's largest banks, for helping Iran evade sanctions, under an order targeting Iran's financial sector; the Treasury warned foreign banks still dealing with VTB of greater sanctions risk.

The Pentagon's inspector general told Congress that munitions use in the Iran war has caused "strategic inventory shortfalls" and exposed industrial bottlenecks, putting the operation's cost at $33.4 billion to 30 June, $22.3 billion of it munitions, and listing four F-15s and up to 30 Reaper drones destroyed. It also said Iranian strikes damaged or destroyed hundreds of buildings at US bases in eight countries and listed 18 US military dead as of 27 August.

US Air Force Secretary Troy Meink said the United States now has on-orbit "space control weapons capable of defending the Joint Force against hostile adversary action"; China's foreign ministry and the Kremlin objected.

UN-appointed investigators said there are reasonable grounds to believe US strikes on a school in Minab (more than 150 killed, about 120 of them children) and in Lamerd (22 civilians) on 28 February were war crimes; US Central Command has said it did not strike Lamerd that day. The same mission found that killings of protesters by Iran's security forces occurred on a massive scale.

The Houthis claimed an attack with dozens of ballistic missiles and drones on King Khalid Air Base at Khamis Mushait, saying it answered more than 300 Saudi air strikes in five days; Saudi Arabia did not comment, and civil defence alerts were briefly issued for the area. Yemeni government forces said they advanced in western Taiz.

Brent crude traded above $108.5 a barrel during Monday's session, up 3.7 percent, as Saudi Arabia's pipeline stayed shut and the Gulf-Iran meeting was postponed. UK 30-year borrowing costs rose to their highest since 1998, and Saudi Arabia reportedly told OPEC its August output was its lowest since 1990.

US Energy Secretary Chris Wright said about 10 million barrels of oil a day passed through the Strait of Hormuz on average over the past week, while Reuters ship-tracking data showed transits falling to single digits a day over the weekend, against a 10-day average of 14.

Austria denied entry to Iran's atomic energy chief, Mohammad Eslami, for the nuclear agency's General Conference after the United States objected to a UN sanctions exemption; Iran called it a political act.

The nuclear agency's director general told its General Conference that, apart from a June inspection at Bushehr, it has carried out no verification in Iran for more than six months and has lacked continuity of knowledge over Iran's 60 percent enriched uranium for more than a year.

The nuclear agency's chief said the Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant has lost off-site power ten times since June and its emergency diesel generators have used almost all their fuel; a local ceasefire he negotiated allowed repairs to restore a power line.

NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte said Russia's strike near the Polish border would not deter Ukraine's backers — "Our answer is to increase support" — and the EU's Kaja Kallas called it a message to the West. Poland's Donald Tusk said escalation affecting Polish territory cannot be ruled out.

EU sanctions on more than 2,600 Russian individuals and entities are due to expire on 15 September, and their renewal was held up by a dispute over whether to remove one person from the list, the Guardian reported as EU diplomats met in Brussels.

Israel's defence minister, Israel Katz, said the Ali al-Taher ridge in southern Lebanon is now part of Israel's security zone and that anyone approaching it would be killed, as Israeli fire and artillery continued in several southern towns.
Egypt rejected a Houthi request for direct talks on Red Sea shipping, fearing official contact could grant the group implicit recognition, The New Arab reported.

Sweden's left-wing opposition led by Magdalena Andersson held a three-seat majority with 95 percent of votes counted, the far-right Sweden Democrats lost ground for the first time, and parliament can vote on a prime minister from 29 September.

Taiwan's defence ministry recorded five Chinese military aircraft in the day to 13 September, three crossing the median line, and four in the day to 14 September, with navy vessels at five and then six and two other government ships each day.

headline: What this dashboard refused to publish today: a page reporting twelve killed in an Israeli strike in Lebanon, whose metadata dates it to 2024; a page dated 14 August offered as this week's meeting between Saudi Arabia's crown prince and the US Central Command chief; and a claim that a drone fell 800 metres from Poland with jets scrambled, neither established on pages that put the strike about 2 km away.
Saudi Arabia launched dozens of air strikes on western Yemen after Houthi attacks on the kingdom; the Houthis said 54 raids hit five governorates in 24 hours.

NATO fighter jets shot down a drone that flew into Lithuania from Belarus overnight into 15 September. Lithuania's defence minister, Robertas Kaunas, said an explosive device was found at the crash site near Kruonis and neutralised; Italy, whose jets downed it, said it most probably came from Russia.

The Saudi-led coalition said Houthi missile and drone attacks on Khamis Mushait, Abha and Taif wounded 13 civilians and damaged seven homes and two vehicles; its spokesman said the coalition would respond "responsibly and firmly".

Ukraine's General Staff said its forces struck Russia's Syzran oil refinery and the Atlant Aero drone plant in Taganrog overnight, a day after Trump said both sides had agreed to stop hitting energy targets; Samara's governor said more than 40 drones were shot down over the region.

Saudi Arabia said its air defences intercepted and destroyed a Houthi drone heading for Mecca on Tuesday evening, before it entered restricted airspace; coalition spokesman Turki al-Maliki called the security of the holy mosques and pilgrims a "red line". The Houthis denied targeting Mecca, and later claimed they shot down a Saudi F-15 over Marib, which has not been independently confirmed. The Organisation of Islamic Cooperation and the Arab League chief condemned the attempt.

The US Justice Department charged five alleged agents of Russian intelligence, including former intelligence colonel Yuri Khrameev and his son, over a network it says tried this summer to have a Russian dissident in the US murdered and planned attacks on infrastructure in European countries backing Ukraine. All five remain at large.

Reuters reported that three of Russia's six largest diesel refineries have halted or cut output in September after Ukrainian drone strikes: Kirishi has shut down, and NORSI and Volgograd are running at about a quarter of capacity. Leningrad region's governor introduced temporary fuel limits at filling stations until 1 October.

Denmark summoned Russia's ambassador after a Russian frigate fired two emergency flares toward a Danish military helicopter in international waters near Gedser, the Danish Armed Forces said; Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen called it "reckless action from Russia", and Russia blamed Denmark.
Suspected sabotage disrupted Dutch railway tracks at 30 locations, the operator said, including key transport routes; Dutch authorities are investigating and have not said who is responsible.
The UN humanitarian office said fighting in Yemen has displaced at least 18,000 households, about 125,000 people, since the start of September.

Oman said it was searching for two missing crew from the Panama-flagged tanker El Gaia, attacked in the Strait of Hormuz about 103 nautical miles northeast of Musandam and towed toward an Omani port after an engine-room fire; 23 crew were evacuated. Iran's Revolutionary Guards claimed it hit mines; US Central Command said an Iranian missile struck it last month and an Iranian drone hit it again recently.
Iran's security chief rejected talks with the United States, criticising "mixed signals" from Trump, who had said on 14 September that he was willing to negotiate.

Russian drones killed one man and injured eight in Kyiv, hitting two state-owned Ukrnafta gas stations, warehouses and an office building, police said; Russia launched 200 strike drones overnight, Ukraine's air force said.

Lebanon's and Israel's ambassadors to Washington were due to meet at the State Department to discuss the US-sponsored framework, with no decisions expected, Lebanese officials told The New Arab; the next formal negotiating round is set for Rome in October.

What this dashboard refused to publish today: a 7 September Lebanon death toll re-served under a 14 September "updated" stamp; an April 2026 Israel-Lebanon envoy summit offered as current; US sanctions on Chinese satellite firms offered as a new 14 September action, which no page read supports; and an Iranian civilian death range from an unvetted tracker.

The Congressional Budget Office said the Iran war has cost $38 billion and will rise by about $3 billion a month, and that it has depleted US missile-interceptor stocks. The House then voted 220-204 for a third time to end the war, with seven Republicans in favour; any measure reaching Trump is expected to be vetoed.

The US House passed the Russia sanctions bill named for the late Senator Lindsey Graham by 262 votes to 159 on 16 September, with 58 Democrats joining most Republicans, sending it to President Trump after the Senate's 86-11 vote in August. It would sanction Russian officials, companies and banks and let the president impose tariffs of up to 100% on major importers of Russian oil and gas, such as China and India.

Trump threatened the EU over its offer to make Canada its first associate member: "If I think it's at all a hostile act, I will put very serious tariffs or stop trading with Europe on many things," he told reporters, calling the proposal "laughable". France's Europe minister said the United States has no veto over European choices.

Taiwan's defence ministry recorded 15 Chinese military aircraft in the day to 16 September, 12 crossing the median line, with 8 navy vessels and 2 official ships, up from 8 aircraft, 7 crossing, and 7 navy vessels the day before.

headline: Poland scrambled fighter jets and suspended flights at Lublin and Rzeszow airports for about 40 minutes as Russian drones attacked western Ukraine, its armed forces' operational command said; nothing was reported entering Polish airspace.

A Russian drone hit a passenger bus in the Nikopol district of Dnipropetrovsk Oblast on the morning of 16 September, killing five people and injuring at least seven, Governor Oleksandr Hanzha said. Russian attacks killed at least nine and injured 36 across Ukraine over the past day; the air force said Russia launched 80 drones overnight and 63 were shot down.

Pakistani and Turkish ministers said Saudi Arabia has not requested support under their joint defence pact, which they describe as not yet fully operational, after Riyadh said it destroyed a Houthi drone heading for Mecca. The Houthis said Saudi warplanes carried out as many as 450 air strikes in Yemen this week.

Belarus freed 25 political prisoners, and a Trump envoy said the United States lifted sanctions on two Belarusian companies, paint maker Lakokraska and forestry group Bellesbumprom, in return. No matching action had appeared on the Treasury sanctions office's recent-actions page when it was checked.

Iran's foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, was due in Beijing to meet Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi, his second visit of the war, ahead of a planned Trump-Xi meeting in Washington later in September.

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen invited Canada to become the EU's first "associate member", with Prime Minister Mark Carney in the chamber, as Canada seeks to reduce its dependence on US trade.
A war-damaged residential building collapsed in Gaza City, killing at least 20 people, including children, with dozens more missing under the rubble, rescuers said.

The Trump administration plans a $2.8 billion sale of 2,000-pound bombs to Israel, Al Jazeera reported, as Vice President JD Vance said US Middle East policy cannot be "subservient to Israel". Gregory Meeks, the top Democrat on the House foreign affairs committee, said he "will not clear this sale at this time", citing insufficient assurances on civilian protection.

What this dashboard refused to publish today: an F-35 among US aircraft losses, which the report's own relay does not list; a 2.3-point inflation effect for the war, where the budget office's figure read was 0.5 points; seven Chinese government ships around Taiwan, which counted navy vessels; and a Brent settlement from an unvetted price site.

The Houthis said they targeted the Khamis Mushait air base and an oil facility in the Saudi Red Sea port of Yanbu after 40 Saudi air strikes in 24 hours, and released video of wreckage bearing Saudi insignia they say is the F-15 they claim to have downed. Saudi Arabia has not commented.

Central Command spokesman Captain Tim Hawkins said the Strait of Hormuz is open, that US forces have helped move more than 900 million barrels of crude through it since early May, and that they have redirected more than 100 ships trying to breach the blockade of Iranian ports. The US and Iran continue to make competing claims about who controls the strait.

Trump said "hopefully we are towards the end of the war" with Iran and that the Iranians "want to make a deal", and said he had spoken with Iranians directly. No Iranian official has confirmed any contact, and Reuters reports no negotiations have been held since the June interim agreement collapsed.

The FBI and US Coast Guard said they boarded two foreign-flagged, US-bound oil tankers in the Gulf of Mexico after their networks were breached on 21 and 24 August; they reported no operational disruption and named no culprit.

Saudi Arabia has asked France, Pakistan, Egypt and the United Kingdom to deploy air-defence support as it runs low on missile interceptors, two officials told the Associated Press. Reuters reported that President Trump has so far rebuffed Saudi pleas for US military support against the Houthis.

Wreckage from a Houthi drone shot down over Taif killed a Yemeni resident and injured two people, one critically, Saudi civil defence said — the first reported death in Saudi Arabia in the current escalation. Jordan, Kuwait, Bahrain, the Arab League and the EU condemned the attack.

The US State Department approved a possible $24.3 billion sale to Saudi Arabia of 48 F-35 fighter jets with engines and support equipment; the sale still requires congressional approval. Saudi Arabia's embassy welcomed it as a sign of the strategic partnership.

Slovakia's Prime Minister Robert Fico said he does not want Slovakia to be part of an armed conflict "because of some Article 5", NATO's mutual-defence clause, while saying Slovakia values its membership; he called the Russia-Ukraine war "out of control".

Taiwan's defence ministry said 19 Chinese military aircraft detected from 08:45 on 17 September, 15 of them crossing the median line, harassed the island together with navy ships "under the pretext" of what Beijing calls a "joint combat readiness patrol"; they fall within the ministry's count of 28 aircraft for the day to 18 September.

headline: Russia launched 157 drones and 10 cruise missiles overnight into 17 September, mainly at Kyiv, Zaporizhzhia and Odesa regions, Ukraine's air force said, downing 124 drones and 7 missiles. Kyiv's mayor said 20 people, including two children, were injured in the capital.
Ukraine said a Russian strike hit a Tanzanian-flagged civilian ship in the Black Sea, killing its captain.

Taiwan's defence ministry recorded 19 Chinese military aircraft in the day to 17 September, 17 of them crossing the median line, with 8 navy vessels and 2 official ships — the third daily rise in a row, from 4 aircraft on 14 September.

headline: What this dashboard refused to publish today: a US vice-president's quote on Houthi talks, attributed to a Reuters page that does not contain it; an Iran war death toll from a non-news tracking site; a Hormuz transit figure that traced to a 3 September article; a 24 September Trump-Xi date on no government page; and a Saudi capacity figure a research agent calculated.

India warned that new US tariffs over its purchases of Russian oil could affect relations, after the House passed a sanctions bill allowing tariffs of up to 100% on major buyers of Russian oil and gas.

Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they struck and detained the Togo-flagged oil tanker Trend, which they said caught fire during an "illegal passage" through the Strait of Hormuz, Iranian state media reported. UKMTO reported a security incident 16 nautical miles north-east of Khasab, Oman, the same day but did not name the vessel.

Russia and China vetoed a US-backed UN Security Council resolution that would have extended the mandate for independent experts to monitor the sanctions on Iran reinstated in September 2025. Eleven members voted in favour; Pakistan and Somalia abstained. Russia called the snapback illegal; Iran thanked Moscow and Beijing.

Trump told Axios, in an interview published 17 September, that he has a "big decision" coming on Iran: "Do I want to go in and annihilate them or do I not? It's a big decision. Anything could happen with me." He gave no timing, a day after saying he hoped the war was near its end.

Italy's defence minister Guido Crosetto said the navy has been told to prepare a possible operation to protect Italian ships through the Bab al-Mandab strait without waiting for the EU's Aspides mission; no deployment has been decided, and any would need government and parliament approval.

Sweden's Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson resigned after the final count gave the centre-left opposition 176 seats, a three-seat majority; Social Democrat leader Magdalena Andersson has invited the Left, Centre and Green parties to coalition talks expected to take weeks.

Putin signed a decree placing the Russian assets of Nestlé, Auchan and three other foreign companies under the temporary management of a Russian company, according to Russian media cited by the Kyiv Independent.

Satellite images from 13 September cited by the Institute for Science and International Security show Iran rapidly rebuilding the Taleghan 2 facility at the Parchin military complex, bombed by Israel in October 2024 and again in March, with a tarp erected over the destroyed site, the Times of Israel reported.

The State Department said the United States designated two entities and three individuals in a digital-currency network it says gave Iran's regime, including its central bank, a gateway to the global financial system, among them the BitBank platform tied to financier Babak Zanjani.

Taiwan's defence ministry recorded 28 Chinese military aircraft around the island in the day to 18 September, 24 of them crossing the median line, with 7 navy vessels and 2 official ships — the fourth daily rise in a row, from 4 aircraft on 14 September.

headline: The UK Maritime Trade Operations agency said on 18 September that a tanker had been hit by an unknown projectile in the Strait of Hormuz, causing a fire that was put out; the crew were reported safe. It did not name the ship, and it is not clear whether this is the tanker Iran's Revolutionary Guards say they struck on 17 September.

South Korea's President Lee Jae Myung said three times that Seoul will not send troops to the Strait of Hormuz, despite growing US pressure: "There will be no engagement or involvement in war." He said South Korea would carry out only the minimum activity needed to protect its own ships.

President Trump signed the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 into law on 18 September. It lets the president impose tariffs of up to 100% on the five largest buyers of Russian oil and natural gas, sanctions Putin, Russian officials, oligarchs and banks, and extends US sanctions on Iran's energy and weapons sectors. China and India, the largest buyers of Russian crude, are most exposed.

The US, Denmark and Greenland announced a defence pact covering US military bases, troops and security operations in Greenland, to be signed at the UN General Assembly next week subject to approval by the Danish and Greenlandic parliaments. Trump said it guarantees the US will "FOREVER" be able to do what is necessary in Greenland; Denmark's Mette Frederiksen said it recognises the kingdom's sovereignty and Greenlanders' right to self-determination.

The Philippines said a China Coast Guard ship rammed one of its fisheries vessels near a shoal in the Spratly Islands on 18 September; China's coast guard said the Philippine boat bore full responsibility.

What this dashboard refused to publish today: a claim that Saudi Arabia restored half the East-West pipeline's capacity, seen only in a search summary; a report of two missing F-15 crew from an outlet outside its directory; and an Iran war death breakdown from a tracker this board has not vetted.

The White House rejected the UN fact-finding mission's finding that US strikes on a Minab school and in Lamerd were likely war crimes; deputy press secretary Anna Kelly told Al Jazeera the UN Human Rights Council has been "spouting unserious nonsense for decades" and that "the only party in this conflict that has committed war crimes is the Iranian regime".

The Washington Post reported, citing six US officials, that at least 22 US service members have died in the Iran war, four more than the 18 in the Pentagon's public database; Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth called the report a lie.

US Central Command told lawmakers the Iran war had cost the US military $43.6 billion as of 3 September, with munitions at $28.1 billion, up from $21.7 billion in the budget office's count to 1 August.

Luxembourg's Findel airport halted flights on 18 September after unauthorised drones were detected around and over it, diverting an incoming London flight to Liège; operations resumed early on 19 September and authorities have not identified the drones' origin.

Saudi civil defence issued its first air-raid alerts for Riyadh since the Houthi war escalated, and for al-Kharj and other regions, overnight on 18-19 September; AFP and Reuters journalists heard two explosions before an all-clear about half an hour later. Saudi Arabia has not said where the threat came from.

Taiwan's defence ministry recorded 20 Chinese military aircraft around the island in the day to 19 September, 13 of them crossing the median line, with 11 navy vessels — the highest naval count this month — and 3 official ships.

sources.name: Republic of China Ministry of National Defense

headline: Saudi-led coalition spokesman Major-General Turki al-Maliki said air defences intercepted a Houthi ballistic missile fired at Riyadh at dawn on 19 September, and that Bisha, Taif, Farasan and Yanbu were also targeted. Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said the group attacked with cruise and ballistic missiles and drones, naming sites in Riyadh and Aramco facilities. Saudi authorities reported no casualties or damage in Riyadh. This attributes the capital's first air-raid alerts, which were unsourced at the morning update.

Turkey's banking regulator revoked the licence of Iranian Bank Mellat's Istanbul branch, citing risks to depositors and financial stability, in a decision published in the Official Gazette on 19 September; it did not cite US sanctions.

The Pentagon is weighing options to reduce US troops and military assets in Europe in a review begun in June, NBC News reported, citing security sources, with commanders expected to submit plans to Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth in the coming days; Hegseth has called allies' refusal of base access for the Iran war "shameful".

Russian attacks killed 11 people and injured at least 64 across Ukraine over the past day, regional authorities said; a glide bomb hit an apartment block in Sumy and a drone double-tap strike killed four in Balakliia. Ukraine's air force said it downed 138 of 174 drones.

Iran's interior ministry spokesman said international mediation to return to the Islamabad agreement with the United States is continuing and that Iran wants the other side to honour its commitments; no US response was reported.
North Korea rejected a resolution by the UN nuclear watchdog, accusing the agency of "double standards" and saying its nuclear status is "irreversible".

What this dashboard refused to publish today: a 24 September Trump-Xi date presented as confirmed on the strength of a July article, when no government has published a date; a duplicate Riyadh account from an outlet outside this board's directory; and a Saudi F-15 tail number from an enthusiast site.

Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, told Al Jazeera that Tehran has conveyed to Washington through Qatar its conditions for ending the war: an end to the war on all fronts, the release of frozen funds and an end to the naval blockade. He said Iran is awaiting Trump's response and that a new US strike is “very much on the cards”. No US response was reported.

Turkey's foreign minister said Turkey backs Saudi security and could help meet Saudi military needs under the Mecca joint defence agreement. It is an offer of capability, not an announced deployment, and no Turkish forces or systems have been committed.

Ukraine attacked the Moscow region with hundreds of drones on the final day of Russia's parliamentary election, killing at least two people; Russian officials said the Moscow Oil Refinery at Kapotnya and a logistics park at Sofyino were struck and that drones reached 16 regions. President Zelensky said Ukraine had hit one of Russia's key oil-industry facilities.

The European Union's listings on roughly 2,600 Russians are running on a seven-day technical extension that expires on 22 September, after member states failed to agree a six-month renewal. France and Slovakia are withholding agreement to secure the removal of Alisher Usmanov, and unanimity is required.

Iran's central military command said it had information that the United States is preparing to resume strikes and warned that states allowing US use of their territory would be considered complicit. Trump told Fox News he is in a 'deciding mode', weighing military action, economic pressure or a deal, and said he would be open to meeting Iran's president at the UN.

Iranian lawmakers submitted a bill with triple urgency to withdraw Iran from the nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty; it needs the parliament speaker's approval to reach the floor. Security chief Mohsen Rezaei said Iran has not decided and that any decision depends on Washington's behaviour.

Xi Jinping will meet President Trump at the White House on Thursday 24 September, the first state visit by a Chinese leader in eleven years. Treasury Secretary Bessent and trade representative Greer met Vice Premier He Lifeng in New York on 20 September ahead of the visit, on the trade truce, rare earths and AI.

Taiwan's defence ministry recorded 5 Chinese military aircraft, all crossing the median line, 11 navy ships and 6 other government ships in the day to 20 September — the month's highest count of government ships. This dashboard earlier said no 20 September record had been published; that was wrong.

headline: Russia's three-day State Duma election closed, including voting in occupied Ukrainian territory, with no official result announced. Russian officials said voting systems came under cyberattack and blamed Ukraine without publishing evidence.

Iran's parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said the Strait of Hormuz will remain closed until Iran's conditions are met, restating through a more senior office the terms Tehran sent Washington via Qatar. Ships are still transiting in single-digit daily numbers, so this dashboard's Strait status stays CONTESTED rather than closed.

The US embassy in Israel issued a security alert over escalating Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, warning of possible flight disruption. No new attack on Riyadh was reported on 20 September; the day's coverage is aftermath of the 19 September dawn strike.

Two German states, Berlin and Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, held elections, with polls open through the day and no results at this update. Commentary framed the votes as a test of Chancellor Friedrich Merz's standing; both are state contests and neither changes the federal government.

What this dashboard refused to publish today: a Trump-Xi meeting called confirmed for 24 September on the strength of a July article about what Trump expected; an attribution of the Dutch rail sabotage to a domestic farmers' group, carried by a single site outside this board's directory, which would have corrected a framing the board already publishes; and a claim that North Korea has fired about 150 ballistic missiles at Ukraine, which no wire corroborated.

Exit polls in Germany's Berlin and Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania state elections put the far-right AfD first in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania at about 37% and the Linke first in Berlin, with Chancellor Friedrich Merz's CDU falling below the 5% threshold in the north-eastern state. Merz called the outcome a disaster and said he would stay in office and press on with reforms.

Voting closed in Russia's three-day State Duma election with turnout reported at 56.66%. Partial official returns from the Central Election Commission put United Russia at about 57.5%, with the Communists, LDPR, New People and Just Russia trailing; the first full official results are expected Monday. Deputy chairman Dmitry Medvedev said the party had performed with dignity.

North Korea fired two short-range ballistic missiles from the Wonsan area about three hours apart, flying about 450 km and more than 600 km into the sea, and said it would bolster its nuclear deterrent against US 'hostilities'.
President Zelensky said he and Trump agreed in a phone call to meet in New York during the UN General Assembly this week, in talks he said 'could change a lot'.

Warehouses operated by the logistics firm Sovremennye Skladskie Tekhnologii at Sofyino in the Ramensky district were among the sites hit in Ukraine's 20 September drone attack on the Moscow region, with a large fire reported.
Taiwan's defence ministry recorded 4 Chinese military aircraft, 3 crossing the median line, 7 navy ships and 4 other government ships in the day to 21 September.

headline: Russia's election commission put United Russia at 57.8% of the party-list vote with 83.5% of precincts counted, leading in 208 of 225 single-member districts; five parties are on course to enter the Duma. Ukraine rejects voting held in occupied territory.

Shipping data cited by Al Jazeera showed 12 commodity vessels crossed the Strait of Hormuz over the weekend, down from 35 the previous weekend. Qatar said mediators are exchanging proposals between Tehran and Washington, and Foreign Minister Araghchi left for New York via Doha.

What this dashboard refused to publish today: a 24 September date for the Zelensky–Trump meeting, carried only by an outlet outside this board's directory; a list of damaged units at the Kapotnya refinery from a non-directory outlet; and a research return treating the 17 September Taif death as a new one.

EU governments renewed sanctions listings on about 2,600 Russian individuals and entities for three years — the first renewal beyond six months — after agreeing to remove billionaires Alisher Usmanov and Mikhail Fridman. Latvia abstained; Ukraine opposed the removals.
The United States, Denmark and Greenland signed an Arctic security agreement that opens the way for US forces at additional Greenland sites, including the Mestersvig outpost.
The Pentagon's public casualty database now lists 19 US military deaths in the Iran war after adding an Army officer; officials told the Washington Post the true figure is at least 22.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Vladimir Putin has been invited to the G20 summit the US hosts in Miami in December; a bipartisan group of senators urged Trump to rescind the invitation.

Reuters reported, citing three sources, that Aramco had restarted flows on the East-West pipeline at reduced rates after the 10-11 September drone attacks; Saudi Arabia has made no official statement, and full capacity may take weeks.

Iran proposed a seven-day plan to end the war, presented by Foreign Minister Araghchi to US envoy Steve Witkoff at the UN: a halt on all fronts including Lebanon, frozen assets released, oil sanctions lifted and the US blockade ended, with the Strait of Hormuz reopening on day seven.

The Saudi-led coalition said air defences intercepted six Houthi ballistic missiles fired at Taif and the Yanbu oil port; a Greek air-defence crew at Yanbu downed a missile and a drone. Mecca received its first civil-defence alert in about a decade. No damage was reported.

Xi Jinping's two-day state visit to Washington ended with the US-China trade truce extended by two months to 10 January, a commitment to explore a channel for AI security incidents, and no deals on tariffs, rare earths, chips or Taiwan.
President Macron said France will send soldiers, radar systems and defence systems to Saudi Arabia to protect the Yanbu site targeted by the Houthis.

Taiwan's defence ministry recorded 10 Chinese military aircraft, 5 crossing the median line, 6 navy ships and 6 other government ships in the day to 24 September, and 2 aircraft, 6 navy and 5 government ships the next day, during Xi's visit.

Russia launched 282 drones plus Zircon and ballistic missiles at Ukraine overnight into 25 September; seven people were killed in Kyiv, including a 14-year-old, and 59 injured, with strikes continuing into the day.

The Wall Street Journal reported that Trump rejected Iran's seven-day plan and sees a renewed bombing campaign as likely; a US official told the BBC that constructive discussions continue through mediators. The White House has not commented on the record.

Six Democratic senators urged Secretary of State Rubio to abandon the Saudi civil nuclear agreement, citing a US intelligence assessment given to Congress that Saudi Arabia has not ruled out developing nuclear weapons.
Yemen's president Rashad al-Alimi called on citizens to join the armed forces and offered amnesty to Houthi defectors, in his first speech since the Houthis took the western Red Sea coast.
The UN said it is gravely concerned as fighting between Ethiopian federal forces and Tigrayan forces spreads across multiple fronts in northern Ethiopia, disrupting aid operations and telecoms.
Pakistan's prime minister Shehbaz Sharif told the UN General Assembly that any Indian attempt to stop or divert Pakistan's share of the Indus waters will be treated as an act of war.
Trump rejected Iran's seven-day plan to end the war and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, calling it not acceptable. No US counter-proposal was published and no strike followed.
Russia launched 173 Shahed-type drones overnight into 26 September, 134 of them shot down, killing six people and injuring 45 across Ukraine as Kyiv faced a second day of strikes.
Ukraine's General Staff confirmed a drone strike that set fire to Russia's Ilsky oil refinery in Krasnodar region, about 400 km from the launch area.
The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted Houthi drones heading for Riyadh and missiles aimed at Khamis Mushait; a senior Houthi official threatened a much larger escalation.

What this dashboard refused to publish today: a $114.89 Brent price for 22 September from a single aggregator, against the board's own $97.88 the day before; a claim the EU added 1,571 new listings, which no report of the renewal carries; and '12 navy ships' off Taiwan, which added navy and government vessels together.

British counter-terrorism police arrested five men near RAF Fairford, a base US bombers use in the Iran war, on suspicion of preparing a terrorist act; police say those held are UK nationals from London. Iran denied any link.

Russian drones and a missile struck Kyiv for a fourth straight night, killing two and injuring at least eight at a market and a gas station. On 28 September daytime drone strikes hit the National Academy of Sciences and a medical centre in central Kyiv.

Trump said Ukraine should take it easy on Russian refineries; a Ukrainian official told the Kyiv Independent that Kyiv would stop only if Russia agrees to an energy truce, and nothing has been agreed.

US ambassador to the UN Mike Waltz said Washington rejected Iran's plan because Tehran was asking for everything up front. Foreign Minister Araghchi said Iran still awaits an official US reply and only negotiation can end the war.
US ambassador to China David Perdue said Trump offered to sell American weapons to Xi Jinping during his visit; the White House later said there are no plans for such a sale.
Russia struck the headquarters of Kyivstar, Ukraine's largest mobile operator, and data centres in Kyiv; three people including two children were injured at one site.
Swiss voters rejected, by about 70 percent, an initiative for stricter neutrality that would have ended Switzerland's sanctions on Russia.
Netanyahu met UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed in Abu Dhabi, an Israeli official said; the visit was not announced in advance and the UAE did not comment.
NPR reported that the US military formally ends its more than two-decade presence in Iraq this week.

Brent's expiring November contract rose more than 3% to about $107 a barrel after Trump's rejection of Iran's plan; December, now the front month, traded near $100. Ship-tracking counted 132 Strait of Hormuz transits in the week to 27 September, up from 116, against about 130 a day before the war.
The US and China released reciprocal lists of about $30bn of goods each on which they will cut tariffs, from consumer electronics to farm products; no strategic goods are included.

Trump told Axios he expects more talks with Iran this week; an Iranian negotiating source told state media the delegation in New York has no plans to negotiate with the US. Qatar has relayed messages between Araghchi and envoys Witkoff and Kushner.
Schools in Riyadh told parents they are switching to remote learning for a week, giving no official reason, amid near-daily Houthi attacks aimed at Saudi Arabia.

An Iraqi investigation found that Iran's Revolutionary Guards and the Houthis launched more than 15 drones from Iraq's Maysan province at Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline on 10 September, Iraqi officials told The New Arab anonymously.
Poland will no longer require pilots to identify drones and missiles entering from Russia visually before shooting them down, its deputy defence minister said.

The EU sanctioned 10 individuals and 17 entities over the deportation of Ukrainian children to Russia, and separately listed Russian judges and a prosecutor's official over the barring of the anti-war Yabloko party from the Duma election.
France's National Rally and its allies won a record 14 seats in partial Senate elections, enough to form a Senate group for the first time, seven months before the presidential vote.
Israeli minister Itamar Ben-Gvir led hundreds of Israelis into the Al-Aqsa Mosque compound during Sukkot; Jordan condemned it as a violation of the status quo.
Ethiopia's army chief accused Sudan and Egypt of backing Tigray rebels as fighting continues in the north; both governments rejected the claim.
Ukraine's 3rd Army Corps said its counter-offensive retook three more settlements on the Lyman axis; the claim has not been independently confirmed.

What this dashboard refused to publish today: a claim that 170 drones hit Kyiv in one night, which the cited reporting does not contain; an Italian frigate's 18 September escort offered as a national mission, when it sailed under the EU's Aspides; and a Kharkiv injury toll reported as both 22 and 43.

The Saudi-led coalition said a Houthi attack at 05:11 on 29 September disabled a transformer at Medina's Taibah power station, which supplies the Prophet's Mosque; the Houthis denied it. Turkey, Qatar, the Arab League and Al-Azhar condemned the strike.

Russia attacked Kyiv from overnight into the evening of 30 September, with 285 drones in the daytime phase alone, 254 of them intercepted, after an overnight wave of drones and Zircon, Oniks and Iskander missiles across Ukraine. Four people were killed in Kyiv, the Trypilska power plant was damaged, and the capital spent 20 hours 44 minutes under alert.

The Pentagon said the last US troops had left Iraq, departing Erbil airbase as the coalition mission against the Islamic State ended on 30 September; operations moved to Jordan, and hundreds of US troops remain in Syria.

A FlyDubai co-pilot stabbed the captain on a Dubai–Tel Aviv flight carrying about 170 people, most of them Israelis, before passengers subdued him; the UAE is leading the investigation into a possible terror link, and Netanyahu said the attacker had been radicalised. No group or state has been linked.

The US Treasury designated Russia's A7 shadow-banking network, its sub-agents and the rouble-backed A7A5 token as a transnational criminal organisation, saying the network moved $140 million from Iranian sanctions-evasion entities. Separately it sanctioned Iran's carmakers, state railway and steel exporters.

Putin told the Valdai forum that an attack on Kaliningrad would put the use of "all weapons" in Russia's arsenal on the agenda, a day after Russian embassies said Russia would use nuclear weapons if NATO tried to isolate the exclave. NATO denounced the "irresponsible nuclear rhetoric."

British police arrested a 27-year-old British-Iranian dual national in London on suspicion of preparing terrorist acts in the RAF Fairford investigation; the five men first arrested were released on bail without charge. Prime Minister Andy Burnham said there were "strong indications that Iran played a part"; Iran denied involvement and summoned Britain's ambassador.

The US urged European allies to release strategic diesel reserves immediately as Trump said he was thinking about banning US diesel exports; the EU's trade chief warned a ban would have very dramatic consequences. US diesel averages $6.39 a gallon, up more than 70% since the war began.

The UN General Assembly debated China and Russia's 17 September veto of a US-backed resolution to keep a panel of experts monitoring sanctions on Iran's nuclear programme; China said it opposed the draft citing US strikes, and the EU urged the mandate be extended.
Houthi forces are massing in Saada near the Saudi border, The New Arab reported citing military sources, while Yemen's government said it carried out 20 strikes on Houthi positions in Taiz.

Taiwan's defence ministry recorded 23 Chinese military aircraft in the 24 hours to 06:00 on 1 October, 16 of them crossing the median line, with seven navy and seven government ships; the next day's count fell to six aircraft, seven navy and eight government ships.

Eritrea severed diplomatic ties with Ethiopia after Addis Ababa closed its embassy in Asmara, as fighting in Ethiopia's north spread; explosions were heard in Addis Ababa after drone flights were banned.

The US nuclear security agency set off a 16-ton chemical explosion in a Nevada tunnel to improve detection of hidden low-yield nuclear tests, an experiment aimed at China's alleged 2020 test; no US nuclear test has been conducted.

The US is sending a third aircraft carrier, the Theodore Roosevelt, and about 2,000 Marines toward Iran, a US official told Al Jazeera, with the full buildup due by the end of November. Trump said Iran would be "hit very hard" but has signalled no action before the midterms.
A 2.5-million-barrel supertanker caught fire after being hit by an unknown projectile in the Strait of Hormuz, according to UKMTO as reported by Al Jazeera; the ship has not been named.

G7 governments agreed to release up to 100 million barrels of emergency oil and diesel stocks over four months, coordinated by the International Energy Agency, with a large diesel release in the first 20 days. Trump then said the US would not ban diesel exports, and Brent briefly fell below $100 before rebounding to about $102 by evening.
Russian drones hit Kyiv's Southern Bridge again overnight, closing it to traffic, and killed one person in the capital; Ukraine says it struck oil facilities in Russia's Volgograd and Samara regions.

Non-Iranian crude exports through the Strait of Hormuz averaged 13.5 million barrels a day in the week to 28 September, roughly pre-war levels, according to Kpler data reported by The New Arab; overall traffic remains far below normal.

What this dashboard refused to publish on 2 October: a claim that the Pentagon confirmed a cut in US troops in Europe, dated to a day that had not yet happened, and Iran war death tolls offered without a source we could read. Correction, 5 October: our refusal of the prime minister's "strong indications" remark on Iran and the Fairford plot was wrong; he said it in a broadcast interview.

The Houthis claimed a ballistic missile and drone strike on an Aramco facility in Riyadh, saying it caused fires; a large smoke plume was seen near the site, Al Jazeera reported. The Saudi-led coalition called the claim misleading.
Ethiopian federal forces and allied fighters captured Mekelle, the capital of Tigray; the Tigray People's Liberation Front said it had temporarily withdrawn and would fight on from elsewhere.

Israel struck Gaza City's Rimal neighbourhood targeting Ali al-Amoudi, whom it called the most senior Hamas figure in Gaza, killing five people including four women; Israel said it was reviewing whether he was killed or injured.
North Korea tested a hypersonic intermediate-range missile on 3 October, Al Jazeera reports; 38 North assesses it as a solid-fuel Hwasong-16B with a glide vehicle.

Two Iranian nationals were charged in Britain with preparing terrorism over an alleged bomb plot against Manchester's Jewish community; police say they were in contact with an overseas third party who 'may be in Iran'. Police say it is unconnected to the RAF Fairford case.

The Pentagon said all US bombers deployed to RAF Fairford have returned to their home bases in the United States over security concerns after the alleged plot against the base; about a dozen B-1s had been stationed there, Al Jazeera reported. Prime Minister Burnham suggested last week that Iran played a part; Iran denies it.

A projectile struck a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz on 4 October, damaging its engine room, UKMTO said; the crew is reported safe and the attacker is unidentified. It is the latest in a run of attacks on tankers in the Strait since the supertanker fire on 2 October.

Yemen's Saudi-backed government launched an offensive to retake all Houthi-held territory after the Houthis took Turbah, a town on the main Aden–Taiz road; the Saudi-led coalition said it carried out 97 strikes on Houthi forces, and air strikes hit Sanaa and Saada.

Iran's parliament speaker and chief negotiator Mohammad Baqer Ghalibaf said the Strait of Hormuz will not open until Iran's seven conditions under the Islamabad memorandum are met. Tehran said it is reviewing US views passed through intermediaries, which it described as focused on nuclear issues.

Zelensky said the US is proposing technical-level talks with Russia and Ukraine in a trilateral format by the end of October, possibly in the UAE, covering energy-facility ceasefires and the Black Sea grain corridor; neither Washington nor Moscow has commented.

Russian drones hit Kyiv's Northern Bridge, injuring two, after repeated strikes on the Southern Bridge, as German Chancellor Merz visited Kyiv and pledged €1.3 billion, including €1 billion in military aid for interceptor drones and long-range weapons.
Ukraine's defence ministry said its strikes have disabled 51% of Russia's oil refining capacity, up from 45% claimed on 21 September; the figure has not been independently verified.
Zelensky said Russia is sharing jet-powered drone technology with North Korea, calling it a very dangerous moment; he cited no evidence and no Western government has confirmed it.
Flávio Bolsonaro took about 47% of valid votes to President Lula's about 45% in the first round of Brazil's presidential election (nearly 99% counted), forcing a runoff on 25 October.
A US strike on a boat in the Caribbean killed four, the 70th such strike since September 2025, Stars and Stripes reports; at least 235 people have been killed in the campaign.

Egypt, Eritrea, Sudan's army leader Burhan and Somalia's president declared at El Alamein that Red Sea governance is the 'exclusive responsibility' of littoral states and rejected unilateral Nile measures, as Ethiopia presses for sea access.

Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan activated their Mecca defence pact for the first time, agreeing at an emergency Riyadh meeting to 'provide the agreed military forces and capabilities and ensure their rapid deployment' to Saudi Arabia against Houthi attacks, under each country's laws. No force size was given.

Russia launched 205 drones, 49 of them jet-powered, overnight into 5 October, and Ukraine's Air Force says 172 were intercepted; five people were killed and 61 injured across Ukraine over the day, including in a Banderol strike on Kharkiv.

Taiwan's defence ministry recorded no Chinese military aircraft in the two days to 06:00 on 5 October, after five the day before, while Chinese government ships around the island rose to eight and then nine and navy ships held at seven to eight.

The FBI arrested Wanying Zhang, 34, of Irvine, California, on a charge of acting as an unregistered agent of China, alleging she surveilled Taiwanese President Lai Ching-te's son and sent photos, video and licence-plate details to Chinese officials.

Kpler data show Middle East oil exports excluding Iran exceeded pre-war levels in September for the first time since the war began, with about 40% now bypassing Hormuz through Saudi and UAE pipelines.

What this dashboard refused to publish today: an account of Bahraini soldiers killed by a Houthi drone on the Saudi border, which dates from September 2023, not this war; a Lebanon death toll carried only by outlets outside our directory; and a claim of fuel rationing in Moscow offered without a source we could read.

Yemen's government said its forces took the Dhubab district and the Red Sea port of Mocha and had 'neutralised' 1,747 Houthi fighters; the Houthis denied losing Dhubab, and the claims could not be independently verified.
Abiy was sworn in for a third term, vowing that Ethiopia will secure 'an outlet to the sea'.

About 500 US troops with helicopters and drones were sent to the Texas border after an alleged late-September shooting at US Coast Guard personnel from across the Rio Grande; Mexico says it has seen no evidence of the shooting.

A projectile struck a Panama-flagged tanker in the Strait of Hormuz on 6 October, injuring 12 crew members; the attacker was not identified. Al Jazeera counts nine attacks on tankers in the Strait so far in October.

UK counter-terrorism police arrested a 22-year-old British man in London on suspicion of preparing terrorist acts in the RAF Fairford investigation. The six men arrested earlier, including a British-Iranian dual national, have been released on bail, and police found petrol but no explosives.

German prosecutors arrested former BND foreign-intelligence chief August Hanning on suspicion of treasonous espionage for a foreign service they did not name; Süddeutsche Zeitung reports Russia is not involved.
CNN reported, citing unnamed sources, informal US-China talks on reciprocal visits to nuclear laboratories and possibly test sites; neither government has confirmed them.

Houthi missile and drone attacks on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh and Abha International Airport on 6 and 7 October killed three civilians and injured 36, Saudi civil aviation authorities said. The Houthis claimed a ballistic missile strike on the Riyadh airport, and explosions were heard in Riyadh on 8 October.

A tanker was hit by multiple projectiles about 94 km north of Madinat ash Shamal off Qatar's north coast, with casualties reported, UKMTO said; it is the first reported tanker attack in the western Gulf in weeks, and no attacker was named.

Russia launched 48 cruise missiles, ballistic missiles and 130 drones at Ukraine overnight into 7 October, Putin's birthday, Ukraine's Air Force said. At least 30 people were killed, more than 20 of them in Pryluky, including five children.

Denmark's intelligence service said Russia has moved from planning to attempting sabotage against Danish firms supplying Ukraine, targeting weapons production, Reuters reports; it named no firms, and Russia's embassy denied it.
A Congressional Research Service update said 81 US military aircraft have been lost or damaged in the Iran war, up from 42 in May, including 45 MQ-9 Reaper drones and 12 F-15E jets.

Lithuania said it will deploy soldiers to help border guards along its border with Russia's Kaliningrad region, calling it a preventive step after armed escorts brought migrants across Latvia's border from Belarus and masked men stole border equipment on 6 October.

Witnesses said dozens of Eritrean soldiers in uniform were seen in Adigrat in Ethiopia's Tigray region, the first reported Eritrean presence since fighting resumed on 23 September; Eritrea's information minister did not deny that troops had crossed.

Taiwan's defence ministry recorded 14 Chinese military aircraft, nine crossing the median line, in the day to 06:00 on 7 October, after none the day before; Chinese government ships fell from eight to one as the aircraft returned.

EU ambassadors approved the bloc's 22nd sanctions package, about 1,700 listings aimed at Russia's missile, drone and electronics supply, with formal adoption expected on 12 October, Euromaidan Press reports.

Fires were reported at the Salavat oil refinery in Bashkortostan and at Yandex's largest data centre in Ryazan region after overnight drone attacks, according to videos and monitoring groups; neither government commented, and the reports are unverified.
Britain renamed its consulate in East Jerusalem a 'mission' and kept a reduced staff after Israel's deadline to close it expired; Israel said most of the consulate's diplomats were leaving.

What this dashboard refused to publish today: a $91.93 Brent price for 7 October from an unlisted website, which Al Jazeera's $101.53 contradicts; a 3 October North Korean missile test described as 'AI-capable' that no listed outlet carried; and a Lebanon death toll carried only by outlets outside the board's directory.
OFAC designated 27 entities, six people and 22 vessels in Iran's oil-shipping network, including five Hong Kong companies.

The US, UK, Australia, Canada, Japan, New Zealand and Spain jointly attributed a hacking toolset to actors enabled by China's Integrity Technology Group, linked to Flax Typhoon, used against government, manufacturing and healthcare networks.

The UN Security Council extended the Darfur-only arms embargo to 11 December after Russia and China blocked a US push for a nationwide Sudan embargo; Russia's deputy envoy said Moscow would not allow 'even a hint of broadening'.

Trump said he agreed with Putin to let Russian diesel onto world markets, starting with more than 300,000 tonnes, and the Treasury issued a Russia-related general licence on 9 October; Euromaidan Press reports it authorises Russian diesel sales until April 2027. Russia said it partially lifted its diesel export ban the next day.

The US Treasury placed the International Criminal Court itself on its sanctions list, with a six-month grace period; Britain, France, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, Denmark, Canada and Japan said they 'regret and strongly disagree' with the move.
The UAE's attorney general said the FlyDubai co-pilot who tried to seize a Dubai–Tel Aviv flight on 30 September planned a suicide attack on Ben Gurion airport and acted alone.

EU and Chinese trade officials reached a partial deal in Beijing: China will moderate hybrid-car exports to Europe and keep a 'green channel' for rare-earth and magnet export licences, with further talks set for early 2027.

A missile strike on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh on 10 October killed 12 people and wounded 309, Saudi authorities said; France 24 called it the deadliest on Saudi soil in more than a decade. No group has claimed it; the Saudi-led coalition blamed the Houthis and vowed a 'decisive response'.

Trump said Ukraine should 'get a new president' and that Zelensky 'better damn well stop' striking Russian refineries. Zelensky called the diesel deal a 'weak decision'; EU foreign policy chief Kallas said it was 'not the time to ease pressure on Russia, and Europe won't.'
Trump called the Riyadh airport attack 'not acceptable' and, asked whether he would now join Saudi strikes on the Houthis, said 'We may'.

A US fighter jet struck the stern of the Panama-flagged cargo ship Ocean Molica in the Gulf of Oman after it ignored warnings and tried to run the blockade of Iran, disabling its propulsion without harming the crew, Central Command said. Iran's Revolutionary Guard said it struck an LPG carrier in the Strait for taking an 'illegal route'.

Russian glide bombs hit apartment blocks in Zaporizhzhia early on 10 October, killing at least 20 people including three children; at least 24 were killed across Ukraine in a day, and missiles struck Kyiv that afternoon.

Taiwan's defence ministry recorded 21 Chinese military aircraft, 13 of them crossing the median line, in the day to 06:00 on 10 October, Taiwan's National Day, after two the day before; the count fell to 12 the next day.
Yemen's government said its forces were advancing on the Houthis around the Bab al-Mandab strait; a Houthi official said the attack was repelled. Neither claim could be independently verified.

Trump revoked four orders dating from 1985 to 2007 that barred direct flights between the United States and Lebanon; Lebanon's President Aoun welcomed it, though flights still await US security assessments.

Eritrea asked the UN Security Council to condemn Ethiopia and take 'deterrent measures', calling Ethiopia's accusations a 'declaration of war', after Ethiopia told the Council it was acting in self-defence.
An air strike on a gold-mining site at Jabal al-Uqaydat on the Sudan-Egypt border killed at least 72 miners; a Sudanese lawyers' group blamed Egypt's air force, and Egypt did not comment.

Trump announced an 'energy ceasefire' between Russia and Ukraine, saying both had agreed; Kyiv said it was not told in advance, and Moscow has not formally confirmed it. Russia struck Kharkiv's CHP-5 power plant hours later.

A third Yandex data centre in Russia, in Vladimir region, was shut after a reported drone attack, following strikes on sites in Sasovo and Kaluga on 8 and 9 October; Zelensky said Ukraine 'always responds in kind'.

A cyberattack disabled refrigeration in hundreds of French supermarkets, about 150 to 200 Intermarché stores and nearly 100 Coopérative U outlets, forcing them to discard fresh food; Paris prosecutors are investigating, and no one has been named.
A projectile struck Riyadh's King Khalid airport again on 11 October, killing one person and wounding 11, Saudi authorities said, a day after the strike that killed 12.

EU foreign ministers adopted the bloc's largest-ever set of Russia sanctions listings in Luxembourg on 12 October: 1,569 targets, 826 defence-industry companies and 743 of their executives, with asset freezes and entry bans. Kallas said it was not the time to ease pressure on Moscow.

UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham told Parliament it was 'highly likely' the RAF Fairford incident was coordinated in Iran and 'almost certainly directed' by the Revolutionary Guard; Iran rejected the claim. No one has been charged.
EU foreign policy chief Kallas said in a post on X that EU foreign ministers had 'just adopted nearly 1,600 new sanctions listings targeting Russia's military-industrial complex', Tasnim reports.
Ethiopian federal forces had taken Shire, Adigrat, Adwa and Zalambessa up to the Eritrean border before pausing on 12 October, Critical Threats reports.

Ukrainian officials told the Kyiv Independent that US officials threatened to cut intelligence sharing and PURL weapons purchases unless Ukraine stops striking Russian oil refineries. No US official has confirmed it on the record.

German police detained two Turkish nationals over the 23 September arson of a Starlink ground station near Warsaw that serves Ukraine; Poland says Russian intelligence was behind it and will charge them with sabotage for a foreign service.

North Korea fired at least two ballistic missiles 17 minutes apart; Japan's deputy defence minister said the second flew more than 910 km on an irregular path and may have been hypersonic. Seoul called it a show of force after its own first hypersonic test on 8 October.
Pakistan and the Taliban kept fighting along the Kurram-Paktia border after Moscow-format talks ended on 5 October with no joint statement; Pakistan declared an emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

Russia fired 39 ballistic missiles and more than 120 drones at Ukraine overnight into 14 October, Zelensky said, hitting all three of Kyiv's combined heat and power plants; four people were killed, 25 injured and 600,000 left without power. Kyiv says allies gave no launch warning on 12 or 13 October.

The Houthis hit an Aramco administrative building in Dhahran on 13 October, causing a fire but no casualties, a Saudi energy ministry official said; debris from missiles intercepted over Riyadh injured four people and damaged 15 homes.

The Singapore-flagged container ship GFS Pride sank in the Strait of Hormuz after being hit and catching fire; all 21 crew were evacuated, Singapore's maritime authority said. Reuters reports it is the war's second ship sinking; the bulk carrier Cape Dao, struck on 23 September, also sank.

MI5 chief Ken McCallum called Russia 'aggressor number one', saying it is escalating hybrid attacks below NATO's Article 5 threshold and hiring criminals after nearly 1,000 expulsions of its officers; he cited more than 50 Iran-linked arrests in Britain in a year.
Asked whether Russia had broken the energy ceasefire, Trump said 'I'll let you know about that later' and that 'Ukraine hit many sites the day before'.

SpaceX capped the speed of moving Starlink terminals on Ukraine's military service package, a presidential adviser said, calling it 'not a coincidence'; a defence ministry source confirmed the limit. SpaceX and the White House have not commented.

The Saudi-led coalition struck the Yemeni Oil Company's al-Sabah station in Sanaa after an evacuation order, saying the Houthis stored missiles there, and hit oil sites at Ras Isa and in Hodeidah; the company said its tanks were empty.

Trump said the Houthis were 'behaving very badly' and that he might ask Turkey's Erdogan to intervene for Saudi Arabia; the Houthis told civilians to leave Aramco sites, calling them 'a legitimate target'.

Israel's Channel 12 reported that Netanyahu pressed Trump to resume fighting with Iran before Israel's and America's elections; Netanyahu's office denied it. Trump said: 'We'll make a decision on Iran very soon.'

A previously unknown group, 'Black Rus', claimed the 6 October raid that took cameras from Latvia's border with Belarus and promised more incursions into NATO territory; Lukashenko says Latvia staged it, and NATO's StratCom centre in Riga calls it an operation linked to Belarusian and Russian authorities.

NATO began its annual Steadfast Noon nuclear exercise in Italy, running to 23 October with 17 nations; NATO calls it routine and not linked to current events, and its nuclear-policy chief said Russia's nuclear posture had not changed significantly.
Russia detained Yuki Imai, a Hokkaido Shimbun journalist, on FSB espionage charges, alleging he gathered information on mobilised troops for Japanese intelligence; Japan protested.
French forces seized a suspected Russian shadow-fleet tanker near Réunion in the Indian Ocean; Moscow called it piracy.

North Korea test-fired two types of submarine-launched strategic cruise missiles off its east coast, from a vertical tube and a torpedo tube, South Korea's military said; Stars and Stripes says it is the first publicly reported such test since January 2024.

Iran has stepped up attacks on ships around the Strait of Hormuz, Reuters reports via The New Arab, with at least five incidents in 48 hours; Iranian officials say the aim is to frustrate US efforts to lower oil prices before the midterms.
China and North Korea were to open the long-delayed New Yalu River Bridge on 15 October, Chinese state media said, after Xi's June visit to Pyongyang.
A US Marine on Okinawa was arrested over the killing of a Japanese woman in Naha; US forces imposed a curfew to 8 November, which Prime Minister Takaichi called inadequate.

A Sofia court cleared arrest warrants for two 19-year-old Germans charged in absentia over the 9 October fire at Bulgaria's Plana teleport, a Starlink site serving Ukraine; they had crossed from Serbia and returned there. Bulgaria called it sabotage but named no state.
A Ukrainian ex-officer went on trial in Hamburg as the alleged leader of the 2022 Nord Stream pipeline sabotage; he denies it, and Kyiv denies involvement.

Conflict Armament Research said the Houthis are seeking to build a Kheibar Shekan-type ballistic missile with Chinese-sourced components seized en route to Hodeidah in July, AP reports; the Chinese embassy did not respond.
Russia launched 580 drones and two Kh-59 missiles overnight into 15 October, Ukraine's Air Force said, downing or jamming 536. Kirovohrad's governor called it the oblast's heaviest attack of the war.

Two tankers caught fire off Romania's Sulina, near the Danube mouth, amid drone attacks on Black Sea shipping; seven crew of a San Marino-flagged chemical tanker are missing. Bulgaria said it had no proof Russia was responsible.
Houthi missiles struck Aden's Maashiq presidential palace, the seat of Yemen's government; the cabinet was unharmed. Officials gave tolls ranging from two to five killed.
Zelensky told the Financial Times that Ukraine will resume strikes on Russian oil refineries, which it had paused at Washington's demand.

Taiwan's defence ministry counted 15 Chinese military aircraft, 13 across the median line, with 10 navy and seven government ships in the day to 06:00 on 15 October; the next two days showed 8 and 9 aircraft.

The Chinese carrier Liaoning and three destroyers flew aircraft inside Japan's exclusive economic zone south of Ishigaki and passed between Okinawa and Miyako into the Pacific; Japan scrambled jets. China called it routine annual training.
Up to 100 soldiers from the US 1st Infantry Division arrived at Pabradė, Lithuania, with two battalions expected by mid-November, as the Pentagon reviews its force posture in Europe.
The US Treasury designated an Iraqi bank, two offshore Iranian banks, exchange houses and a Hong Kong trading firm in a new round against Iran's finances.

Iraq's parliament approved the remaining cabinet, making Asaib Ahl al-Haq's Laith al-Khazali, a US-designated terrorist, one of three deputy prime ministers, Reuters reports, two weeks after US troops left.

Trump signed an executive order implementing Congress's Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act and, in the same order, waived its sanctions and tariffs on Russia with no end date. Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev called it 'historic'.

Reuters reports, citing two US officials and a Western official, that the order to slow SpaceX's Starshield service for Ukraine's military came from inside the White House. A senior US official said the president made no such request.

Romania blamed Russia for the drone attacks on ships off its coast, Euromaidan Press reports, and proposed a joint NATO Black Sea command, led in rotation by the alliance's Black Sea members, which it offered to host from 2028.

Two missiles struck Aden airport as a Cairo-bound flight prepared to leave, with no casualties; the Houthis claimed it. The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted a ballistic missile aimed at Yanbu, the kingdom's Red Sea oil hub.

UKMTO reported a tanker struck by an unknown projectile 68 nautical miles northeast of Jubail, Saudi Arabia, inside the Gulf; all crew were evacuated, Times of Israel reports. The ship has not been named.

CENTCOM commander Adm. Brad Cooper said the blockade has kept $25 billion of Iranian oil from export and that Iran-aligned militias are withholding soldiers' pay to send money to the Revolutionary Guard.
A drone strike on a cattle market in Nyala, South Darfur, killed at least 30 people and wounded 47, AFP reports, citing a hospital source; the RSF blamed the army, which did not claim it.

Two Romanian F-16s shot down two jet-powered Geran drones over Romanian territorial waters near Sulina on the evening of 17 October, Romania's defence ministry said. NATO's North Atlantic Council holds a special Black Sea session on 20 October at Romania's request.

Russia launched 332 drones and Iskander-M or North Korean KN-23 ballistic missiles overnight into 17 October; Ukraine's Air Force said 289 drones were downed. Seven were killed across Ukraine, and Al Jazeera reports power was cut to about one million people.

Iran's Revolutionary Guard says a supertanker carrying over two million barrels of crude struck a naval mine on an 'unauthorised route' through Hormuz and caught fire. No ship has been named and no independent body has confirmed it.
Pakistan suspended trade with Iran at the Taftan and Gabd border crossings, citing security and smuggling, stranding about 2,000 trucks; Iran cited technical issues.

Taiwan's coast guard drove away 16 Chinese vessels, four of them fishing boats, operating simultaneously around the main island and Pratas, calling it 'hybrid warfare' and an attempt to 'unilaterally alter the status quo'; some entered restricted waters.
Trump defended waiving the Graham Act's Russia sanctions, writing that he did not want to 'drive, foolishly, Russia away from the bargaining table' and 'I can sign it later, or any time that I want!'
Ukrainian drones hit an oil terminal, a fuel depot and a data centre near St Petersburg, about 1,000 km from the front, Euromaidan Press reports, a week into the US-announced energy truce.

Lithuania foiled a night arson attack on a Starlink site serving Ukraine, the third such target after Poland and Bulgaria, Euromaidan Press reports; the prime minister said he believes the perpetrators are known.

A drone carrying explosives crossed into Lithuania; NATO jets could not identify it through cloud, and officials later said it was Ukrainian. Prime Minister Sinkevičius asked NATO for talks on allowing shoot-downs on radar detection alone.

Russia fired 16 ballistic missiles and more than 200 drones overnight into 19 October, hitting 28 substations and other energy facilities in 11 oblasts; at least 550,000 households lost power. Zelensky said Ukraine 'once again' had no advance warning from partners.

Zelensky said the Pentagon is delaying missiles European countries have already paid for, pending Defence Secretary Hegseth's signature. Secretary of State Rubio denied intelligence sharing had been withdrawn; Trump said Zelensky 'doesn't know what he's talking about' and that it is time for somebody else to negotiate for Ukraine.

Houthi ballistic missiles struck the al-Alam military camp near Ataq in Shabwa province, where new recruits were training; a Yemeni military source told DPA more than 30 soldiers were killed. The government's army spokesman blamed the Houthis, who have not commented.

Kim Yo Jong said North Korea's military is considering deploying 'tactical strike means' along the DMZ, calling the border 'very unstable' after South Korean warning shots at troops crossing the demarcation line; Seoul vowed to retaliate firmly against provocations.

Russia's Cosmos 2612 satellite manoeuvred to within about 500 metres of an ICEYE commercial radar satellite that supports Ukraine between 15 and 19 October, commercial trackers say; LeoLabs called it the most advanced and potentially dangerous uncooperative approach it has observed.

Trump said Russia 'has been fine on Ukraine. They haven't been doing much,' hours after a drone strike killed six in a Kharkiv Oblast park. He said he was open to a summit with Putin and Xi, mainly on nuclear disarmament.

US envoy Witkoff plans talks in Oslo this week with Zelensky and European officials, followed by a separate trip to meet Putin in Russia, Reuters reports, citing unnamed people; the schedule is tentative.

The Houthis claimed attacks on an Aramco site in Yanbu, the Shaybah oilfield, Riyadh's King Khalid airport and Abha airport. Saudi Arabia did not confirm them, and Reuters could not verify the claims.

US embassies across the Middle East issued a security alert citing Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and the risk of Iranian or proxy attacks on Americans, warning hostilities 'have the potential to escalate rapidly'.

Russian Foreign Minister Lavrov, in Tehran, called for conditions in Hormuz to return to those before the US-Israeli war on Iran and said Russian personnel would gradually return to the Bushehr nuclear plant. Iran's Araghchi blamed US and Israeli attacks for the Strait's instability.

US Defence Secretary Hegseth met Netanyahu on an unannounced visit to Israel, at an air base in the south per Army Radio; the Pentagon declined to comment. Trump had endorsed Netanyahu for the 27 October election; Vance declined to.

Egypt's parliament postponed to 26 October its vote on Sisi's request to authorise sending air-defence forces and logistics to Saudi Arabia if asked; one party told its MPs to abstain, citing Red Sea risks.

Keen Sword, the biennial US-Japan exercise, began with about 56,000 US and Japanese troops and seven partner nations through 29 October; the carrier USS Theodore Roosevelt joined from Yokosuka, and US Marines are deploying NMESIS anti-ship missiles to Yonaguni, Japan's island nearest Taiwan.

Japan scrambled jets 442 times in April–September against 265 a year earlier, with scrambles against Russian aircraft up from 59 to 152; Defence Minister Koizumi called joint Russia-China flights a show of force.
