Finland plans to buy one million anti-personnel mines for about €100 million, with contracts by the end of 2027, after leaving the Ottawa Convention; its foreign minister urged an EU-wide ban on tourist visas for Russians.

The US sanctioned five China-based entities under the Protecting American Intellectual Property Act over the theft of Google AI trade secrets, including the investor MiraclePlus and its funds, barring Americans from buying their equity or debt.

A former OpenAI engineer was charged with planting a recording device in an executive conference room; prosecutors say he 'appears to have received considerable support' from the Saudi government but do not allege it directed the recording.

Florida issued an arrest warrant for former Cuban leader Raúl Castro, 95, on a murder-conspiracy charge over the 1996 shoot-down of Brothers to the Rescue planes; a federal indictment already covers the case. Washington has run a de facto oil blockade of Cuba since January, AFP reports.

Human Rights Watch said Malian army and Russian Africa Corps air strikes killed 89 civilians from April to August, about double a year earlier; Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger have resumed talks with ECOWAS.

US Secretary of State Rubio met Central Asian foreign ministers in Samarkand, backing a Trans-Caspian trade route that bypasses Russia and critical-minerals cooperation; Uzbekistan announced about $12 billion in agreements.
Drone strikes on a market and a village in Abyei, on the Sudan–South Sudan border, killed dozens of civilians, the UN said; Guterres condemned them. No side was named.

Britain will fly RAF Typhoon jets on 'defensive counter air missions' to protect Saudi cities and infrastructure from Houthi missiles and drones, and extend air-to-air refuelling, the Ministry of Defence said; the jets will not attack the Houthis.

China's Southern Theater Command said the USS Charleston 'illegally intruded' near Sabina Shoal in the Spratlys and that its navy tracked the ship; the Philippines said no nation can require permission for lawful transit. Reuters notes the last known US freedom-of-navigation operation there was over a year ago.

NATO will send more maritime patrol aircraft, radars, drones and intelligence staff to the Black Sea after drone attacks on shipping, the alliance said after its council met at Romania's request. It announced no new command or naval mission.

France and Britain held their first joint airborne nuclear-strike exercise on 20–21 October: RAF Typhoons escorted French Rafales on a simulated nuclear mission over the Mediterranean, France's armed forces ministry said. No nuclear weapons were involved.

Saudi Arabia postponed its Future Investment Initiative conference, set for 26–29 October, to 2027, citing continuing Houthi strikes; government agencies in Riyadh told staff to work from home, AFP reports.
Taiwan's defence ministry counted 2, 5 and 14 Chinese military aircraft in the three days to 06:00 on 20 October, with 8 of the 14 crossing the median line; navy ships ran at 5, 6 and 7.

Turkey sent the Mecca defence pact with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan to parliament for ratification, Reuters reports citing parliamentary sources; a Turkish official said Turkey's role would likely be limited to equipment, intelligence and weapons systems.
US envoy Tom Barrack said in Doha that the US is moving away from the Gulf's oil-for-security bargain but is 'not leaving' the Middle East.

Taiwan's coast guard said a Chinese coast-guard ship entered restricted waters at Pratas and broadcast that 'the so-called Republic of China does not exist', Reuters reports; a US congressional review commission chair called Chinese coast-guard patrols east of Taiwan 'highly destabilizing'.
Reuters reports Trump has not approved a new $14 billion arms package for Taiwan, having called arms sales a 'negotiating chip' with Xi.

South Korea will withdraw more embassy staff from Kyiv after Zelensky publicly disclosed that two captured North Korean soldiers had been transferred to Seoul, which says the transfer was meant to stay confidential.

The European Commission presented an Arctic strategy that would extend tracking of Russia's shadow fleet to the North Atlantic and Arctic and set up an 'Arctic Cable Club' against sabotage; an EU official said Russia's merging of its Baltic and Arctic fleets shows Moscow treats the regions as one.

Hungary blocked the next step in the EU membership bids of Ukraine and Moldova at a meeting of member-state experts, giving no explanation; diplomats expect the final two negotiating clusters to open in December.

US envoy Witkoff met Putin in St Petersburg; the Kremlin says Putin agreed to resume three-way talks with Ukraine and the US, possibly next month. Putin said Russia wants talks on a final deal, not a short ceasefire, and freed Stephen Hubbard, a 74-year-old American.

A late-night attack on Dammam airport killed two people, a Saudi and an Indian, and injured eight, Saudi Arabia's civil aviation authority said; it did not say who carried it out. Arab News reports debris from an intercepted drone killed two workers at the Shaybah oil field the same day.

Germany's armed forces raised their Russian sabotage threat level to 'significant', the second-highest, for the first time, Süddeutsche Zeitung reports and a defence ministry spokesperson confirmed. SZ says the trigger was an explosive-laden drone found near Wunstorf air base.

Taiwan's defence ministry counted 29 Chinese military aircraft, 23 of them across the median line, plus 6 navy ships and 9 official ships in the 24 hours to 06:00 on 21 October. It detected no aircraft in the next two days as Typhoon Champi approached.

The US Treasury sanctioned the Panama- and Piraeus-based law firm Karnakis & Karnakis, three shipping firms and nine vessels for Iran oil trade. The same day it issued a Russia licence for the sale of Lukoil International and lifted several North Korea and Belarus listings.

The EU proposed 117 new Russia listings, including 52 banks and 31 oil firms, in response to the US diesel deal, Kyiv Independent reports. Kallas: 'pressure the aggressor to stop the war, not the victim to surrender.' Member states must still approve it.
The US ordered some diplomats and non-emergency staff to leave Saudi Arabia because of Houthi attacks, AP reports.

A senior Revolutionary Guard official, Yadollah Javani, warned that undersea internet cables under the Strait of Hormuz could be targeted if Iranian infrastructure is attacked, Iran International reports.

Iran's Revolutionary Guard claimed seven tankers were struck on 21–22 October near Hormuz, naming none; AP could not confirm and UKMTO has not reported them. Trump said Iran is 'making up fake hits'. Lloyd's List counts 28 ship attacks in October, the war's highest month.

Russia fired 21 ballistic missiles at Kyiv in three waves overnight into 22 October, plus about 200 drones, Zelensky and the Air Force said; Kyiv's metro was cut in two. At least seven people were killed across Ukraine.

Aramco ordered staff to evacuate its Dhahran headquarters and work remotely, the first time since the Yemen war resumed, Reuters reports citing six sources; Bloomberg says an alarm preceded it. Aramco did not comment.

Moscow's mayor said 630 Ukrainian drones were tracked over the Moscow region overnight and 163 heading for the city were shot down; Russia's defence ministry claimed 808 intercepted nationwide. Astra says a military storage site in Serpukhov was hit, unverified.

Downing Street rejected Witkoff's description of Putin as acting on humanitarian concerns: 'We certainly do not recognise that characterisation,' a spokesperson said, adding that Putin has killed thousands.
Trump said Musk had restored Ukraine's Starlink access; Zelensky told CNN it is 'still limited', with speed caps that hamper drone interception. The Pentagon denies ordering the cap.

Bloomberg reports Rosneft officials privately say a few more months of Ukrainian refinery strikes could cause lasting damage; Ryazan has been shut more than half the time since May and Tuapse since April.
German federal prosecutors arrested a Ukrainian man in Brandenburg suspected of spying for Russia on arms production and NATO eastern-flank facilities since July 2025.
A defendant in London's Iran plot trial testified that his handlers wanted an Iran International journalist's arms and legs broken; three men deny National Security Act charges.

Kim Yo Jong said North Korea's border loudspeakers will be ready to broadcast into the South within days; South Korea's military says it may restart its own. Its army chief told troops to act if provoked.
Israel's army chief sees no operational need to strike Iran before the 27 October election, Channel 13 reports, via Times of Israel.

A drone strike sank the Comoros-flagged cargo ship Khoryv about 13 nautical miles off Constanta, just outside Romania's territorial waters; one sailor was killed and three are missing. Romania's President Dan called it part of Russia's escalation.
Austria expelled four Russian diplomats, three from the embassy and one from Russia's OSCE delegation, for activities incompatible with their status; Moscow said a response is unavoidable.
A Russian Geran drone crashed in Moldova's Telenești district, under 100 metres from a home and near an energy facility, the defence ministry said; Moldova expelled a Russian embassy staffer.

A Russian diesel cargo for the US under Washington's waiver, about 40,000 tonnes on the tanker Agioi Fanendes, loaded at Primorsk bound for New York and is due on 7 November, Reuters shipping data show; Reuters calls it the first under the Trump–Putin deal.

Gunmen attacked a funeral at a Greek Orthodox church in Jordan's Karak governorate, killing eight and injuring about 40, the health ministry said; three wounded suspects were arrested on 26 October after a firefight. No group has been named.

Two Israeli soldiers were killed at a checkpoint near Hebron and both attackers were shot dead; Israel then removed about 250 Palestinian families from the city, its mayor said, and will close West Bank crossings on election day.
Drone strikes killed at least 306 people in Sudan in the first three weeks of October, the UN human rights office said, attributing them to both the army and the RSF.

Polish prosecutors are investigating a $30,000 offer, made over Telegram, to set fire to a drone factory in Gliwice that supplies Ukraine; they say the recruiter worked for a foreign intelligence service. Journalists traced the account to a Russian number.

Russia and Ukraine agreed a ceasefire in occupied Oleshky from 04:00 on 27 October to let aid in and civilians out; the White House said Melania Trump brokered it, and both militaries confirmed they would observe it.

Kim Jong-un crossed the New Yalu River Bridge into China and met Communist Party standing committee member Wang Huning in Dandong, his first China visit since September 2025, Xinhua and Seoul's unification ministry said.
Secretary of State Rubio urged Cubans seeking change to form a 'discrete partnership' with the CIA, a day after Trump said he would deal with Cuba once Iran is settled.

Iran's armed forces chief of staff Ali Abdollahi said Iran 'will not allow US military ships in the Persian Gulf under any circumstances', state television reported; Trump said on 23 October, 'We may do another little Epic Fury.'

Kremlin aide Ushakov said Russia will be ready to resume three-way talks with Ukraine and the US after 4 November; Zelensky says technical meetings are planned in the first half of November, possibly in Abu Dhabi. No date is set.

Kremlin aide Ushakov said Moscow, Beijing and Washington are 'in principle ready' for a Putin–Trump–Xi meeting on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen on 18–19 November; neither Washington nor Beijing has confirmed it.

Lula won Brazil's presidential runoff with just over 51 percent to Flávio Bolsonaro's 48 percent at 98.76 percent counted; Bolsonaro said it is 'impossible to recognise the results' and pledged to annul the vote.
Serbia's President Vučić conceded his party lost the snap parliamentary election to the student-led movement; a CESID projection gives the Student List 138 of 250 seats on turnout near 70 percent.

CENTCOM commander Adm. Brad Cooper flew over the Strait of Hormuz and said its primary transit routes remain free of Iranian sea mines; CENTCOM says US support helped Gulf states export more than 1.5 billion barrels since the summer.

The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted Houthi ballistic missiles fired at Riyadh as the capital's airport partly reopened, and that it destroyed two missile launchers in Sanaa; no casualties were reported.

Israel's Channel 12 reported that army chief Eyal Zamir resisted a Netanyahu order for military action tied to Iran; Netanyahu called the report nonsense and Defence Minister Katz called talk of a rift baseless.
Zelensky said Ukraine's Starlink links are back to full speed; Musk said SpaceX had restricted the service because Ukraine broke its terms, which Kyiv rejects.
Algeria's senate voted 148 of 174 to send troops to Niger, which a senator told AFP is to protect energy facilities; troop numbers were not given.

North Korea told the UN Security Council that South Korea 'fabricated' the 21 September DMZ mine blast that injured three of its soldiers, and said violations of its sovereignty could trigger self-defence; Seoul proposed military talks on the border line.

Saudi Arabia's defence minister, Pakistan's army chief Asim Munir and Turkey's intelligence chief are due in Tehran for security talks between the Mecca pact states and Iran, Iranian state media say; Iran told Munir there will be no US talks until its demands are met.

Saudi Arabia's defence minister Khalid bin Salman, Turkey's intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin and Pakistan's army chief Asim Munir met Iranian leaders in Tehran on 26 October. A Saudi deputy minister said the aim was to reduce hostilities and support Qatari and Pakistani mediation; no outcome was announced.

Egypt's parliament authorised President Sisi to send military support to Saudi Arabia if Riyadh asks for it, by the two-thirds majority the constitution requires; Sisi says Egypt's role is limited to defending Saudi territory.

A Kuwaiti state security court sentenced three men to death for spying for Iran and Hezbollah and plotting to assassinate First Deputy Prime Minister Sheikh Fahad Al-Yousef; the sentences can be appealed. On 28 October Kuwait summoned Iran's ambassador over an embassy statement on the case.
An army strike on Tanqonj Market in Nyala, South Darfur, killed at least 102 people, AFP reports; the UN chief said on 31 October he was appalled by drone attacks on civilians in Sudan.
Taiwan's defence ministry detected no Chinese military aircraft in the two days to 06:00 on 25 October and three, one across the median line, in the day to 26 October, with five to six navy ships.

Turkey's parliamentary foreign affairs committee approved the Mecca defence agreement with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan, a 16-article pact binding for ten years; it now goes to the full assembly, with no date set.

The Oleshky humanitarian ceasefire took effect on 27 October with no violations reported by either side; Russia said it halted strikes on Ukraine's Kherson, and Ukraine's negotiator Arakhamia said the truce runs to 1 November. An evacuation is planned.

Russia fired 16 ballistic missiles and more than 280 drones at Ukraine overnight into 27 October, hitting a Kyiv university campus and the Southern Bridge and killing one woman. Zelensky says Russia has fired more than 100 ballistic missiles at the Kyiv area since 14 October and Ukraine lacks Patriot interceptors while it waits for US sign-off.

The Trump administration is considering lifting sanctions on a Russian state investment fund, the New York Times reported on 27 October, citing an unnamed US official; no Treasury action has been published.

Russian satellites passed over Saudi oil and air-base sites before and after attacks by Iran-backed groups, AP reported, citing a private analysis firm and anonymous Saudi and Houthi officials. Russia did not comment; the claim rests on that analysis and unnamed sources.

Two men were charged in London under the National Security Act over an incident at RAF Fairford, the base US bombers used to strike Iran; one is accused of helping a foreign intelligence service, which prosecutors say is Iran's.
IAEA chief Rafael Grossi told the UN Security Council the agency has seen no activity to repair or rebuild any Iranian nuclear facility damaged in the 2025 and 2026 attacks.

The US told several Gulf states to prepare for a possible short but intense campaign against Iran after the 3 November midterms, the Wall Street Journal reported; Trump has not decided, and the White House says all options are on the table. An extra Patriot battery is moving to Israel.

Vice President Vance wrote to Mohsen Rezaei, head of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, proposing a framework for negotiations, the Wall Street Journal reported; Trump said it was Vance's idea. A senior Iranian official called Qatar's latest ideas unacceptable.

US naval forces advised ships with no need to transit the Strait of Hormuz area to stay well clear, citing the geopolitical situation and blockade enforcement, in a notice issued through the Joint Maritime Information Center.

Three sea drones hit a Liberian-flagged container ship about 21 miles southeast of Shabla, in Bulgaria's exclusive economic zone; all 18 crew were evacuated safely. Bulgaria named no attacker; Moscow denies involvement.

Houthi media said Saudi strikes killed 14 people at a market and petrol station in Yemen's Jawf province; Yemen's government said two Houthi ballistic missiles hit the perimeter of Aden airport, wounding civilians.

With about 86 percent of votes counted, Israeli broadcasters projected Netanyahu's bloc at 53 of 120 seats and Gadi Eisenkot's bloc at 48, with Arab-majority parties at a record 19; Netanyahu stays caretaker prime minister during coalition talks.
Pentagon data put US spending on the Iran war at more than $47 billion, about 25 percent above July estimates, Reuters reported.
The US and Japan agreed to build a facility in Japan for joint production of advanced medium-range air-to-air missiles, Japan's defence minister said after meeting Hegseth in Cebu.
Ethiopia received 12 Russian Su-35 fighter jets, a year early, and will later get four S-400 air-defence systems, Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed said.

Russia's defence ministry said the submarine Generalissimus Suvorov fired a Bulava intercontinental missile from the Sea of Okhotsk to the Chizha range; USNI News says the launch date was not given and that such autumn tests are regular.

North Korea fired around a dozen short-range ballistic missiles from the Wonsan area into the sea on 29 October; they flew about 250 km. Seoul called it a breach of UN resolutions amid a row over a border landmine blast that wounded three South Korean soldiers.
Russia said 613 Ukrainian drones were launched towards Moscow overnight into 29 October; Moscow's mayor said 231 were downed on approach to the city.

Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said the timing of the next three-way talks with Ukraine and the US is linked to the Middle East conflict and does not allow a meeting in the near future; Zelensky had hoped for Abu Dhabi between 6 and 10 November.
UKMTO received a report of a ship on fire about nine nautical miles north of Oman's Khasab in the Strait of Hormuz; the cause and crew status were not given.

A small boat attached two limpet mines to the Panama-flagged tanker Louise 1 about 25 nautical miles northeast of Khasab, UKMTO and maritime security sources said; an engine-room fire disabled the ship; the crew is safe. gCaptain calls it the first reported limpet-mine hit on a merchant ship in this war.

Russian strikes killed at least 27 civilians and injured more than 140 across six Ukrainian regions on 29 October, Euromaidan Press tallied from regional reports; the Dnipro railway station toll reached 15, and Ukraine asked for an emergency UN Security Council meeting.

The Wall Street Journal reported that Ukraine agreed under US pressure to pause refinery strikes until after the midterms; Kyiv Independent sources say Ukraine never agreed, and one said Jared Kushner suggested a 30-day pause. Zelensky says no such order was given.

Drones struck the Jari 2 displacement camp near Hayk in Ethiopia's Amhara region, killing at least 15 people including five children; no party was named. Ethiopia accuses Eritrea of sending troops across the border, and Eritrea calls that a declaration of war.
Israel's final results gave Netanyahu's bloc 53 seats, Gadi Eisenkot's opposition camp 48 and Arab parties a record 19; President Herzog will consult party leaders before giving anyone the mandate.

AFP heard at least eight explosions in Riyadh and the city issued a phone alert for a hostile aerial threat, later lifted; the Houthis said Saudi strikes killed 12 in Taiz province. Saudi officials confirmed neither.

Pentagon officials are treating freezer failures at US military commissaries as a suspected hack, Reuters reports, citing four unnamed officials; at least six sites were affected and no attacker has been named.
Somali pirates seized the Iranian fishing vessel Azini off Puntland, the status of its 21 crew unknown; the New Arab counts at least 15 attacks since April.

Hackers stole about $6.3 billion in tokens from Binance, reported as the largest crypto theft on record; TRM Labs said with high confidence that North Korea-linked TraderTraitor did it, and about $3 billion of the assets were frozen.

The US State Department approved a possible $2.1 billion sale of 500 PAC-3 Patriot missiles to Ukraine, financed by Canada, Germany, Norway and EU-backed funds. Zelensky says deliveries may start only in years; Kyiv Post sources say after 2030.

NATO's top commander, US General Grynkewich, said weapons European allies paid for under the PURL scheme have been delivered, with a delivery in the last week and nothing delayed; he gave no types or numbers and did not address Zelensky's claim of a hold.

Evacuees left occupied Oleshky through Crimea, Anapa and four flights to Belarus, reaching Ukrainian-held territory on 31 October; no official total was given. Ukraine's ombudsman says neither side recorded a ceasefire violation.
The G20 foreign ministers' family photo in Atlanta was cancelled after about a third of the countries, including European states, the UK and Australia, refused to stand with Lavrov.

Pentagon officials have asked Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia to tone down their rhetoric on Russia, Reuters reports, citing four people familiar with the matter; Pentagon policy chief Elbridge Colby was among those involved. The Pentagon declined to comment.
The US is pressing Lithuania to allow Belarusian potash through Klaipeda despite EU sanctions, Politico reports via LRT; Lithuania's foreign minister says EU sanctions also forbid transit.

UKMTO reported a vessel hit by an unknown projectile about 40 nautical miles south of Lavan Island, causing a fire; the crew is safe. Iran's Revolutionary Guard Navy separately claimed four tankers on 'unauthorised routes' caught fire, which Reuters could not verify.
The Qatari LNG carrier Al Mayeda was struck in Gulf waters by what Qatar's state news agency called unidentified objects; there were no casualties and Qatar named no attacker.
Two missiles hit the presidential palace compound in Aden, a police official told AFP, without casualties; no one claimed it, and the official blamed the Houthis.
OCHA says more than 300,000 people displaced since March remain so in Lebanon, with Israeli demolitions, fires and strikes continuing in the south this week; about 970,000 have returned.

Lebanon's military court charged 13 people over a 780 kg explosives truck seized on the Beirut highway this month; Hezbollah said the explosives were its own and meant for Israeli forces in the south.
The UN rights office says Israeli deployment in Gaza is being expanded to 70 percent of the territory and that a 25 October drone strike on tents in Gaza City displaced about 800 people.

China expelled a record number of officials at the fifth plenum, among them 16 generals and former nuclear, aerospace and shipbuilding chiefs, SCMP reports; the purge reaches former theatre commanders.
Russian strikes left about 280,000 Ukrainian families without power, Zelensky said; drones hit Kyiv's water system, cutting supply across much of the city, according to Mayor Klitschko.
Polish Deputy Defence Minister Wziątek said a US decision on a first permanent base in Poland is expected in December and could slip into next year; no US official has confirmed it.
UNHCR says more than 280,000 people have been displaced in Yemen by fighting that ended a four-year truce, and that its appeal is 19 percent funded.
China denied a New York Times report that a Chinese executive at Singapore's Megaspeed passed information to Beijing while dealing with Nvidia's chief; Nvidia calls the dealings routine.

North Korea fired KN-25 rockets at a demonstration for Kim Jong Un at a drone exhibition, USNI News reports; Seoul counted 10 short-range missiles on 29 October, against the 'around a dozen' first reported.

A Polish judge suspended the Constitutional Tribunal's president and deputy for a month; Tusk calls it the rule of law, President Nawrocki calls it a forcible takeover, police cordoned the court, and the EU Commission says appointing judges is the Sejm's right.

The FBI said North Korea was responsible for stealing more than $6 billion from Binance, naming the TraderTraitor group and saying the assets are being laundered into Ethereum. Trump said 'we don't know if it's North Korea'; Binance says it replaced 90 percent and is resuming withdrawals.

Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei told commanders any threat must meet an 'immediate, impactful and geographically unrestricted response' and ordered the target list updated; Rubio said Trump has not decided on new strikes.

Trump said the US still has to 'take care of one or two' sites in Iran, naming Pickaxe Mountain, and spoke to Netanyahu, the WSJ reports; MSNOW says Gulf officials were warned of strikes as early as 4 November. Trump says he is in no hurry.

Iranian and Qatari envoys held more than 12 hours of talks in Tehran and met again in Doha, Reuters reports. Security chief Rezaei says Vance's letter changed the US tone, but Iran will not reopen Hormuz or negotiate until its seven conditions are met.

A US delegation is expected to join indirect Iran talks in Doha with no arrival date set, The New Arab reports, citing mediators and Axios; Foreign Minister Araghchi says no meetings with Americans are planned.

Oman's Maritime Security Centre said its navy rescued 25 crew from the Panama-flagged tanker Riti after it was targeted and caught fire; Iran's Guard says it halted three tankers on an 'unauthorised route'.

Rubio said in Atlanta he does not know whether a negotiated peace in Ukraine is achievable; Kyiv Post, citing a Radio Liberty correspondent and European officials, says he doubts Putin will settle before spring 2027.

The US Embassy warned of a credible threat of a 'mass casualty event' at the Tsaritsyno palace park in Moscow and told people to stay away; Russia's FSB said it received the warning, according to TASS.
Erdogan told Zelensky in Istanbul that attacks on civilian ships in the Black Sea are unacceptable whoever carries them out; Ankara's proposal to end such strikes has not been taken up.
Syria's foreign minister confirmed Damascus is discussing joining the Mecca defence pact of Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan, giving no timeline.

North Korean state media KCNA said the country tested a Standard Type 2 cluster-bomb warhead on Hwasong-11D missiles, claiming it can destroy 12 to 13 hectares and that units will field four warhead types this year; the claim is unverified.

China's coast guard announced a new patrol off Taiwan's east coast with two ships and sent another near Pratas; Taiwan's coast guard says China is harassing shipping by radio and claiming a fictional jurisdiction.

Quad foreign ministers voiced grave concern about overcapacity and finalised a leaders' summit in the Philippines next month, weeks before Trump meets Xi in Shenzhen, SCMP reports; Rubio says the group is not anti-China but that the behaviours come from one country.
At the Manama Dialogue, the Gulf Cooperation Council's chief attributed casualties and infrastructure damage in member states to Iranian attacks; the meeting ended without a joint statement.

The US Treasury says no Iranian oil has been loaded since 25 August and that unloadings at known locations fell to about 400,000 barrels a day by 19 October, from over a million when its pressure campaign began.
Russia extended its ban on most diesel exports through January, Bloomberg reports, while November quotas for the US deal rise; the government order had not yet been published.
The UN rights chief demanded an independent investigation into the death of UN staffer Mohammad el Shami, held by the Houthis since June 2024; 71 UN personnel were held as of mid-October.
Joint List leader Ahmad Tibi said the Arab party would back an anti-Netanyahu government from outside without joining it; several opposition parties rule out a coalition with Arab parties.
China's commerce ministry opposed a US FCC decision barring device testing in China by 2028, saying it harms the stability of economic ties.

Ukrainian drones struck the Lukoil refinery and an adjacent power plant in Kstovo overnight, starting major fires, after hits on a Bashneft plant in Ufa and a rocket-fuel plant in Kamensk-Shakhtinsky.

The US struck Iranian surface-to-air missile sites on Qeshm and Hengam islands near Bandar Abbas late on 2 November, a US official told AP and Euronews, describing them as defensive; Iranian state media reported explosions and no casualties.

A Russian strike on a school used as an aid point in Komyshuvakha, Zaporizhzhia region, killed at least 31 people, with about 50 missing, regional officials say; Russia's defence ministry says it hit Ukrainian troops.

Houthi forces advanced to within about 80 km of Aden, taking Al-Maqatirah district and fighting at the entrance to Tur al-Bahah, Reuters reports, citing four military sources; the Taiz-Aden road has been cut since early October.

Iran's foreign ministry spokesman Baghaei said Iran could reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days, down from seven, if the US meets its conditions, which Euronews lists as ending hostilities, releasing frozen assets, lifting oil sanctions and ending the naval blockade.

The Kremlin said it has 'no similar plans for now' after the Oleshky truce, which ended on 1 November without an extension; Russia's ombudsman reported no violations, while its foreign ministry alleged a Ukrainian drone strike.
Israeli forces withdrew from Hebron after a siege that began on 23 October; the municipality says almost 5,000 people were displaced and at least 15 buildings demolished.

The Indian-flagged dhow Al-Jusufi was hit by what India's shipping minister called an unidentified aerial object near Limah in Omani waters; one Indian crewman died and Oman's coast guard rescued 13. India says 15 Indian seafarers have been killed near Hormuz since March.

Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress in the US midterms, with at least 54 Senate seats per Al Jazeera; Trump said the Iran war and petrol prices played a part, but that the war decision was right.

Russia launched its largest attack on Ukraine's energy system this year, 289 drones, 17 ballistic and 59 cruise missiles per energy minister Shmyhal; a substation serving the Khmelnytskyi nuclear plant was hit, and Kyiv faced power cuts and water outages.

The White House said the US will mediate working-level talks between Ukraine and Russia in Abu Dhabi on 10 and 11 November, the first three-way talks since February; the Kremlin confirmed and is sending Vladimir Medinsky again.

On the night of 2 November a Qatari foreign ministry delegation held more than three hours of talks in Tehran and returned to Doha; Qatar says it is working on an interim agreement and that mediators are exchanging proposals, but no date for US-Iran talks was announced.

Israel told US and Gulf officials that Iran may use chemical weapons, the New York Times reports; some US officials believe the claim is meant to pull Trump back into war, Gulf states called it unserious, and Iran denies having such weapons.
Lavrov rejected Ukraine's proposals for an immediate ceasefire and for narrower truces on energy, food, air and sea, saying they would let Kyiv rearm, TASS reports.
Ukrainian drones struck the Yaroslavl oil refinery overnight, wounding two workers, regional officials said.

Poland's Tusk said border guards saw people with flashlights at the Kaliningrad border just after midnight and forces were sent, after intelligence warned of sabotage or provocations in early November; counter-terrorism police were deployed to two border regions.
Norway is adding NASAMS air-defence sensors and about 30 troops at Kirkenes, near the Russian border; defence minister Sandvik called it preventive and said no elevated air threat is seen.

Taiwan's defence ministry reported 49 Chinese military aircraft sorties in the 24 hours to 6 am on 3 November, the highest one-day count this year, as the Liaoning carrier group operated in the western Pacific, SCMP reports.

Kremlin spokesman Peskov said a Putin-Trump-Xi meeting in China should be finalised in the coming days for later this month; China's foreign ministry did not mention Trump, and the White House has not confirmed.
Russian defence minister Belousov, in Beijing, said Russia-China military ties have reached an unprecedented level, meeting Central Military Commission vice-chair Zhang Shengmin.
Syria said it arrested a Hezbollah-linked cell planning to attack the Homs oil refinery and seized explosives; Hezbollah denies operating in Syria.

Iran's Revolutionary Guard said four 'non-compliant' oil tankers hit naval mines on a prohibited route south of the Strait of Hormuz and were destroyed; it named no ships, and France 24 reported no independent confirmation.
Two explosive-laden drones struck Iranian Kurdish opposition sites near Sulaymaniyah and east of Erbil in Iraqi Kurdistan, Reuters reports; no casualties were reported and no one claimed the attack.
Russia launched 310 drones overnight into 4 November; Ukraine's air force says 272 were downed and 19 sites were hit, including energy targets in Zhytomyr, Rivne, Odesa and Dnipro regions.

North Korea fired several missiles from the Sondok area toward the Sea of Japan, South Korea's military said, after Kim Yo Jong denied the FBI's Binance accusation and ruled out talks with Washington.

Israel's election commission said it found no evidence of irregularities and rejected Netanyahu's fraud claims; neither bloc has a majority, and President Herzog will consult parties after certification.

One seafarer was killed when the Marshall Islands-flagged tanker Velos Sapphire was hit in the Gulf, probably by a missile, while sailing empty toward Bahrain, its Greek manager told Reuters; the attacker was not identified.

Turkey's parliament approved the Mecca defence agreement with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan by 279 votes to 119; the pact treats an attack on one as an attack on all, but sending Turkish troops needs a separate vote.

Trump met Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev privately at the White House and said a coming deal 'might involve all of Europe'; Kushner listed five aims for a European security framework but announced no agreement.

A Helsinki court jailed the Russian captain and an Azerbaijani crew member of the cargo ship Fitburg for aggravated sabotage after it dragged its anchor about 130 km and cut two Finland-Estonia cables last year.

Iran's Revolutionary Guard said two oil tankers and a tugboat caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz after using 'unauthorised routes', one after hitting a mine; it named no ships and there was no independent confirmation.
South Korea's defence ministry will ask parliament to extend its Cheonghae naval unit's operating area closer to the Strait of Hormuz, limited to open waters south of Oman.

The Financial Times reported Russian arms-industry documents showing an export order of 90 helicopter-mounted missile launchers for Iran in 2024-25; the documents do not show whether they were delivered.
Putin placed the Russian operations of Japan Tobacco International under state control; Japan demanded the return of four businesses.
Russian diesel tankers that were bound for the US under Trump's waiver changed course toward Brazil, Africa and the Mediterranean, The Moscow Times and Euromaidan Press report.
Moldova banned Transnistria's Kremlin-backed leader Vadim Krasnoselsky from leaving the country for five years after Putin gave him a state award in Moscow.
The US imposed further sanctions on networks supporting Cuba's foreign military operations and revenue, the State Department said; details of who was named were not read.

Trump confirmed new 'minor' US strikes on an Iranian air-defence site on Qeshm island, saying 'we knocked it out in about 15 minutes'; Iranian state media reported two missile impacts in the Suza area. CENTCOM gave no on-record comment.

Saudi air defences shot down two ballistic missiles aimed at Najran and a drone over Makkah region on 6 November and a cruise missile aimed at Riyadh early on 7 November, the coalition spokesman said; no casualties were reported.

EU foreign policy chief Kallas said in Warsaw the EU will not implement any US-Russia agreement it is not party to; Poland's and Ukraine's foreign ministers agreed, and Zelensky said 'we don't want Yalta 2.0'.

CENTCOM publicised a State Department offer of up to $20 million and possible relocation for information on Iran's nuclear facilities, equipment and scientists, citing the IAEA's lost 'continuity of knowledge'.

Israel's Channel 12 reported that Netanyahu and the Mossad chief planned an operation against Iran on the eve of the 27 October election that was halted after the US was tipped off; the prime minister's office denied it.
Defence minister Rustem Umerov will lead Ukraine's delegation at the US-mediated talks with Russia in Abu Dhabi on 10-11 November, a senior official confirmed.
The UK and France will lead the first major exercise for a multinational force meant to deploy to Ukraine after a ceasefire.
US European Command launched a vigilance campaign for troops, families and civilians in Europe as hybrid threats mount, after explosive-drone and sabotage incidents near bases this autumn.

Russia's Security Council called for rapid deployment of the Rassvet satellite network, a Starlink rival with just over 30 satellites, describing Starlink and OneWeb as tools for destabilising states.
Denmark and Lithuania joined a Finnish scheme to buy 'Blocker' naval mines, part of a five-nation Baltic mine cooperation with Finland, Germany and Norway.

The US Air Force proposed more than 6,000 aircraft operations a year at airfields on Saipan, Tinian and Rota, reviving Second World War bases to disperse forces in the Pacific; comments are due 29 November.

The US Treasury sanctioned eight Canadian money-exchange firms, including crypto business Cryptoyal, for moving Iranian funds; a separate FinCEN order cut crypto exchange MEXC Global off from the US financial system, citing about $16 billion in illicit flows.

Regional officials told Reuters a Qatari bridge plan would have the US lift its blockade and release some frozen funds while Iran admits IAEA inspectors, then reopen Hormuz on day two; Iran is reviewing it and the White House declined comment.

Russia fired 36 ballistic missiles at Kyiv and its region overnight, Zelensky said, closing the Northern Bridge and and, he said, hitting substations linking the Rivne and Khmelnytskyi nuclear plants to Kyiv; at least six were injured in Kyiv, and police reported one death in the region.
The death toll from Russia's 2 November strike on a school used as an aid point in Komyshuvakha, Zaporizhzhia region, rose to 55, Ukrainian officials said.
China's foreign ministry said it is 'in communication with relevant parties' about a meeting of Xi, Trump and Putin, possibly at APEC in Shenzhen this month; AP reports nothing is set.

US aircraft fired on the St Kitts-flagged cargo ship Huda about 18 nm east of Khor Fakkan after its crew ignored warnings to stop running the blockade, disabling it; the UAE rescued 22 crew and no one was killed.
Israel's President Herzog gave opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot the mandate to form a government after more lawmakers recommended him than Netanyahu, who remains caretaker prime minister.
Ukraine said its drones hit the Saratov oil refinery and Neptune missiles struck a plant in Oryol overnight.

A Revolutionary Guard spokesman said the range restriction on Iran's ballistic missiles 'has been lifted', citing the supreme leader; he did not say whether Iran has missiles beyond its declared 2,000 km.

An airstrike in Bani Hushaysh, Sanaa province, killed at least 40 people, mostly women and children, according to Houthi-run media, which blamed the Saudi-led coalition; the coalition did not comment.
Bulgaria's interior ministry confirmed six bodies aboard the tanker Wine Trader, set ablaze by drones off Romania on 15 October, after remains were found during repairs in Varna.

A Houthi missile attack on Riyadh damaged an Aramco office tower in the King Abdullah Financial District; Saudi authorities blamed falling shrapnel and reported no casualties after intercepting missiles at Riyadh and the Eastern Province.
CENTCOM set up Task Force Iron Gate, a small team tasked with stopping weapons, dual-use goods and sanctioned materials reaching Iran over land borders and across the Caspian.
Iran's Revolutionary Guard said two oil tankers hit mines and caught fire on an 'unauthorised' Hormuz route; Reuters could not confirm the claims and Iran suggested the blasts were not US attacks.
Trump said he expects to meet Putin and Xi at the APEC summit in Shenzhen on 18-19 November; China says only that it is in communication about a three-leader meeting.

Trump said after meeting Qatar's prime minister that the Iran war is 'militarily effectively over' and renewed US strikes are 'quite unlikely', while warning the US remains ready; Rubio reported no progress in talks.

The US moved refuelling tankers out of RAF Mildenhall over an Iran-linked threat and raised Mildenhall and Lakenheath to FPCON Charlie, the Wall Street Journal reported; it is the second UK base vacated after Fairford.

France blamed the Revolutionary Guard's Shahid Kaveh cyber unit for October attacks that raised fridge temperatures at hundreds of French supermarkets; prosecutors opened a probe and sought warrants for two officials.
An attack on the East-West oil pipeline in the Medina region caused a limited fire; Saudi Arabia said operations were unaffected and its defences intercepted missiles fired at Riyadh.

A drone killed a worker at the Russian-occupied Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant, the IAEA said, a day after the plant lost its only external power line for about 10 hours; a second drone killed a worker at the nearby thermal plant.
Russian forces struck the Trypillia thermal power plant near Kyiv; state operator Centrenergo warned of 'extremely serious' consequences as the grid campaign continues before winter.
Canada sanctioned 38 entities and 24 people linked to Russia's ballistic-missile industry, Russian cyber actors and financial enablers including crypto exchanges.

China extended its trade truce with the US by two months, keeping a 24% tariff suspended and extending export-control waivers on certain critical minerals and its port-fee suspension to 10 January 2027.
Lithuania's president confirmed talks on renaming Taiwan's representative office in Vilnius, a move Beijing has sought since 2021; Taiwan said it has no plans to change the name.
US-mediated talks between Russia and Ukraine began in Abu Dhabi, the first in nine months, with the delegations seated opposite each other and US envoys Witkoff and Kushner at the head of the table.

US officials said their plan for the Abu Dhabi talks includes a 'long-term security architecture' between Russia and Europe, a possible revived NATO-Russia Council, possible sanctions relief and NATO-like guarantees for Ukraine.

German, French, British, Italian and EU officials met Ukraine's and the US delegations in Abu Dhabi outside the three-way format; the Kremlin rejected any European role, and France said European security cannot be negotiated before a ceasefire.
